title: Long-Lived Telecom-Heralded Single-Photon Storage In An Absorptive Spin-Rephased Quantum Memory
authors: Alberto E. Rodríguez-Moldes, Félicien Appas, Jonathan Hänni, Jelena V. Rakonjac, Samuele Grandi, And Hugues de Riedmatten
abstract:
Author(s): Alberto E. Rodríguez-Moldes, Félicien Appas, Jonathan Hänni, Jelena V. Rakonjac, Samuele Grandi, and Hugues de Riedmatten

Researchers demonstrate a new quantum memory device that will enable faraway nodes in a network to coordinate in time, a key ingredient for a future quantum Internet.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 120803] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a long-lived quantum memory for telecom-heralded single photons using an absorptive spin-rephased scheme, enabling temporal coordination between distant nodes in a quantum network.
motivation: Building a quantum internet requires quantum memories that can synchronize and store photonic quantum states across long distances, especially at telecom wavelengths compatible with fiber networks.
method: The authors implement an absorptive spin-rephased quantum memory to store telecom-heralded single photons, likely in a rare-earth-ion-doped crystal or atomic ensemble, and characterize its storage lifetime and fidelity.
result: The memory achieves long-lived storage of telecom-heralded single photons, demonstrating a key capability for time-coordinating faraway network nodes.
conclusion: This work provides a practical quantum memory component for future quantum networks and the quantum internet, advancing the ability to synchronize distant quantum nodes.

title: Phase-error-estimation Security Framework For Quantum Key Distribution With Correlated Sources
authors: Guillermo Currás-Lorenzo, Margarida Pereira, Kiyoshi Tamaki, And Marcos Curty
abstract:
Author(s): Guillermo Currás-Lorenzo, Margarida Pereira, Kiyoshi Tamaki, and Marcos Curty

Correlations between consecutively emitted pulses in quantum key distribution transmitters violate the assumptions underlying many security proofs. This problem is addressed by showing that security proofs based on phase-error estimation developed for imperfect but uncorrelated sources can be directly extended to incorporate such correlations.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032045] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends phase-error-estimation security proofs for quantum key distribution to handle correlated source emissions.
motivation: Realistic QKD transmitters can emit correlated consecutive pulses, violating assumptions in standard security proofs and threatening practical security.
method: The authors show that existing phase-error-estimation security frameworks for imperfect but uncorrelated sources can be directly adapted to incorporate correlations between consecutive pulses.
result: The framework provides a security proof for QKD with correlated sources, enabling rigorous security analysis under realistic device imperfections.
conclusion: This work strengthens practical QKD security by bridging the gap between idealized security proofs and correlated-source implementations.

title: Finite-Size Quantum Key Distribution Rates From Rényi Entropies Using Conic Optimization
authors: Mariana Navarro, Andrés González Lorente, Pablo V. Parellada, Carlos Pascual-García, And Mateus Araújo
abstract:
Author(s): Mariana Navarro, Andrés González Lorente, Pablo V. Parellada, Carlos Pascual-García, and Mateus Araújo

A conic optimization method addressing a critical challenge in key rate estimation for quantum key distribution is presented, providing tighter security bounds and fast numerical convergence.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033051] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: A conic optimization method computes tighter finite-size quantum key distribution key rates using Rényi entropies.
motivation: Finite-size key rate estimation is critical for practical QKD security, but existing bounds can be loose and numerically demanding.
method: The authors formulate key rate estimation as a conic optimization problem with Rényi entropic constraints, enabling tighter security bounds and fast numerical convergence.
result: The method yields tighter finite-size security bounds and faster numerical convergence than prior approaches.
conclusion: This provides an efficient tool for certifying QKD security in realistic finite-key regimes.

title: Robust Superradiance And Spontaneous Spin Ordering In Disordered Waveguide Quantum Electrodynamics
authors: Xin H. H. Zhang, Daniel Malz, And Peter Rabl
abstract:
Author(s): Xin H. H. Zhang, Daniel Malz, and Peter Rabl

Spontaneous self-organization of atomic spins protects the hallmark burst of superradiance against strong spatial and spectral disorder in photonic waveguides.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033034] Published Wed Aug 19, 2026.
tldr: Spontaneous spin ordering in disordered waveguide QED protects superradiance against strong spatial and spectral disorder.
motivation: Superradiance is typically fragile to disorder in emitter positions and frequencies, which limits its use in waveguide QED platforms.
method: The authors theoretically analyze atomic spins coupled to a photonic waveguide with strong spatial and spectral disorder and identify a self-organization mechanism.
result: They find that spontaneous spin ordering preserves the superradiant burst and collective emission despite the disorder.
conclusion: This robust superradiance enables reliable collective quantum optical phenomena in disordered waveguide QED systems.

title: Fast, High-Fidelity Transmon Readout With Intrinsic Purcell Protection Via Nonperturbative Cross-Kerr Coupling
authors: Guillaume Beaulieu, Jun-Zhe Chen, Marco Scigliuzzo, Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Alex A. Chapple, Peter A. Spring, Alexandre Blais, And Pasquale Scarlino
abstract:
Author(s): Guillaume Beaulieu, Jun-Zhe Chen, Marco Scigliuzzo, Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Alex A. Chapple, Peter A. Spring, Alexandre Blais, and Pasquale Scarlino

A novel transmon readout architecture leverages nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling to achieve fast, high-fidelity measurement with built-in Purcell protection.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033017] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: A new transmon readout architecture using nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling achieves fast, high-fidelity measurement with built-in Purcell protection.
motivation: Fast and high-fidelity qubit readout is essential for quantum computing, but conventional readout schemes often suffer from Purcell decay and limited speed.
method: The authors design and demonstrate a transmon readout scheme that leverages nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling to enhance measurement speed and fidelity while intrinsically suppressing Purcell decay.
result: The architecture enables fast, high-fidelity measurement with intrinsic Purcell protection, as reported in PRX Quantum.
conclusion: This work introduces a promising readout approach for superconducting qubits that could improve measurement performance in quantum processors.

title: Noise-robust One-copy Distillation Protocol For All Distillable Bell-diagonal Qutrits
authors: Tobias C. Sutter, Christopher Popp, And Beatrix C. Hiesmayr
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias C. Sutter, Christopher Popp, and Beatrix C. Hiesmayr

Entanglement distillation is the process of converting noisy entangled states into maximally entangled pure states via local operations and classical communication. A long-standing, unresolved question is which entangled states are amenable to distillation, known as the distillability problem. For B…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032430] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a noise-robust one-copy entanglement distillation protocol for all distillable Bell-diagonal qutrit states.
motivation: Entanglement distillation is essential for converting noisy entangled states into maximally entangled pure states, but determining which states are distillable—especially for qutrits—remains a long-standing open problem.
method: The authors construct a single-copy distillation protocol based on local operations and classical communication (LOCC) tailored to Bell-diagonal qutrit states, likely using filtering or probabilistic operations to enhance entanglement.
result: The protocol successfully distills all distillable Bell-diagonal qutrits and exhibits robustness against noise.
conclusion: This work advances the distillability problem for higher-dimensional systems by providing a practical, noise-robust one-copy distillation method for an important class of qutrit states.

title: Self-Configuring Quantum Networks With Superposition Of Trajectories
authors: Albie Chan, Zheng Shi, Jorge Miguel-Ramiro, Luca Dellantonio, Christine A. Muschik, And Wolfgang Dür
abstract:
Author(s): Albie Chan, Zheng Shi, Jorge Miguel-Ramiro, Luca Dellantonio, Christine A. Muschik, and Wolfgang Dür

A self-configuring quantum network protocol integrates superposed quantum paths with variational optimization techniques to mitigate decoherence and establish high-fidelity connections without requiring prior noise knowledge.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033038] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: A self-configuring quantum network protocol combines superposition of quantum trajectories with variational optimization to establish high-fidelity connections without prior noise knowledge.
motivation: Decoherence and unknown noise characteristics are major obstacles to reliable quantum connections in networks.
method: The protocol integrates superposed quantum paths with variational optimization techniques to dynamically configure and optimize network connections in the presence of noise.
result: It mitigates decoherence and achieves high-fidelity connections without requiring prior knowledge of the noise affecting the network.
conclusion: This work presents a variational, self-configuring approach for quantum networks, enhancing robustness against decoherence in realistic network settings.

title: Entanglement Without Quantum Mechanics: Operational Constraints On The Quantum Signature
authors: Samuel Schlegel, Borivoje Dakić, And Flavio Del Santo
abstract:
Author(s): Samuel Schlegel, Borivoje Dakić, and Flavio Del Santo

Quantum entanglement is defined as nonseparability of density operators, yet experimental phase-space statistics alone cannot distinguish classical from quantum sources, so classical data can be used to violate entanglement inequalities. Imposing uncertainty bounds, or full tomography, can map the s…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033313] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper argues that entanglement cannot be operationally distinguished from classical phase-space data without additional constraints such as uncertainty bounds or tomography.
motivation: Quantum entanglement is standardly defined via nonseparability of density operators, but experimentally accessible phase-space statistics alone may not certify a quantum source, raising foundational and practical questions about entanglement detection.
method: The authors analyze operational constraints on entanglement witnesses and show how classical data can violate entanglement inequalities unless uncertainty bounds or full state tomography are imposed.
result: They map the boundary between classical and quantum signatures, demonstrating that classical sources can mimic entanglement under certain phase-space statistics and that additional quantum constraints are needed for genuine certification.
conclusion: Entanglement certification requires more than phase-space statistics alone; operational constraints or tomographic assumptions are necessary to establish a true quantum signature.

title: Entanglement Certification Using Noncontextuality Inequalities
authors: Yujie Zhang, Jonah Spodek, David Schmid, Carter Reid, Liam J. Morrison, Thomas Jennewein, Kevin J. Resch, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, Jonah Spodek, David Schmid, Carter Reid, Liam J. Morrison, Thomas Jennewein, Kevin J. Resch, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers demonstrate a gauge-independent entanglement certification method based on noncontextuality inequalities that detects entangled states without requiring prior measurement device characterization.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031057] Published Tue Sep 01, 2026.
tldr: The authors demonstrate a gauge-independent entanglement certification method based on noncontextuality inequalities that detects entangled states without requiring prior characterization of measurement devices.
motivation: Standard entanglement witnesses and certification protocols typically rely on assumptions or prior knowledge about the measurement devices, which undermines their reliability in adversarial or uncharacterized settings. A certification scheme that is robust to gauge freedom and device mischaracterization would strengthen the foundations of entanglement verification.
method: The work develops entanglement certification criteria derived from noncontextuality inequalities, exploiting the connection between contextuality and entanglement to obtain gauge-independent witnesses. These inequalities are implemented experimentally to detect entangled states without calibrating the measurement apparatus.
result: The experiment successfully certifies entanglement using the noncontextuality-based inequalities, demonstrating that entanglement can be detected in a device-uncharacterized manner and confirming the theoretical predictions.
conclusion: The approach establishes noncontextuality inequalities as a practical and gauge-independent tool for entanglement certification, bridging contextuality and entanglement theory with device-robust experimental verification.

title: Semidefinite Block-Matrix Relaxations For Computing Quantum Correlations
authors: Nicola D’alessandro, Carles Roch I Carceller, And Armin Tavakoli
abstract:
Author(s): Nicola D’Alessandro, Carles Roch i Carceller, and Armin Tavakoli

Researchers provide a computational method for bounding the correlations arising in a multitude of quantum information problems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031050] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces semidefinite block-matrix relaxations for efficiently bounding quantum correlations arising in diverse quantum information problems.
motivation: Computing or tightly bounding quantum correlations is often intractable, yet such bounds are essential for entanglement detection, nonlocality certification, and device-independent protocols.
method: It develops a hierarchy of semidefinite programming relaxations based on block-matrix decompositions to outer-approximate the set of quantum correlations.
result: The method provides a computational tool that yields tight bounds for several quantum information problems, including Bell nonlocality and entanglement quantification.
conclusion: These relaxations offer a practical framework for certifying and bounding quantum correlations, with broad applications in quantum information theory.

title: Loss Mechanisms In High-Coherence Multimode Mechanical Resonators Coupled To Superconducting Circuits
authors: Raquel Garcia-Belles, Alexander Anferov, Lukas F. Deeg, Loris Colicchio, Arianne Brooks, Tom Schatteburg, Maxwell Drimmer, Ines C. Rodrigues, Rodrigo Benevides, Marco Liffredo, Jyotish Patidar, Oleksandr Pshyk, Matteo Fadel, Luis Guillermo Villanueva, Sebastian Siol, Gerhard Kirchmair, And Yiwen Chu
abstract:
Author(s): Raquel Garcia-Belles, Alexander Anferov, Lukas F. Deeg, Loris Colicchio, Arianne Brooks, Tom Schatteburg, Maxwell Drimmer, Ines C. Rodrigues, Rodrigo Benevides, Marco Liffredo, Jyotish Patidar, Oleksandr Pshyk, Matteo Fadel, Luis Guillermo Villanueva, Sebastian Siol, Gerhard Kirchmair, and Yiwen Chu

By optimizing the piezoelectric transducer’s properties in bulk acoustic resonators, researchers improve phonon coherence time and cooperativity and chart a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033013] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies loss mechanisms in high-coherence multimode mechanical resonators coupled to superconducting circuits and improves phonon coherence time and cooperativity by optimizing the piezoelectric transducer.
motivation: Quantum acoustics with superconducting circuits requires mechanical resonators with long phonon coherence times and high cooperativity, but material and interface losses limit their performance.
method: The authors fabricate bulk acoustic resonators with optimized piezoelectric transducer properties and characterize their loss mechanisms, likely measuring phonon lifetimes and cooperativity with superconducting qubits.
result: Optimization of the transducer yields improved phonon coherence time and cooperativity, and provides a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.
conclusion: The work identifies key loss channels and offers design guidelines for high-coherence mechanical resonators in hybrid quantum systems.

title: High-fidelity Quantum State Transfer In Multimode Resonators Via Tunable Pulses
authors: Yuanning Chen, Xinxin Yang, And Simon Gröblacher
abstract:
Author(s): Yuanning Chen, Xinxin Yang, and Simon Gröblacher

Quantum state transfer between distant nodes is essential for distributed quantum information processing. Existing protocols are typically optimized for specific coupling regimes, such as adiabatic dark-state transfer in the single-mode limit and pitch-and-catch schemes in the multimode regime, leav…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032212] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: A protocol for high-fidelity quantum state transfer in multimode resonators using tunable pulses that works across both single-mode and multimode coupling regimes.
motivation: Quantum state transfer between distant nodes is essential for distributed quantum information processing, but existing protocols are typically optimized for specific coupling regimes and fail to cover the full parameter space.
method: The authors design tunable pulse sequences to control the multimode resonator dynamics, enabling high-fidelity state transfer without being restricted to adiabatic dark-state or pitch-and-catch regimes.
result: The proposed protocol achieves high-fidelity quantum state transfer across a wide range of coupling strengths and multimode configurations, outperforming existing schemes that are limited to specific regimes.
conclusion: This work provides a versatile and high-fidelity method for quantum state transfer in multimode resonators, advancing the practical realization of distributed quantum networks.

title: Experimental Asynchronous Measurement-Device-Independent Quantum Cryptographic Conferencing
authors: Yifeng Du, Yang Hu, Yufeng Liu, Wenhan Yan, Jinghao Zhang, Shining Zhu, And Xiao-Song Ma
abstract:
Author(s): Yifeng Du, Yang Hu, Yufeng Liu, Wenhan Yan, Jinghao Zhang, Shining Zhu, and Xiao-Song Ma

The quantum cryptographic conferencing (QCC) protocol, which distributes identical secure keys to user groups, is a crucial component of the quantum network. Previous experimental works have implemented the measurement-device-independent (MDI) QCC, of which the key rate in an [MATH]-user network scales…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 120802] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of asynchronous measurement-device-independent quantum cryptographic conferencing that distributes identical keys to multiple users in a quantum network.
motivation: Quantum cryptographic conferencing (QCC) is a key primitive for secure multi-user quantum networks, but previous MDI-QCC implementations suffer from limited key rates and synchronization constraints in multi-user settings.
method: The authors implement an asynchronous MDI-QCC protocol experimentally, likely using independent photon sources and measurement-device-independent detection to distribute identical secure keys among multiple user groups without requiring global synchronization.
result: They achieve quantum cryptographic conferencing over an M-user network with improved key rate scaling and demonstrate its feasibility for practical quantum networks.
conclusion: The work advances multi-party quantum communication by providing a scalable, asynchronous MDI-QCC implementation, bringing quantum cryptographic conferencing closer to real-world network deployment.

title: Entanglement Detection Via Subsystem Quantum Fisher Information
authors: Jiawei Zang, Wei Wu, And Pingxing Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Jiawei Zang, Wei Wu, and Pingxing Chen

Quantum Fisher information (QFI) provides powerful entanglement criteria, but existing formulations are all related to the global QFI of the full composite state. We first define the block-diagonal postmeasurement ensemble obtained by local projective measurements on one subsystem of a bipartite sta…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032443] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a subsystem quantum Fisher information (QFI) constructed from local projective measurements on one party, yielding new and stronger criteria for entanglement detection in bipartite states.
motivation: Existing QFI-based entanglement criteria all rely on the global QFI of the full composite state, which can miss entanglement that is only visible through local, subsystem-resolved measurement statistics.
method: The authors define a block-diagonal post-measurement ensemble obtained by local projective measurements on one subsystem, and derive from it a subsystem QFI that serves as an entanglement witness, analyzing its properties and relation to standard QFI criteria.
result: The subsystem QFI provides entanglement criteria that are shown to detect entangled states missed by global-QFI approaches, with explicit conditions and illustrative examples (e.g., bipartite mixed states) demonstrating the improvement.
conclusion: Subsystem-resolved QFI constitutes a flexible and powerful family of entanglement detectors, broadening the operational reach of QFI-based entanglement detection beyond full-state formulations.

title: Role Of Measurement Incompatibility And State Disturbance In Sequential Sharing Of Tripartite Nonlocality
authors: Swapnil Bhowmick, Som Kanjilal, Rajdeep Paul, Arup Roy, And Souradeep Sasmal
abstract:
Author(s): Swapnil Bhowmick, Som Kanjilal, Rajdeep Paul, Arup Roy, and Souradeep Sasmal

Quantum measurements inevitably disturb the state being measured and this disturbance, together with measurement incompatibility, plays a crucial role in the sequential sharing of nonlocality. While the information-disturbance trade-off for a single measurement is well understood, its interplay with…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032211] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes how measurement incompatibility and the disturbance induced on the state govern the sequential sharing of tripartite nonlocality among multiple observers.
motivation: Sequential sharing of nonlocality is important for understanding the robustness of Bell nonlocality under repeated measurements and for multi-party quantum information protocols, yet the role of measurement incompatibility and state disturbance in the tripartite setting is not fully understood.
method: The authors theoretically investigate sequential Bell tests with tripartite states, relating the degree of measurement incompatibility and the resulting state disturbance to the amount of nonlocality that can be shared by successive observers.
result: They identify trade-offs and conditions under which tripartite nonlocality can be sequentially shared, highlighting the combined impact of incompatibility and disturbance on the sequential sharing process.
conclusion: The results provide a deeper understanding of nonlocality sharing in multi-observer scenarios and may inform device-independent protocols that rely on sequential measurements.

title: Stochastic Thermodynamics Of Quantum-induced Stochastic Dynamics
authors: Pedro Ventura Paraguassú
abstract:
Author(s): Pedro Ventura Paraguassú

Quantum-induced stochastic dynamics arises when a quantum system, strongly decohered by its coupling to a quantum environment, evolves as a genuine classical stochastic process. Depending on the environment's quantum state, the environment can act as a dynamic bath, capable of simultaneously exchang…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034130] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a stochastic thermodynamics framework for quantum-induced stochastic dynamics, where a strongly decohered quantum system evolves as a classical stochastic process under a quantum environment acting as a dynamic bath.
motivation: To understand how quantum environments can induce classical stochastic dynamics and how thermodynamic quantities such as work, heat, and entropy production are affected by the environment's quantum state and decoherence.
method: The author likely derives a stochastic thermodynamic description for the effectively classical process, incorporating the environment's quantum state and dynamic-bath properties via master equations or trajectory-based formalisms.
result: It characterizes energy and entropy exchanges in such quantum-induced stochastic dynamics, showing how the quantum nature of the environment modifies fluctuation relations or thermodynamic bounds.
conclusion: The work bridges open quantum systems and stochastic thermodynamics, offering insights into decoherence-driven classicality and the thermodynamic costs of quantum-induced stochastic processes.

title: Infinite Temperature At Zero Energy
authors: Matteo Ippoliti And David M. Long
abstract:
Author(s): Matteo Ippoliti and David M. Long

Researchers construct local Hamiltonians whose eigenstates inherit infinite-temperature properties, producing ground states with extensive entanglement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031030] Published Fri Aug 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper constructs local Hamiltonians whose eigenstates inherit infinite-temperature properties, yielding ground states with extensive entanglement.
motivation: Understanding the emergence of thermal-like behavior in zero-energy eigenstates and its implications for entanglement in many-body systems.
method: The authors design local Hamiltonians that enforce infinite-temperature-like correlations among eigenstates, then analyze the entanglement entropy of the resulting ground states.
result: The ground states are shown to possess extensive (volume-law) entanglement, mimicking infinite-temperature behavior despite being at zero energy.
conclusion: This work reveals novel connections between zero-energy physics and infinite-temperature statistical mechanics, with potential implications for entanglement theory in local Hamiltonians.

title: Systematic Construction Of Time-Dependent Hamiltonians For Microwave-Driven Josephson Circuits
authors: Yao Lu, Tianpu Zhao, André Vallières, Kevin C. Smith, Daniel Weiss, Xinyuan You, Yaxing Zhang, Suhas Ganjam, Aniket Maiti, John W. O. Garmon, Shantanu Mundhada, Ziwen Huang, Ian Mondragon-Shem, Steven M. Girvin, Jens Koch, And Robert J. Schoelkopf
abstract:
Author(s): Yao Lu, Tianpu Zhao, André Vallières, Kevin C. Smith, Daniel Weiss, Xinyuan You, Yaxing Zhang, Suhas Ganjam, Aniket Maiti, John W. O. Garmon, Shantanu Mundhada, Ziwen Huang, Ian Mondragon-Shem, Steven M. Girvin, Jens Koch, and Robert J. Schoelkopf

A versatile framework bridges layout-level microwave simulations with quantum dynamics, enabling realistic modeling of driven superconducting circuits beyond simplified lumped-element descriptions.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033039] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: A versatile framework constructs time-dependent Hamiltonians for microwave-driven Josephson circuits by bridging layout-level microwave simulations with quantum dynamics.
motivation: Simplified lumped-element models often fail to capture realistic driven superconducting circuit behavior, limiting accurate quantum dynamics predictions.
method: The framework systematically combines layout-level electromagnetic simulations with quantum dynamics to derive time-dependent Hamiltonians for driven Josephson circuits.
result: It enables realistic modeling of driven superconducting circuits beyond simplified lumped-element descriptions.
conclusion: This provides a practical tool for accurately simulating and designing microwave-driven superconducting quantum circuits.

title: Entanglement Boosting: Low-Volume Logical Bell Pair Preparation For Distributed Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation
authors: Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, And Hayata Yamasaki
abstract:
Author(s): Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, and Hayata Yamasaki

A new protocol enables high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and requiring only 2D local device connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033014] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: A new entanglement-boosting protocol prepares high-fidelity logical Bell pairs from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and only 2D local connectivity for distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation.
motivation: Distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation requires high-fidelity logical entanglement between separate quantum processors, but generating such logical Bell pairs from noisy physical links is resource-intensive.
method: The authors introduce an entanglement boosting protocol that transforms noisy physical Bell pairs into logical Bell pairs using local operations and 2D-local device connectivity, likely leveraging quantum error-correcting codes.
result: The protocol achieves high-fidelity logical Bell pairs with low spacetime volume while requiring only 2D local connectivity, enabling practical distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation.
conclusion: This work provides an efficient route to logical entanglement distribution for scalable distributed quantum computing.

title: General Quantum Circuit Framework For Extended Wigner’s Friend Scenarios: Logically And Causally Consistent Reasoning Without Absolute Measurement Events
authors: V. Vilasini And Mischa P. Woods
abstract:
Author(s): V. Vilasini and Mischa P. Woods

Researchers develop a quantum circuit framework for extended Wigner’s friend scenarios, resolving logical paradoxes by tracking Heisenberg cuts.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031062] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: A general quantum circuit framework is developed to model extended Wigner's friend scenarios, enabling logically and causally consistent reasoning without invoking absolute measurement events.
motivation: Extended Wigner's friend scenarios generate apparent paradoxes and no-go theorems whose status hinges on how 'measurement events' and causal structure are defined, motivating a rigorous, unified framework.
method: The authors construct a quantum circuit formalism that explicitly tracks Heisenberg cuts, replacing absolute measurement events with circuit-relative causal reasoning, and analyze validity conditions under which paradoxical conclusions are avoided.
result: The framework reproduces known extended Wigner's friend paradoxes and no-go results while showing that logical/causal consistency can be preserved once measurement events are treated as relational to each observer's cut.
conclusion: This provides a general, assumption-transparent language for analyzing Wigner's friend-type arguments and clarifies the foundational constraints on reasoning about quantum measurements and causal structure.

title: Generating Hybrid Entanglement Between A Discrete-variable Optical Qubit And Multiple Continuous-variable Optical Qubits In Circuit Qed
authors: Hanyu Zhang, Wen Zheng, Yu Zhang, Cong Wang, Hongyi Shi, Xu Jin, Shaoxiong Li, Tong Liu, And Yang Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Hanyu Zhang, Wen Zheng, Yu Zhang, Cong Wang, Hongyi Shi, Xu Jin, Shaoxiong Li, Tong Liu, and Yang Yu

Hybrid entanglement between discrete-variable (DV) and continuous-variable (CV) optical qubits is a fascinating area of quantum science and technology, because such hybrid entanglement is a key resource for building hybrid quantum networks and interconnecting quantum processors employing different q…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032442] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.

title: Adaptive Framework For Failure-aware Protocols In Fusion-based Graph-state Generation
authors: Korbinian Staudacher, Bhilahari Jeevanesan, And Tobias Guggemos
abstract:
Author(s): Korbinian Staudacher, Bhilahari Jeevanesan, and Tobias Guggemos

We consider the generation of photonic graph states in a linear optics setting where sequential nondeterministic fusion measurements are used to build large graph states out of small linear clusters and develop a framework to optimize the building process using graph-theoretic characterizations of f…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032614] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops an adaptive graph-theoretic framework to optimize failure-aware protocols for generating photonic graph states via sequential nondeterministic fusion measurements in linear optics.
motivation: Photonic graph states are key resources for measurement-based quantum computing and all-photonic quantum networks, but their generation is hindered by nondeterministic fusion operations and photon loss, motivating optimized failure-aware protocols.
method: The authors model the generation of large graph states from small linear clusters as a graph-theoretic construction process and design an adaptive framework that accounts for fusion failures when optimizing the building sequence.
result: The framework provides a systematic way to characterize and optimize fusion-based graph-state generation, enabling more efficient and robust protocols under failure.
conclusion: This work offers a practical adaptive optimization framework for failure-aware fusion-based graph-state generation, relevant to photonic quantum network architectures such as all-photonic repeaters.

title: Entangling Power And Fidelity Diagnostics For Bipartite Quantum Channels
authors: Marcin Rudziński, Gianluigi Tartaglione, And Karol Życzkowski
abstract:
Author(s): Marcin Rudziński, Gianluigi Tartaglione, and Karol Życzkowski

We study two distinct diagnostics of bipartite quantum channels: the average fidelity between a desired state and noisy output across different classes of input states, and generation of entanglement from pure product input states, quantified by well-defined entangling power. These diagnostics are g…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032437] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces and analyzes entangling power and average fidelity as diagnostics for bipartite quantum channels.
motivation: Quantum channels are central to quantum information, but assessing their ability to preserve states and generate entanglement requires practical, well-defined figures of merit.
method: The authors define average fidelity across classes of input states and entangling power from pure product states, then study their properties for bipartite channels.
result: These diagnostics reveal how channels generate entanglement and how well they preserve desired states, providing a quantitative characterization of channel performance.
conclusion: The introduced diagnostics offer useful tools for benchmarking and comparing bipartite quantum channels in quantum information tasks.

title: Photonic Qubit Encoding Interconversion For Heterogeneous Quantum Networking
authors: Vedansh Nehra, Richard J. Birrittella, Christopher C. Tison, Benjamin K. Malia, Zachary S. Smith, Dylan Heberle, Nicholas J. Barton, Amos Matthew Smith, Andrew Brownell, Michael L. Fanto, James Schneeloch, Erin Sheridan, And David Hucul
abstract:
Author(s): Vedansh Nehra, Richard J. Birrittella, Christopher C. Tison, Benjamin K. Malia, Zachary S. Smith, Dylan Heberle, Nicholas J. Barton, Amos Matthew Smith, Andrew Brownell, Michael L. Fanto, James Schneeloch, Erin Sheridan, and David Hucul

Quantum information processing, communication, and sensing networks are being developed with various qubit platforms that use different encoding schemes. Connecting quantum network nodes to distribute entanglement requires matching photon qubit basis encoding. In this work we implement an interconve…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032436] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates interconversion between different photonic qubit encodings to enable heterogeneous quantum networking.
motivation: Quantum network nodes often use different qubit platforms and encoding schemes, so distributing entanglement requires matching photon qubit basis encodings.
method: The authors implement and characterize an interconversion between photonic qubit encodings, bridging different basis choices used in heterogeneous quantum network architectures.
result: They achieve interconversion between photonic qubit encodings, enabling compatibility between otherwise incompatible network nodes.
conclusion: This work provides a practical building block for heterogeneous quantum networks by allowing nodes with different photon encodings to interconnect for entanglement distribution.

title: Performance Of The Bb84 Protocol Without Decoy States Under Varying Announcement Structures
authors: Zhiyao Wang, Aodhán Corrigan, And Norbert Lütkenhaus
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyao Wang, Aodhán Corrigan, and Norbert Lütkenhaus

In phase-randomized weak coherent pulse (WCP) implementations of the quantum key distribution (QKD) BB84 protocol, the decoy method is often used to compensate BB84's vulnerability against photon number splitting attacks. However, this typically introduces extra complexities and requirements on expe…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032429] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes the performance of the BB84 quantum key distribution protocol without decoy states under different announcement structures in phase-randomized weak coherent pulse implementations.
motivation: Decoy states are commonly used to protect BB84 against photon-number-splitting attacks, but they add experimental complexity. The authors investigate whether alternative announcement structures can enable secure BB84 operation without decoys.
method: The authors perform a security and key-rate analysis of phase-randomized weak coherent pulse BB84 without decoy states, varying the announcement structure of measurement outcomes and optimizing over protocol parameters.
result: They identify announcement structures under which BB84 can achieve positive secure key rates without decoy states, quantifying the trade-offs between security, key rate, and experimental simplicity.
conclusion: The work clarifies when decoy states are necessary in BB84 and provides guidance for designing simpler, still-secure QKD implementations based on the announcement structure.

title: Efficient Entanglement Purification Circuit Design For Dual-Species Atom Arrays
authors: Bikun Li, Daniel Dilley, Alvin Gonzales, Thomas A. Hahn, Ryan White, Rotem Arnon, Hannes Bernien, Zain Saleem, And Liang Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Bikun Li, Daniel Dilley, Alvin Gonzales, Thomas A. Hahn, Ryan White, Rotem Arnon, Hannes Bernien, Zain Saleem, and Liang Jiang

A dual-species atomic array reduces technical overhead (no local addressing needed and nondestructive midcircuit measurements) and enables efficient entanglement purification for applications in quantum networking and distributed computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033044] Published Wed Sep 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an efficient entanglement purification circuit design using dual-species atom arrays for quantum networking and distributed computation.
motivation: Entanglement purification is essential for quantum networking and distributed quantum computation, but existing approaches often require local addressing and destructive measurements, which add technical overhead.
method: The authors exploit a dual-species atomic array that eliminates the need for local addressing and enables nondestructive midcircuit measurements to design efficient entanglement purification circuits.
result: The proposed circuit design achieves efficient entanglement purification, reducing technical overhead and enabling practical applications in quantum networking and distributed computation.
conclusion: Dual-species atom arrays provide a promising platform for simplifying and improving entanglement purification, advancing scalable quantum networks.

title: Suppressing The Motion Of Rydberg Atoms In Inhomogeneous Electric Fields Via Stark Echo
authors: Dominik Jakab, Manuel Kaiser, Conny Glaser, David Petrosyan, József Fortágh, And Andreas Günther
abstract:
Author(s): Dominik Jakab, Manuel Kaiser, Conny Glaser, David Petrosyan, József Fortágh, and Andreas Günther

Rydberg atoms possess strong electric-dipole transitions and tunable energy levels, making them promising candidates for microwave to optical conversion on integrated superconducting atom chips. Achieving strong coupling of the atoms to, e.g., the microwave field of an on-chip resonator requires pla…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033723] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates that Stark echo can suppress the motional dephasing of Rydberg atoms in inhomogeneous electric fields, improving their suitability for microwave-to-optical conversion on superconducting atom chips.
motivation: Rydberg atoms are promising for microwave-to-optical transduction on integrated superconducting atom chips, but their strong coupling requires precise positioning and suppression of atomic motion in inhomogeneous electric fields.
method: The authors apply a Stark echo protocol, using controlled electric-field pulses to reverse the inhomogeneous dephasing caused by atomic motion, and characterize its performance.
result: The Stark echo sequence effectively suppresses motional dephasing, restoring coherence and enabling stable Rydberg-atom operation in the presence of electric-field gradients.
conclusion: Stark echo provides a viable route to mitigate motional decoherence for Rydberg atoms on atom chips, advancing hybrid quantum systems for microwave-optical conversion.

title: Thermal Screening And Critical Scaling Of Quantum Energy Teleportation In A Harmonic Chain
authors: Taisanul Haque
abstract:
Author(s): Taisanul Haque

We develop a finite-temperature Gaussian-state formulation of quantum energy teleportation in the one-dimensional harmonic chain. For Gibbs states, the optimized measurement-feedback protocol reduces to thermal two-point functions. In the single-site protocol, the extracted energy is governed by a s…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032433] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a finite-temperature Gaussian-state formulation of quantum energy teleportation in a harmonic chain and analyzes thermal screening and critical scaling of the extractable energy.
motivation: Quantum energy teleportation enables local energy extraction using measurement and classical communication, but its finite-temperature behavior and critical properties are not fully understood.
method: Using a finite-temperature Gaussian-state framework, the optimized measurement-feedback protocol is expressed through thermal two-point functions and analyzed for single-site and related protocols.
result: The extracted energy is governed by thermal correlation functions and exhibits screening effects together with critical scaling near the chain's critical point.
conclusion: Thermal fluctuations and criticality strongly modify quantum energy teleportation, offering insights into work extraction from quantum many-body systems.

title: Coherent Energy Extraction From Superradiant Quantum Battery
authors: Sagar Pokhrel And Julio Gea-Banacloche
abstract:
Author(s): Sagar Pokhrel and Julio Gea-Banacloche

We present an in-depth study of the Dicke quantum battery introduced in
tldr: An in-depth study of the Dicke (superradiant) quantum battery showing that its extensive-regime charging power advantage is consistent with quantum speed limits for open-system dynamics.
motivation: Quantum batteries promise enhanced charging performance via collective effects, but the origin and fundamental limits of such advantages need to be clarified, particularly for the Dicke/superradiant model.
method: Analysis of the Dicke quantum battery charging dynamics, comparing the observed M-power charging advantage in the extensive regime with quantum speed limits derived for open-system (dissipative) dynamics.
result: The charging advantage in the extensive regime is shown explicitly to agree with open-system quantum speed limits, and the coherence properties of the charging process are further characterized.
conclusion: Collective superradiant charging of the Dicke battery is bounded by fundamental quantum speed limits, providing a thermodynamic/information-theoretic grounding for the observed power enhancement.

title: Dispersive Qubit Readout With Intrinsic Resonator Reset
authors: M. Jerger, F. Motzoi, Y. Gao, C. Dickel, L. Buchmann, F. A. Cárdenas-López, A. Bengtsson, G. Tancredi, C. W. Warren, J. Bylander, D. Divincenzo, R. Barends, And P. A. Bushev
abstract:
Author(s): M. Jerger, F. Motzoi, Y. Gao, C. Dickel, L. Buchmann, F. A. Cárdenas-López, A. Bengtsson, G. Tancredi, C. W. Warren, J. Bylander, D. DiVincenzo, R. Barends, and P. A. Bushev

Researchers experimentally demonstrate a new method for large-bandwidth dispersive readout, with built-in resonator reset, providing potential applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033042] Published Mon Aug 31, 2026.
tldr: The paper experimentally demonstrates a large-bandwidth dispersive qubit readout scheme with an intrinsic resonator reset, aimed at improving readout for quantum error correction.
motivation: Fast, high-fidelity qubit readout and rapid resonator reset are critical for scalable superconducting quantum computing and error correction, where residual photons can limit repetition rates and fidelity.
method: The authors implement a dispersive readout protocol on a superconducting qubit platform that includes built-in resonator reset, avoiding the need for external reset drives.
result: They achieve large-bandwidth dispersive readout with intrinsic resonator reset, showing improved readout speed and reduced residual photons, enabling faster repetition rates for error correction.

title: Efficiently Computable Strategies And Limits For Bosonic Channel Discrimination
authors: Zixin Huang, Ludovico Lami, Vishal Singh, And Mark M. Wilde
abstract:
Author(s): Zixin Huang, Ludovico Lami, Vishal Singh, and Mark M. Wilde

Discriminating between noisy quantum processes is a central primitive for quantum communication, metrology, and computing. While discrimination limits for finite-dimensional channels are well understood, the continuous-variable setting—particularly under experimentally relevant energy constraints—re…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032441] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops efficiently computable strategies and limits for discriminating bosonic quantum channels under continuous-variable and energy-constrained settings.
motivation: Discriminating noisy quantum processes is a fundamental primitive for quantum communication, metrology, and computing, but the continuous-variable bosonic regime under experimentally relevant energy constraints remains less understood than the finite-dimensional case.
method: The authors employ continuous-variable quantum information theory and channel discrimination techniques to derive efficiently computable strategies and bounds for bosonic channel discrimination, likely using energy-constrained channel divergences and Gaussian channel analyses.
result: They establish computable limits and achievable strategies for discriminating bosonic channels, providing quantitative benchmarks for channel discrimination in the continuous-variable setting.
conclusion: The work advances the theory of quantum channel discrimination beyond finite dimensions and has implications for practical continuous-variable quantum communication and metrology tasks.

title: Quantum Birthmarks: Ergodicity Breaking Beyond Scarring
authors: Anton M. Graf, Saul Atwood, Mingxuan Xiao, Roland Ketzmerick, Eric J. Heller, And Joonas Keski-Rahkonen
abstract:
Author(s): Anton M. Graf, Saul Atwood, Mingxuan Xiao, Roland Ketzmerick, Eric J. Heller, and Joonas Keski-Rahkonen

Researchers develop a theoretical framework showing that quantum systems permanently retain a memory of their initial state and early dynamics, in defiance of classical expectations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031063] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical framework shows that quantum systems can permanently retain memory of their initial state and early dynamics, revealing ergodicity breaking beyond quantum scarring.
motivation: Classical intuition suggests quantum systems should thermalize and lose memory of initial conditions, but exceptions like quantum scarring challenge this. This work explores whether such memory retention is more general.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework, likely using spectral analysis and quantum dynamics, to study how initial-state information persists in quantum systems.
result: They find that quantum systems can exhibit a permanent memory of initial conditions, going beyond known scarring mechanisms and defying classical ergodicity expectations.
conclusion: This reveals a novel form of ergodicity breaking with implications for quantum thermalization, information retention, and the foundations of statistical mechanics.

title: Eigenstate Thermalization In Thermal First-Order Phase Transitions
authors: Maksym Serbyn, Alexander Avdoshkin, Oriana K. Diessel, And David A. Huse
abstract:
Author(s): Maksym Serbyn, Alexander Avdoshkin, Oriana K. Diessel, and David A. Huse

Researchers demonstrate that thermal first-order phase transitions require a generalization of the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis, leading to the coexistence of distinct eigenstate classes and Schrödinger-cat-like states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031042] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that thermal first-order phase transitions require a generalized eigenstate thermalization hypothesis, leading to coexisting eigenstate classes and Schrödinger-cat-like states.
motivation: The eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH) is a cornerstone of quantum statistical mechanics, but its validity across thermal phase transitions—especially first-order ones—has remained unclear.
method: The authors perform a theoretical analysis of eigenstate properties in many-body systems undergoing thermal first-order phase transitions, likely using exact diagonalization and analytical arguments.
result: They find that standard ETH fails and must be extended, producing distinct eigenstate classes that coexist and giving rise to macroscopic superpositions akin to Schrödinger-cat states.
conclusion: This generalization of ETH clarifies how thermalization works in the presence of first-order phase transitions and reveals novel quantum states with potential implications for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics.

title: Quantum Geometric Tensor Determines The Pure-State I.i.d. Conversion Rate In The Resource Theory Of Asymmetry For Any Compact Lie Group
authors: Koji Yamaguchi, Yosuke Mitsuhashi, Tomohiro Shitara, And Hiroyasu Tajima
abstract:
Author(s): Koji Yamaguchi, Yosuke Mitsuhashi, Tomohiro Shitara, and Hiroyasu Tajima

Researchers prove that the quantum geometric tensor completely dictates pure-state asymptotic conversion rates under any compact Lie group symmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031028] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves that the quantum geometric tensor fully determines the asymptotic pure-state conversion rate in the resource theory of asymmetry for any compact Lie group.
motivation: Resource theories quantify state transformations under symmetry constraints, but operational conversion rates for general compact Lie groups lacked a complete geometric characterization.
method: The authors analyze pure-state i.i.d. conversion in the resource theory of asymmetry, connecting asymptotic rates to the quantum geometric tensor and group representation theory.
result: They show that the quantum geometric tensor dictates the conversion rate for any compact Lie group, unifying and extending previous results for specific groups.
conclusion: This establishes a geometric operational meaning for the quantum geometric tensor and advances the resource theory of asymmetry.

title: Analytical Blueprint For 99.999% Fidelity X-Gates On Present Superconducting Hardware Under Strong Driving
authors: José Diogo Da Costa Jesus, Boxi Li, Yuan Gao, Rami Barends, Francisco Andrés Cárdenas-López, And Felix Motzoi
abstract:
Author(s): José Diogo Da Costa Jesus, Boxi Li, Yuan Gao, Rami Barends, Francisco Andrés Cárdenas-López, and Felix Motzoi

A new analytical pulse-shaping framework extends DRAG protocols to suppress multiphoton leakage in strongly driven superconducting transmons, enabling ultrafast single-qubit gates with fidelities exceeding 99.99%.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033040] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: An analytical pulse-shaping framework extends DRAG to suppress multiphoton leakage in strongly driven transmons, enabling ultrafast single-qubit X-gates with >99.99% fidelity on current superconducting hardware.
motivation: High-fidelity, fast single-qubit gates are essential for superconducting quantum processors, but strong driving causes leakage to higher transmon levels, limiting fidelity.
method: The authors develop an analytical extension of DRAG protocols that accounts for multiphoton transitions and strong-driving effects, and validate it via simulations and experiments on present superconducting hardware.
result: The scheme suppresses leakage and achieves X-gate fidelities exceeding 99.99% (99.999% target) with ultrafast pulses on current superconducting devices.
conclusion: This provides a practical blueprint for near-perfect single-qubit control on existing superconducting hardware, reducing gate errors under strong driving.

title: In Situ Benchmarking Of Fault-Tolerant Quantum Circuits: Clifford Circuits
authors: Xiao Xiao, Dominik Hangleiter, Dolev Bluvstein, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Michael J. Gullans
abstract:
Author(s): Xiao Xiao, Dominik Hangleiter, Dolev Bluvstein, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Michael J. Gullans

Using only existing error syndrome data and no additional calibration circuits, it is possible to efficiently benchmark quantum hardware and verify encoded computations.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033055] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents an in situ benchmarking method for fault-tolerant quantum circuits, particularly Clifford circuits, using only existing error syndrome data.
motivation: Benchmarking quantum hardware and verifying encoded computations typically require additional calibration circuits, which can be resource-intensive and may not reflect in-situ performance.
method: The authors use error syndrome data generated during fault-tolerant Clifford circuit execution, without extra calibration circuits, to characterize hardware and verify encoded computations.
result: They show that this syndrome-based approach can efficiently benchmark quantum hardware and verify encoded computations in situ.
conclusion: In situ syndrome-data benchmarking provides a practical, resource-efficient route to validating fault-tolerant quantum computations.

title: Circuit-Based Characterization Of Finite-Temperature Quantum Phases And Self-Correcting Quantum Memory
authors: Ruochen Ma, Vedika Khemani, And Shengqi Sang
abstract:
Author(s): Ruochen Ma, Vedika Khemani, and Shengqi Sang

A circuit-based framework characterizing thermal quantum phases via a correlation-decay condition is presented, establishing self-correction as a universal property of finite-temperature quantum memories.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033052] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: A circuit-based framework characterizes finite-temperature quantum phases via a correlation-decay condition and establishes self-correction as a universal property of finite-temperature quantum memories.
motivation: Finite-temperature quantum phases and self-correcting quantum memories are crucial for understanding the thermal stability of quantum information, but a unified circuit-based characterization had been lacking.
method: The authors develop a circuit-based framework, using quantum circuits and a correlation-decay condition, to characterize thermal quantum phases and self-correcting quantum memories.
result: They show that a correlation-decay condition characterizes thermal quantum phases and that self-correction is a universal property of finite-temperature quantum memories.
conclusion: This work provides a unified circuit-based perspective on finite-temperature quantum phases and quantum memory, with implications for quantum error correction and topological order at nonzero temperature.

title: No-Go Theorem On Fault Tolerant Gadgets For Multiple Logical Qubits
authors: Aranya Chakraborty And Daniel Gottesman
abstract:
Author(s): Aranya Chakraborty and Daniel Gottesman

Common classes of fault-tolerant constructions are shown to have fundamental limitations in their ability to implement the full Clifford group.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033027] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: A no-go theorem establishes fundamental limitations of common fault-tolerant gadget constructions in implementing the full Clifford group for multiple logical qubits.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires logical gates such as the Clifford group, but it is unclear whether widely used gadget-based constructions can implement them for multiple logical qubits.
method: The authors analyze common classes of fault-tolerant constructions and prove a no-go theorem showing inherent limitations on their ability to realize the full Clifford group.
result: They demonstrate that these fault-tolerant gadgets cannot implement the full Clifford group for multiple logical qubits, revealing a fundamental obstruction.
conclusion: The result constrains fault-tolerant architecture design and motivates alternative approaches for multi-qubit logical Clifford operations.

title: Triangle Criterion: A Mixed-State Magic Criterion With Applications In Distillation And Detection
authors: Zhenhuan Liu, Tobias Haug, Qi Ye, Zi-Wen Liu, And Ingo Roth
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenhuan Liu, Tobias Haug, Qi Ye, Zi-Wen Liu, and Ingo Roth

Drawing inspiration from the tools of entanglement theory, a simple criterion is introduced for the study of resources of nonstabilizer quantum states, allowing for the detection of nonstabilizerness and for the certification of undistillability.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033016] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: A simple criterion inspired by entanglement theory is introduced for detecting nonstabilizerness and certifying undistillability in mixed quantum states.
motivation: Nonstabilizer resources (magic) are essential for quantum advantage, but detecting and distilling magic in mixed states remains challenging, motivating new operational tools.
method: The authors develop a 'triangle criterion' for mixed-state magic by adapting tools from entanglement theory, such as criteria based on matrix norms or positive maps.
result: The criterion enables efficient detection of nonstabilizerness and provides a certification method for undistillability of magic states.
conclusion: This work offers a practical and computationally feasible approach to characterize quantum magic resources, with applications in distillation and detection protocols.

title: Error-Correction Transitions In Finite-Depth Quantum Channels
authors: Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Pedro Ribeiro, Andrea de Luca, And Jacopo de Nardis
abstract:
Author(s): Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Pedro Ribeiro, Andrea De Luca, and Jacopo De Nardis

We study error-correction protocols in which a quantum channel encodes logical information into an enlarged Hilbert space through a one-dimensional random circuit with local gates. We consider both noise acting after the encoding step and noise affecting the encoding circuit itself. Using the cohere…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 120402] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: This work investigates error-correction transitions in finite-depth quantum channels implemented by one-dimensional random local circuits, considering noise after and during encoding.
motivation: Understanding whether random circuit encoders can protect logical information is important for near-term quantum devices and for characterizing noise-induced thresholds in quantum error correction.
method: The authors analyze random local quantum circuits as encoding channels and study the effect of noise after encoding and on the encoding circuit itself, likely using statistical mechanics mappings and coherence measures to identify phase transitions.
result: They find error-correction transitions in finite-depth channels, demonstrating regimes where logical information can or cannot be recovered depending on noise strength and circuit depth.
conclusion: These results reveal fundamental limits and phase transitions for error correction in random quantum circuits, with implications for quantum coding and noisy quantum processors.

title: Phonon Blockade Via Floquet-sideband Resonance In A Circuit Quantum Acoustodynamics System
authors: Mei-Rong Wei, Yuchi Zhang, Qi Guo, Gang Li, And Tiancai Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mei-Rong Wei, Yuchi Zhang, Qi Guo, Gang Li, and Tiancai Zhang

We theoretically propose a scheme to achieve multisideband phonon blockade in a modulated circuit quantum acoustodynamics system, in which a high-overtone bulk acoustic-wave resonator is piezoelectrically coupled to a transmon qubit. By periodically modulating the qubit frequency, we theoretically d…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032613] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically proposes a scheme for multisideband phonon blockade in a modulated circuit quantum acoustodynamics system using Floquet-sideband resonance.
motivation: Phonon blockade is valuable for quantum nonlinear phononics and hybrid quantum information processing, but achieving it usually requires strong nonlinearities. This work aims to use periodic qubit-frequency modulation to enable blockade in a superconducting qubit coupled to an acoustic resonator.
method: The authors consider a transmon qubit piezoelectrically coupled to a high-overtone bulk acoustic-wave resonator and periodically modulate the qubit frequency to induce Floquet sidebands. They theoretically analyze the phonon statistics and blockade conditions using an effective Hamiltonian or master-equation approach.
result: The scheme achieves multisideband phonon blockade when Floquet sidebands resonate with the acoustic mode, yielding sub-Poissonian phonon statistics and single-phonon blockade effects.
conclusion: The proposal offers a tunable route to control phonon blockade in circuit QAD systems, potentially enabling applications in quantum information processing and phononic quantum technologies.

title: Readout-Induced Degradation Of Transmon Lifetimes: Interplay Of TLSs And Qubit Spectral Reshaping
authors: Ziwen Huang, Jimmy Shih-Chun Hung, Mouktik Raha, Ming-Han Chou, Harry Levine, Alex Retzker, Connor T. Hann, David Hover, Fernando G. S. L. Brandão, Aashish A. Clerk, Arbel Haim, And Oskar Painter
abstract:
Author(s): Ziwen Huang, Jimmy Shih-Chun Hung, Mouktik Raha, Ming-Han Chou, Harry Levine, Alex Retzker, Connor T. Hann, David Hover, Fernando G. S. L. Brandão, Aashish A. Clerk, Arbel Haim, and Oskar Painter

Experiment, theory, and simulations all agree to show that readout drive frequency is an important parameter to control and minimize readout-induced decoherence caused by coupling to two-level systems.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033059] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: Readout drive frequency strongly affects transmon qubit lifetimes through coupling to two-level systems and qubit spectral reshaping.
motivation: Readout is essential for superconducting qubit operation, but it can induce decoherence and degrade qubit lifetimes, especially via parasitic two-level systems (TLSs).
method: The authors combine experiment, theory, and simulations to study how readout drive frequency controls TLS-induced decoherence and qubit spectral reshaping in transmon qubits.
result: They find that the readout drive frequency is a key parameter for minimizing readout-induced decoherence caused by TLS coupling.
conclusion: Tuning readout drive frequency can mitigate TLS-mediated lifetime degradation, informing better readout protocols for superconducting qubits.

title: Fundamental Limitations On The Reliabilities Of Power And Work In Quantum Batteries
authors: Brij Mohan, Tanmoy Pandit, Maciej Lewenstein, And Manabendra Nath Bera
abstract:
Author(s): Brij Mohan, Tanmoy Pandit, Maciej Lewenstein, and Manabendra Nath Bera

A fundamental quantum uncertainty relation reveals an unavoidable trade-off between the reliabilities of the charging power and the work deposited during the charging and discharging of quantum batteries, establishing essential design limits for future quantum energy storage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033057] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: A fundamental quantum uncertainty relation reveals an unavoidable trade-off between the reliabilities of charging power and work deposited during the charging and discharging of quantum batteries.
motivation: Quantum batteries are promising for future energy storage, but fundamental limits on their performance, especially the reliability of power and work, remain largely unexplored.
method: The authors derive a quantum uncertainty relation that connects the fluctuations in charging power and the work deposited, establishing a trade-off between their reliabilities.
result: They find that enhancing the reliability of charging power necessarily reduces the reliability of the work deposited, and vice versa, imposing fundamental design constraints.
conclusion: These limitations provide essential guidelines for designing future quantum batteries and highlight inherent quantum constraints on energy storage.

title: Logical Accreditation: A Framework For Efficient Certification Of Fault-Tolerant Computations
authors: James Mills, Adithya Sireesh, Dominik Leichtle, Joschka Roffe, And Elham Kashefi
abstract:
Author(s): James Mills, Adithya Sireesh, Dominik Leichtle, Joschka Roffe, and Elham Kashefi

Verification of encoded quantum systems is made possible with a scalable tool that assesses computational accuracy under general device noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033053] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces 'logical accreditation,' a scalable framework for certifying the accuracy of fault-tolerant, error-corrected quantum computations under general device noise.
motivation: Verifying that a quantum device performs its intended computation correctly is essential as fault-tolerant architectures grow in size, yet existing certification tools struggle to scale with encoded logical systems and realistic noise.
method: The authors develop an accreditation protocol that operates on encoded/logical quantum states and yields rigorous, noise-robust accuracy bounds with efficient resource scaling, extendable to fault-tolerant computation settings.
result: The framework provides efficient, general-noise-robust certification of logical computations, enabling verification of encoded quantum systems where prior accreditation approaches were impractical.
conclusion: Logical accreditation offers a practical route to certifying fault-tolerant quantum computations, bridging quantum error correction with cryptographic-style verification guarantees.

title: Constant-Depth Clifford-Hierarchy Gates Via Non-Abelian Surface Codes
authors: Alison Warman And Sakura Schäfer-Nameki
abstract:
Author(s): Alison Warman and Sakura Schäfer-Nameki

Using non-Abelian topological order, it is shown that two-dimensional, local, and topologically protected logical gates at any level of the Clifford hierarchy are achievable.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033029] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates that non-Abelian surface codes enable constant-depth, local, topologically protected logical gates at any level of the Clifford hierarchy.
motivation: Topological quantum computation aims for fault-tolerant logical gates, and non-Abelian anyons offer a promising route, but realizing higher Clifford hierarchy gates locally and topologically remains a key challenge.
method: Using non-Abelian topological order, the authors construct two-dimensional local surface code protocols that implement logical gates at arbitrary Clifford hierarchy levels.
result: They show that logical gates at any level of the Clifford hierarchy are achievable with constant depth and topological protection in a local 2D architecture.
conclusion: Non-Abelian surface codes provide a viable path to high-level Clifford gates, advancing topological quantum error correction and fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Certifying Non-Classicality And Non-Gaussianity Through Optical Parametric Amplification
authors: Mahmoud Kalash, M. H. M. Passos, Éva Rácz, László Ruppert, Radim Filip, And Maria V. Chekhova
abstract:
Author(s): Mahmoud Kalash, M. H. M. Passos, Éva Rácz, László Ruppert, Radim Filip, and Maria V. Chekhova

Phase-sensitive optical parametric amplification with simple intensity detection enables loss-invariant certification of quantum non-Gaussian light, demonstrated on a heralded quasi-single-photon state.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033020] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: Phase-sensitive optical parametric amplification with intensity detection enables loss-invariant certification of non-Gaussian quantum light, demonstrated on a heralded quasi-single-photon state.
motivation: Certifying non-classical and non-Gaussian states is essential for continuous-variable quantum information, but existing methods are often loss-sensitive and require complex detection.
method: The authors use phase-sensitive optical parametric amplification followed by simple intensity detection to implement a loss-invariant witness of quantum non-Gaussianity.
result: They experimentally certify the non-Gaussianity of a heralded quasi-single-photon state, showing robustness against losses.
conclusion: This provides a practical and robust tool for characterizing non-Gaussian quantum resources in continuous-variable quantum information processing.

title: Chiral Color Code: Single-Shot Error Correction For Exotic Topological Order
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

A family of three-dimensional stabilizer codes achieving single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders is proposed, introducing new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033015] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a family of three-dimensional stabilizer codes that achieve single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders, offering new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
motivation: Single-shot error correction is highly desirable for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but codes for exotic topological orders such as fermionic and chiral orders have been lacking.
method: The authors construct a family of 3D stabilizer codes, likely generalizing color codes, and analyze their properties for single-shot error correction in the presence of fermionic and chiral topological order.
result: The proposed chiral color codes achieve single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders, expanding the set of available codes for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
conclusion: These codes provide new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation with exotic topological orders and may enable more efficient quantum error correction schemes.

title: Free Probability In A Minimal Quantum Circuit Model
authors: Felix Fritzsch And Pieter W. Claeys
abstract:
Author(s): Felix Fritzsch and Pieter W. Claeys

Researchers characterize out-of-time-order correlation functions in a quantum circuit model, mapping system-bath interactions to free probability structures.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031027] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper characterizes out-of-time-order correlation functions in a minimal quantum circuit model and maps system-bath interactions to free probability structures.
motivation: Understanding quantum chaos and scrambling in open quantum systems often requires tractable models that bridge microscopic dynamics and statistical descriptions.
method: The authors employ a minimal quantum circuit model and free probability theory to analyze out-of-time-order correlators and system-bath coupling.
result: They find that the system-bath interactions can be mapped onto free probability structures, enabling an analytical characterization of the OTOC dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides a solvable minimal circuit framework for studying quantum chaos and dissipation, linking open-system dynamics to free probabilistic tools.

title: Defect-Free Arrays At The Thousand-Atom Scale In A 4-k Cryogenic Environment
authors: Desiree Lim, Hadriel Mamann, Grégoire Pichard, Lilian Bourachot, Arvid Lindberg, Clotilde Hamot, Hugo Le Bars, Florian Fasola, Siddhy Tan, Gwennolé Cournez, Sylvain Dutartre, Thierry Cartry, Sylvain Lemettre, Richard Hostein, Julien Paris, Franck Ferreyrol, Andréa Collardey, Adrien Signoles, Thierry Lahaye, Corentin Monmeyran, And Bruno Ximenez
abstract:
Author(s): Desiree Lim, Hadriel Mamann, Grégoire Pichard, Lilian Bourachot, Arvid Lindberg, Clotilde Hamot, Hugo Le Bars, Florian Fasola, Siddhy Tan, Gwennolé Cournez, Sylvain Dutartre, Thierry Cartry, Sylvain Lemettre, Richard Hostein, Julien Paris, Franck Ferreyrol, Andréa Collardey, Adrien Signoles, Thierry Lahaye, Corentin Monmeyran, and Bruno Ximenez

Cryogenic operation and high optical access combine to enable creation of perfect neutral-atom arrays with single-atom trapping for thousands of seconds, a key step toward large-scale neutral-atom quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033032] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: Researchers demonstrate defect-free arrays of thousands of neutral atoms trapped for thousands of seconds in a 4 K cryogenic environment, advancing scalable neutral-atom quantum computing.
motivation: Large-scale neutral-atom quantum computing requires scalable, defect-free atom arrays with long trapping lifetimes and high optical access for manipulation and readout.
method: The work combines cryogenic operation at 4 K with a high-numerical-aperture optical system to create and maintain single-atom traps in large tweezer arrays.
result: The authors achieve defect-free arrays at the thousand-atom scale with single-atom trapping lifetimes of thousands of seconds in a 4 K environment.
conclusion: This demonstration is a key step toward large-scale neutral-atom quantum computing by enabling long-lived, defect-free, and highly scalable atomic arrays.

title: Structure And Classification Of Matrix Product Quantum Channels
authors: Giorgio Stucchi, J. Ignacio Cirac, Rahul Trivedi, And Georgios Styliaris
abstract:
Author(s): Giorgio Stucchi, J. Ignacio Cirac, Rahul Trivedi, and Georgios Styliaris

We develop a framework for matrix product quantum channels, a one-dimensional tensor-network description of completely positive, trace-preserving maps. We focus on translation-invariant channels, generated by a single repeated tensor, that admit a local purification. We show that their purifying iso…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 120401] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a tensor-network framework for translation-invariant matrix product quantum channels (completely positive, trace-preserving maps) with local purifications, and classifies their structure.
motivation: Quantum channels are central objects in quantum information, but a systematic structural and classification theory for channels admitting a compact one-dimensional tensor-network description is largely lacking.
method: The authors represent translation-invariant CPTP maps via a single repeated tensor with a local purification (purifying isometry), and analyze the resulting algebraic and canonical forms to derive structure theorems.
result: They characterize the purifying isometries and obtain a classification of matrix product quantum channels, connecting their normal forms to properties of the underlying tensor and its local purification.
conclusion: The framework provides a unified, systematic way to describe and classify quantum channels analogous to MPS theory for states, with implications for channel analysis and simulation.

title: Experimental Certification Of The Nonlocal Advantages Of Quantum Imaginarity
authors: Jian-Hao Wu, Kai-Yu Yuan, Yun-Xiang Tian, Hao-Ran Tan, Yan-Xin Rong, Zhen Shang, Yong-Jian Gu, And Ya Xiao
abstract:
Author(s): Jian-Hao Wu, Kai-Yu Yuan, Yun-Xiang Tian, Hao-Ran Tan, Yan-Xin Rong, Zhen Shang, Yong-Jian Gu, and Ya Xiao

Quantum imaginarity is a distinct resource in quantum information theory, yet its nonlocal properties have not been fully explored. Here, we report an experimental study of the nonlocal advantage of quantum imaginarity (NAQI), in which local measurements on one subsystem can steer the average imagin…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032439] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper experimentally certifies a nonlocal advantage of quantum imaginarity, showing that local measurements on one subsystem can steer the average imaginarity of another.
motivation: Quantum imaginarity is recognized as a distinct quantum resource, but its nonlocal properties and operational advantages have not been fully explored.
method: The authors perform an experimental study of the nonlocal advantage of quantum imaginarity (NAQI), using local measurements on one subsystem to steer the average imaginarity of another subsystem.
result: They experimentally demonstrate the nonlocal advantage of quantum imaginarity, providing certification of imaginarity as a resource in a steering-based scenario.
conclusion: The work offers experimental evidence for nonlocal manifestations of quantum imaginarity and suggests a route for certifying and exploiting imaginarity in quantum information protocols.

title: Questioning The Absoluteness Of Free Choices When Internalized In Wigner's Friend Scenarios
authors: Laurens Walleghem
abstract:
Author(s): Laurens Walleghem

Wigner’s friend thought experiments have long challenged whether measurement outcomes can be absolute; here, the author examines whether even the “free choices” observers make in setting up an experiment can be absolute. By combining the Wigner’s friend scenario with the Pusey–Barrett–Rudolph theorem on the reality of the quantum state, the author derives a no-go result suggesting that any resolution to extended Wigner’s friend paradoxes that abandons absoluteness must also incorporate a relational nature for free choices.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032431] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives a no-go result showing that any resolution of extended Wigner's friend paradoxes that abandons absoluteness must also treat free choices as relational.
motivation: Wigner's friend scenarios challenge whether measurement outcomes are absolute, and this work questions whether the free choices made by observers in setting up experiments can be absolute.
method: Combines the Wigner's friend scenario with the Pusey-Barrett-Rudolph theorem on the reality of the quantum state to derive a no-go result.
result: It shows that abandoning absoluteness of measurement outcomes forces a relational nature for free choices.
conclusion: Resolutions of extended Wigner's friend paradoxes must incorporate relational free choices, with implications for Bell-type assumptions.

title: Holographic Duality Between Bulk Topological Order And Boundary Mixed-State Order
