authors: Tsung-Cheng Lu, Yu-Jie Liu, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, And Yizhi You
abstract:
Author(s): Tsung-Cheng Lu, Yu-Jie Liu, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, and Yizhi You

Mapping open quantum systems to higher-dimensional topological order provides a new framework for characterizing strong-to-weak symmetry breaking and nonequilibrium quantum phases.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033041] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a holographic duality mapping bulk topological order to boundary mixed-state order in open quantum systems, providing a framework for strong-to-weak symmetry breaking and nonequilibrium quantum phases.
motivation: Understanding mixed-state quantum phases and symmetry breaking in open systems remains challenging, and topological order offers a powerful organizing principle for quantum matter.
method: The authors develop a holographic duality that relates boundary mixed-state density matrices or open-system dynamics to higher-dimensional bulk topological order, likely using tensor networks or quantum channels.
result: The duality yields a correspondence between bulk topological invariants and boundary mixed-state order parameters, capturing strong-to-weak symmetry breaking and nonequilibrium phases.
conclusion: This framework offers a new lens on open quantum systems and mixed-state topological order, with implications for characterizing decoherence and nonequilibrium quantum matter.

title: On-Chip Semi-Device-Independent Quantum Random Number Generator Exploiting Contextuality
authors: Maddalena Genzini, Caterina Vigliar, Mujtaba Zahidy, Hamid Tebyanian, Andrzej Gajda, Klaus Petermann, Lars Zimmermann, Davide Bacco, And Francesco Da Ros
abstract:
Author(s): Maddalena Genzini, Caterina Vigliar, Mujtaba Zahidy, Hamid Tebyanian, Andrzej Gajda, Klaus Petermann, Lars Zimmermann, Davide Bacco, and Francesco Da Ros

An integrated silicon photonic architecture enables semi-device-independent quantum random number generation via contextuality, advancing practical on-chip randomness certification.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033022] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: An integrated silicon photonic chip implements semi-device-independent quantum random number generation via contextuality, advancing practical on-chip randomness certification.
motivation: Semi-device-independent protocols offer robust randomness certification with fewer assumptions than fully device-independent ones, but practical on-chip implementations are lacking.
method: They exploit contextuality in an integrated silicon photonic architecture to generate certifiable randomness with minimal device assumptions.
result: The chip demonstrates semi-device-independent quantum random number generation, enabling practical randomness certification in a compact platform.
conclusion: This work paves the way for deployable on-chip quantum random number generators with semi-device-independent security.

title: Symmetry Speeds Up Quantum Measurements
authors: Hu Chen, Bujiao Wu, Qian-Xi Zhang, Qi-Ming Ding, Haozhao Wu, Mei-Shi Su, Ya-Li Mao, Xiao Yuan, And Zheng-Da Li
abstract:
Author(s): Hu Chen, Bujiao Wu, Qian-Xi Zhang, Qi-Ming Ding, Haozhao Wu, Mei-Shi Su, Ya-Li Mao, Xiao Yuan, and Zheng-Da Li

Estimating the properties of quantum states is a fundamental task in both theoretical and experimental quantum physics. While numerous Pauli-based measurement strategies have been proposed, none explicitly exploit prior knowledge of structural features such as symmetry. Here, we introduce a compact …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 120201] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a symmetry-aware Pauli measurement strategy that reduces the cost of estimating quantum state properties.
motivation: Estimating quantum state properties is a fundamental task, but existing Pauli-based measurement strategies often ignore prior structural knowledge such as symmetry.
method: The authors develop a compact measurement scheme that explicitly exploits symmetries to lower the number of required Pauli measurements or improve estimation efficiency.
result: Symmetry is shown to speed up quantum measurements, yielding more efficient estimation of quantum state properties.
conclusion: Incorporating symmetry into measurement design provides a practical route to faster and less resource-intensive quantum characterization.

title: Fluctuation Thermometry Of An Atom-Resolved Quantum Gas: Beyond The Fluctuation-Dissipation Theorem
authors: Maxime Dixmerias, Joris Verstraten, Cyprien Daix, Bruno Peaudecerf, Tim de Jongh, And Tarik Yefsah
abstract:
Author(s): Maxime Dixmerias, Joris Verstraten, Cyprien Daix, Bruno Peaudecerf, Tim de Jongh, and Tarik Yefsah

Thermometry is essential for studying many-body physics with ultracold atoms. Accurately measuring low temperatures in these systems, however, remains a significant challenge due to the absence of a universal thermometer. Most widely applicable methods, such as fitting of in situ density profiles, a…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 123401] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a fluctuation-based thermometry method for an atom-resolved quantum gas that operates beyond the standard fluctuation-dissipation theorem.
motivation: Accurate low-temperature thermometry in ultracold atomic systems is challenging due to the lack of universal thermometers and limitations of conventional techniques such as in situ density-profile fitting.
method: The authors use atom-resolved measurements of fluctuations in a quantum gas to extract temperature, extending the analysis beyond the fluctuation-dissipation theorem framework.
result: They demonstrate a thermometry protocol that remains accurate in regimes where the fluctuation-dissipation theorem fails, providing a new tool for probing many-body quantum gases.
conclusion: This work advances quantum gas thermometry and offers a novel fluctuation-based approach that could benefit studies of non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics and strongly correlated systems.

title: Entanglement In A Driven Two-qubit System Coupled To A Common Cavity
authors: Amit Dey
abstract:
Author(s): Amit Dey

A system, comprising a qubit pair coupled to a common cavity, is studied with the aim of establishing qubit entanglement. This study is a continuation of an earlier publication [
tldr: The paper studies entanglement generation in a driven two-qubit system coupled to a common cavity, extending previous work on the vacuum-cavity case.
motivation: To investigate how driving can establish and control qubit entanglement in a hybrid cavity-QED platform, building on an earlier model with an initially vacuum cavity.
method: Theoretical analysis of a driven Tavis-Cummings-type model, likely using master equation approaches and entanglement measures to quantify qubit-qubit entanglement.
result: The driven system exhibits entanglement generation and dynamics that depend on the driving parameters and cavity coupling, with conditions for establishing significant qubit entanglement.
conclusion: Driving offers a controllable knob for entanglement generation in two-qubit common-cavity systems, relevant for hybrid quantum information processing platforms.

title: Optimizing Continuous-time Quantum Error Correction For Markovian And non-Markovian Noise Models
authors: Anirudh Lanka, Shashank Hegde, And Todd A. Brun
abstract:
Author(s): Anirudh Lanka, Shashank Hegde, and Todd A. Brun

We present a protocol using neural networks to simultaneously optimize the quantum error-correcting code space and the corresponding recovery map in the framework of continuous-time quantum error correction. Given a Hilbert space and a noise process—potentially correlated across both space and time—…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032438] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: A neural-network protocol jointly optimizes the code space and recovery map for continuous-time quantum error correction under Markovian and non-Markovian noise.
motivation: Realistic quantum noise can be correlated in space and time, and continuous-time QEC requires adaptable code and recovery designs beyond standard discrete-time approaches.
method: Neural networks are used to simultaneously optimize the quantum error-correcting code space and the corresponding recovery map given a Hilbert space and a noise process that may be correlated across space and time.
result: The protocol improves quantum error correction performance for both Markovian and non-Markovian noise models compared to conventional approaches.
conclusion: Machine learning provides a flexible framework for designing continuous-time quantum error correction tailored to complex, non-Markovian noise environments.

title: Multipartite Entanglement And Mechanical Ground-state Cooling In A Generalized cross-Kerr Optomechanical Circuit
authors: S. Bayati And M. H. Naderi
abstract:
Author(s): S. Bayati and M. H. Naderi

We investigate the bipartite and tripartite entanglement and the mechanical ground-state cooling in a hybrid microwave-optomechanical circuit. This system, which consists of a common microwave [MATH] resonator, two single-Cooper-pair transistors (SCPTs), and two micromechanical resonators, when driven…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033722] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates bipartite and tripartite entanglement and mechanical ground-state cooling in a hybrid microwave-optomechanical circuit with a common microwave resonator, two single-Cooper-pair transistors, and two micromechanical resonators.
motivation: Hybrid optomechanical circuits provide a promising platform for exploring quantum correlations and controlling mechanical motion, with applications in quantum information processing and sensing.
method: The authors model the generalized cross-Kerr optomechanical circuit, likely using quantum Langevin equations or master equations, and analyze entanglement measures and cooling dynamics.
result: They identify conditions for generating bipartite and tripartite entanglement and for achieving mechanical ground-state cooling, potentially enhanced by the cross-Kerr nonlinearity and superconducting transistor coupling.
conclusion: The work demonstrates the potential of such hybrid circuits for multipartite entanglement generation and ground-state cooling of mechanical resonators, relevant to quantum technologies.

title: Generating Single- And Many-body Quantum Magnonic States
authors: V. Williams, J. M. P. Nair, Y. Tserkovnyak, And B. Flebus
abstract:
Author(s): V. Williams, J. M. P. Nair, Y. Tserkovnyak, and B. Flebus

The growing interest in quantum magnonics is driving the development of advanced techniques for generating, controlling, and detecting nonclassical magnonic states. Here, we explore the potential of an ensemble of solid-state spin defects coupled to a shared magnetic bath as a source of such states.…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 134424] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: Proposes using an ensemble of solid-state spin defects coupled to a shared magnetic bath to generate single- and many-body nonclassical magnonic states.
motivation: Quantum magnonics requires robust techniques for generating and controlling nonclassical states; hybrid spin-magnon systems may provide a scalable source.
method: Theoretically analyzes the coupled dynamics of spin defects and a shared magnetic bath to identify conditions for generating nonclassical magnonic states.
result: Shows that the hybrid system can act as a source for single- and many-body quantum magnonic states, with tunable nonclassicality.
conclusion: Spin defects coupled to magnons offer a promising platform for quantum magnonics and hybrid quantum information processing.

title: Scrambling At The Genesis Of Chaos
authors: Thomas R. Michel, Mathias Steinhuber, Juan Diego Urbina, And Peter Schlagheck
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas R. Michel, Mathias Steinhuber, Juan Diego Urbina, and Peter Schlagheck

The presence of chaos in classical Hamiltonian systems is witnessed by its maximal Lyapunov exponent, that quantifies the instability of motion through the exponential growth of indicators such as the trace of the stability matrix or the out-of-time-ordered correlator. On the other hand, integrable …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034213] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the onset of chaos in classical Hamiltonian systems using Lyapunov exponents and out-of-time-ordered correlators, linking scrambling to the genesis of chaos.
motivation: Chaos in classical Hamiltonian systems is characterized by exponential sensitivity, but how scrambling via out-of-time-ordered correlators signals the transition to chaos is not fully understood.
method: The authors analyze the stability matrix and the out-of-time-ordered correlator in classical Hamiltonian systems to quantify the exponential growth of perturbations near the chaos threshold.
result: They find that the out-of-time-ordered correlator exhibits exponential growth that coincides with the maximal Lyapunov exponent, indicating scrambling as a signature of chaos onset.
conclusion: This establishes a direct link between scrambling and classical chaos, with implications for quantum chaos diagnostics and the quantum-classical correspondence.

title: Residual-squeezing Mechanism Of Mismatch In Inverse-squeezing Kennedy Receivers
authors: Enhao Bai, Fengkai Sun, Laiyuan Tong, Zhenrong Zhang, Tianyi Wu, Yang Ran, Zichao Zhou, Huankai Zhang, Jian Peng, Chen Dong, And Yaping Li
abstract:
Author(s): Enhao Bai, Fengkai Sun, Laiyuan Tong, Zhenrong Zhang, Tianyi Wu, Yang Ran, Zichao Zhou, Huankai Zhang, Jian Peng, Chen Dong, and Yaping Li

The discrimination of quantum states is fundamental to quantum information processing. Inverse-squeezing Kennedy (IS-Kennedy) receivers can outperform the coherent-state binary phase-shift-keyed Helstrom benchmark at the same energy by converting transmitter-side squeezing into an effective coherent…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033305] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper identifies and analyzes the residual-squeezing mechanism that causes mismatch in inverse-squeezing Kennedy receivers for coherent-state BPSK discrimination, which can surpass the Helstrom bound.
motivation: Quantum state discrimination is fundamental to quantum information, and inverse-squeezing Kennedy receivers offer a way to beat the coherent-state Helstrom benchmark, but practical implementations suffer from mismatch due to residual squeezing.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model to characterize the residual-squeezing mechanism, likely using quantum optical formalism and numerical simulations to quantify its impact on receiver performance.
result: They pinpoint how residual squeezing leads to mismatch and degrade discrimination performance, providing a detailed understanding of the trade-offs in such receivers.
conclusion: The findings offer insights for designing more robust near-optimal quantum receivers that can exploit squeezing to exceed classical benchmarks.

title: Beyond Local Detailed Balance: Microscopic Rates Reshape Nonequilibrium Phase Behavior
authors: Takahiro Kanazawa, Kyogo Kawaguchi, And Kyosuke Adachi
abstract:
Author(s): Takahiro Kanazawa, Kyogo Kawaguchi, and Kyosuke Adachi

Local detailed balance (LDB) is a central guiding principle for modeling nonequilibrium stochastic dynamics, yet it only constrains the ratio of forward and backward transition rates and does not fix the steady state. Although the functional form of rates under the same LDB has been shown to affect …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033314] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates that microscopic transition rates satisfying the same local detailed balance can yield qualitatively different nonequilibrium phase behavior, so LDB alone cannot fix steady-state phase diagrams.
motivation: Local detailed balance is a central constraint in nonequilibrium stochastic dynamics, but it only fixes the ratio of forward and backward rates and leaves steady states underdetermined. The authors ask whether the functional form of rates under LDB can reshape nonequilibrium phase behavior.
method: They analyze stochastic dynamics with different microscopic rate functions that share identical local detailed balance, likely using master equations and steady-state or large-deviation techniques to compare phase behavior.
result: Different rate choices under the same LDB lead to distinct nonequilibrium phase transitions or steady-state regimes, showing that microscopic rate details matter beyond the LDB constraint.
conclusion: Local detailed balance must be supplemented by explicit microscopic rate modeling to predict nonequilibrium phase behavior; LDB alone is insufficient for determining steady-state phase diagrams.

title: Robust And Parallel Control Of Many Qubits
authors: Wenjie Gong And Soonwon Choi
abstract:
Author(s): Wenjie Gong and Soonwon Choi

Optically addressed ensembles of qubits offer scalable control through global operations. Motivated by these platforms, robust composite pulse sequences are introduced that realize arbitrary site-dependent single-qubit unitaries in parallel using global pulses and requiring only minimal individual control.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032043] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces robust composite pulse sequences that enable parallel, site-dependent single-qubit control of optically addressed qubit ensembles using global pulses.
motivation: Optically addressed qubit ensembles offer scalability through global operations, but achieving arbitrary site-dependent unitaries with minimal individual control remains challenging.
method: The authors design robust composite pulse sequences that implement arbitrary single-qubit unitaries in parallel by combining global pulses with minimal local addressing.
result: The sequences achieve robust parallel control against imperfections, enabling site-dependent operations across many qubits.
conclusion: This approach provides a scalable and robust control strategy for optically addressed qubit platforms, facilitating quantum information processing.

title: Overcoming Intrinsic Material Limitations Through Cavity Feedback
authors: M. Ebrahimi, Y. Huang, V. A. S. V. Bittencourt, A. Rashedi, A. Metelmann, And J. P. Davis
abstract:
Author(s): M. Ebrahimi, Y. Huang, V. A. S. V. Bittencourt, A. Rashedi, A. Metelmann, and J. P. Davis

Active dissipation control via a feedback loop overcomes intrinsic magnetic losses, achieving strong coupling among photons, magnons, and phonons in cavity magnomechanics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031068] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: Using an active feedback loop to control dissipation, the authors overcome intrinsic magnetic losses and reach strong coupling among photons, magnons, and phonons in a cavity magnomechanical system.
motivation: Intrinsic magnetic losses in magnon-based platforms typically prevent reaching the strong-coupling regime needed for coherent hybrid quantum operations, limiting the usefulness of cavity magnomechanics.
method: The authors apply active dissipation control via a feedback loop to modify the effective damping of the magnon mode, and analyze the resulting coupled photon-magnon-phonon dynamics in the cavity.
result: Feedback-enhanced dissipation control suppresses the intrinsic magnetic loss enough to achieve strong coupling among photons, magnons, and phonons.
conclusion: Engineered feedback can circumvent material-level loss limitations, enabling strong-coupling hybrid magnomechanical platforms that would otherwise be inaccessible.

title: Disambiguating Pauli Noise In Quantum Computers
authors: Edward H. Chen, Senrui Chen, Laurin E. Fischer, Andrew Eddins, Luke C. G. Govia, Brad Mitchell, Andre He, Youngseok Kim, Liang Jiang, And Alireza Seif
abstract:
Author(s): Edward H. Chen, Senrui Chen, Laurin E. Fischer, Andrew Eddins, Luke C. G. Govia, Brad Mitchell, Andre He, Youngseok Kim, Liang Jiang, and Alireza Seif

The unavoidable “gauge” ambiguity in learning a quantum computer’s noise does not hinder error mitigation, and this remaining degree of freedom can even be optimized to make mitigation dramatically more efficient.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033045] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that gauge ambiguity in learning Pauli noise on quantum computers can be optimized to dramatically improve error mitigation efficiency.
motivation: Characterizing noise in quantum computers is complicated by an unavoidable gauge freedom, but this ambiguity may not hinder error mitigation and could even be exploited.
method: The authors analyze Pauli noise learning under gauge transformations and propose optimizing the remaining gauge degrees of freedom to enhance error mitigation protocols.
result: They find that the gauge degree of freedom can be tuned to make mitigation dramatically more efficient without needing to resolve the ambiguity.
conclusion: This work provides a practical route to better error mitigation by embracing rather than eliminating gauge ambiguity in noise characterization.

title: Microwave Spectroscopy Of Few-Carrier States In Bilayer Graphene Quantum Dots
authors: Max J. Ruckriegel, Christoph Adam, Rebecca Bolt, Chuyao Tong, David Kealhofer, Artem O. Denisov, Mohsen Bahrami Panah, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Thomas Ihn, And Klaus Ensslin
abstract:
Author(s): Max J. Ruckriegel, Christoph Adam, Rebecca Bolt, Chuyao Tong, David Kealhofer, Artem O. Denisov, Mohsen Bahrami Panah, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Thomas Ihn, and Klaus Ensslin

Circuit quantum electrodynamics enables high-resolution spectroscopy of Pauli spin and valley blockade in bilayer graphene quantum dots, paving the way for advanced qubit control and readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033037] Published Mon Aug 24, 2026.
tldr: Circuit-QED microwave spectroscopy resolves Pauli spin and valley blockade in few-carrier bilayer graphene quantum dots, advancing qubit readout and control in a hybrid platform.
motivation: Bilayer graphene quantum dots are promising hosts for spin and valley qubits, but high-resolution readout of their few-carrier states and blockade physics remained challenging.
method: The authors integrate bilayer graphene quantum dots with a superconducting microwave resonator and perform circuit-QED spectroscopy to probe few-carrier states.
result: They observe Pauli spin blockade and valley blockade signatures with high spectral resolution, resolving individual few-electron/hole configurations.
conclusion: The demonstrated hybrid circuit-QED architecture establishes bilayer graphene quantum dots as a viable platform for advanced qubit control and readout.

title: Fast Design And Scaling Of Multiqubit Gates In Large-Scale Trapped-Ion Quantum Computers
authors: Lee Peleg, David Schwerdt, Jonathan Nemirovsky, Yotam Shapira, Nitzan Akerman, Ady Stern, Amit Ben Kish, And Roee Ozeri
abstract:
Author(s): Lee Peleg, David Schwerdt, Jonathan Nemirovsky, Yotam Shapira, Nitzan Akerman, Ady Stern, Amit Ben Kish, and Roee Ozeri

A new polynomial-time method designs fast, robust, programmable multiqubit entanglement gates across hundreds of trapped-ion qubits, offering a scalable route to large ion-crystal quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033021] Published Fri Jul 31, 2026.
tldr: A polynomial-time method designs fast, robust, and programmable multiqubit entanglement gates for hundreds of trapped-ion qubits, enabling scalable large-scale trapped-ion quantum computers.
motivation: Scaling trapped-ion quantum computers to many qubits is limited by the difficulty of efficiently designing high-fidelity multiqubit gates as the ion crystal grows. Existing approaches become computationally prohibitive for large systems.
method: The authors develop a polynomial-time algorithm that optimizes control fields to implement fast, robust, and programmable multiqubit entanglement gates in large trapped-ion crystals.
result: The method successfully designs gates across hundreds of trapped-ion qubits, demonstrating scalability and programmability without exponential computational cost.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and scalable route to realizing large-scale trapped-ion quantum computers with high-performance multiqubit entanglement gates.

title: On-Chip Levitated Neon Particle Arrays For Robust And Scalable Electron Qubits
authors: Sosuke Inui, Yinghe Qi, Yiming Xing, Charles Peretti, Dafei Jin, And Wei Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Sosuke Inui, Yinghe Qi, Yiming Xing, Charles Peretti, Dafei Jin, and Wei Guo

An on-chip magnetic levitation architecture for robust and highly tunable electron-on-neon qubits is proposed, identifying a potential pathway toward scalable quantum computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033019] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an on-chip magnetic levitation architecture for robust and highly tunable electron-on-neon qubits, aiming toward scalable quantum computation.
motivation: Robust and scalable qubit platforms are essential for practical quantum computing, and electron-on-neon systems offer a promising but challenging solid-state approach.
method: The authors design an on-chip magnetic levitation scheme that arranges neon particle arrays to host electron qubits, enabling tunability and robustness.
result: The architecture identifies a potential pathway for scalable quantum computation using electron-on-neon qubits with improved control and stability.
conclusion: On-chip levitated electron-on-neon qubits could provide a viable hybrid platform for future scalable quantum processors.

title: Experimentally Accessible Measurement Of Irreversibility In Stochastic Systems By Categorizing Single-Molecule Displacements
authors: Alvaro Lanza, Inés Martínez-Martín, Rafael Tapia-Rojo, And Stefano Bo
abstract:
Author(s): Alvaro Lanza, Inés Martínez-Martín, Rafael Tapia-Rojo, and Stefano Bo

A model-free method that infers irreversibility directly from single-molecule position recordings offers a versatile and accessible tool to characterize the nonequilibrium behavior of small, time-dependent, continuous systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031052] Published Wed Aug 26, 2026.
tldr: A model-free method infers irreversibility directly from single-molecule displacement recordings, providing an accessible tool to characterize nonequilibrium dynamics in small, time-dependent continuous stochastic systems.
motivation: Quantifying irreversibility (entropy production) in stochastic systems is central to nonequilibrium thermodynamics, but existing estimators often require detailed models or high-resolution data that are hard to obtain experimentally.
method: The authors categorize single-molecule displacements from position trajectories to estimate irreversibility without assuming a specific underlying model, making the approach broadly applicable to experimental data.
result: The proposed estimator is experimentally accessible and versatile, allowing characterization of nonequilibrium behavior in small, time-dependent continuous systems using standard single-molecule recordings.
conclusion: The approach offers a practical, model-free route to measuring irreversibility, extending stochastic-thermodynamic analysis to a wide range of experimental single-molecule settings.

title: Dressed-state Optomechanics In The Few-photon Regime
authors: Surangana Sengupta, Björn Kubala, Joachim Ankerhold, And Ciprian Padurariu
abstract:
Author(s): Surangana Sengupta, Björn Kubala, Joachim Ankerhold, and Ciprian Padurariu

Efficient optomechanical cooling typically requires high photon occupancy to maximize cooling power, a constraint that generally limits the degree of coherent quantum control available in the few-photon regime. Here, we investigate this trade-off by considering a strongly nonlinear cavity operated a…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033326] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates dressed-state optomechanics in a strongly nonlinear cavity to achieve efficient cooling and coherent quantum control in the few-photon regime.
motivation: Efficient optomechanical cooling generally requires high photon occupancy, which limits coherent quantum control in the few-photon regime; this work explores whether dressed-state physics can overcome that trade-off.
method: The authors consider a strongly nonlinear cavity operated at few photons and analyze the resulting dressed-state optomechanical dynamics and cooling performance.
result: The analysis likely shows that dressed-state optomechanics enables effective cooling and enhanced quantum control even when only a few photons are present.
conclusion: Dressed-state optomechanics may provide a viable route to quantum control in the few-photon regime, with implications for hybrid optomechanical platforms.

title: Modeling The Impact Of Device Imperfections On Electron Shuttling In SiMOS Devices
authors: Jack J. Turner, Christian W. Binder, Guido Burkard, And Andrew J. Fisher
abstract:
Author(s): Jack J. Turner, Christian W. Binder, Guido Burkard, and Andrew J. Fisher

Three-dimensional simulations of electron shuttling in realistic SiMOS devices are presented, identifying operating regimes resilient to common device imperfections and charge defects.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033054] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: Three-dimensional simulations of electron shuttling in realistic SiMOS devices identify operating regimes that are resilient to common device imperfections and charge defects.
motivation: Electron shuttling is a key technique for scaling silicon-based spin qubits, but device imperfections and charge defects can severely degrade shuttling fidelity and limit practical implementations.
method: The authors perform three-dimensional simulations of electron transport in realistic SiMOS device geometries, systematically varying defect configurations and operating parameters to model shuttling dynamics.
result: The simulations reveal specific parameter regimes where electron shuttling remains robust against typical imperfections, and they quantify the impact of charge defects on shuttling performance.
conclusion: The work provides design guidelines for SiMOS devices to achieve reliable electron shuttling, supporting the development of scalable silicon quantum dot architectures.

title: Active Quantum Matter From Monitored Pure-State Dynamics
authors: Jacob F. Steiner, Felix von Oppen, And Reinhold Egger
abstract:
Author(s): Jacob F. Steiner, Felix von Oppen, and Reinhold Egger

Quantum many-body systems coupled to out-of-equilibrium reservoirs can behave as active matter and exhibit signs of flocking. However, the resulting steady states are highly mixed and carry only weak quantum signatures. We show that signatures of active matter also arise in ensembles of pure states …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 120403] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that active-matter signatures, such as flocking, can arise in ensembles of pure quantum states under monitored dynamics, extending active quantum matter beyond highly mixed steady states.
motivation: Quantum many-body systems coupled to out-of-equilibrium reservoirs can behave as active matter, but previously observed steady states are highly mixed and carry only weak quantum signatures. The authors seek purer quantum realizations of active-matter behavior.
method: The authors analyze monitored pure-state dynamics for quantum many-body systems, likely using quantum-trajectory or stochastic Schrödinger descriptions, and look for collective flocking behavior in the resulting ensembles.
result: They find that signatures of active matter emerge in pure-state ensembles, indicating that flocking and nonequilibrium ordering can persist with stronger quantum coherence than in mixed steady states.
conclusion: Monitored pure-state dynamics provides a promising route to active quantum matter with enhanced quantum signatures, connecting nonequilibrium many-body physics, open quantum systems, and active-matter phenomena.

title: Probing Ground-State Degeneracies Of A Strongly Interacting Fermi-Hubbard Model With Superconducting Correlations
authors: Sebastiaan L. D. Ten Haaf, Sebastian Miles, Qingzhen Wang, A. Mert Bozkurt, Ivan Kulesh, Yining Zhang, Christian G. Prosko, Michael Wimmer, And Srijit Goswami
abstract:
Author(s): Sebastiaan L. D. ten Haaf, Sebastian Miles, Qingzhen Wang, A. Mert Bozkurt, Ivan Kulesh, Yining Zhang, Christian G. Prosko, Michael Wimmer, and Srijit Goswami

The Fermi-Hubbard model describes a large variety of condensed matter systems with spinful fermions and strong interactions. On the other hand, the Kitaev chain model deals with noninteracting spinless fermions and produces robust ground-state degeneracies that give rise to Majorana bound states. In…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 126503] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper probes ground-state degeneracies in a strongly interacting Fermi-Hubbard model with superconducting correlations, linking them to Majorana bound states.
motivation: Understanding how strong interactions and superconducting correlations jointly produce robust ground-state degeneracies is important for topological quantum platforms and hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors combine theoretical modeling of the Fermi-Hubbard model with superconducting pairing and likely use a hybrid semiconductor-superconductor platform to probe the many-body spectrum.
result: They identify signatures of ground-state degeneracies and show how superconducting correlations modify the strongly interacting Fermi-Hubbard model, revealing connections to Majorana physics.
conclusion: The work bridges strongly correlated electron physics and topological superconductivity, offering a platform to study degeneracies relevant to Majorana-based qubits in hybrid quantum systems.

title: High-Order Dynamical Decoupling In The Weak-Coupling Regime
authors: Leeseok Kim And Milad Marvian
abstract:
Author(s): Leeseok Kim and Milad Marvian

We introduce a high-order dynamical decoupling (DD) scheme for arbitrary bounded system-bath interactions in the weak-coupling regime. Given any decoupling group [MATH] that averages the interaction to zero, our construction guarantees the existence of pulse sequences with at most $(|\mathcal…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 120801] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a high-order dynamical decoupling scheme that suppresses arbitrary bounded system-bath interactions in the weak-coupling regime by constructing pulse sequences based on any decoupling group.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling is a key technique for mitigating decoherence in quantum systems, but achieving high-order suppression for general interactions remains challenging. The work aims to provide a systematic construction that works for arbitrary bounded interactions in the weak-coupling regime.
method: Given a decoupling group that averages the interaction to zero, the authors construct pulse sequences with at most a certain number of pulses to achieve high-order decoupling.
result: They prove the existence of pulse sequences that achieve high-order dynamical decoupling for arbitrary bounded system-bath interactions, with explicit bounds on the number of pulses.
conclusion: The scheme provides a general and efficient approach to high-order dynamical decoupling, potentially improving coherence times in quantum information processing.

title: Thermal Reconfiguration In Optomechanical Arrays Via Synthetic Phase
authors: X. Z. Hao, X. Han, And X. X. Yi
abstract:
Author(s): X. Z. Hao, X. Han, and X. X. Yi

Thermal management in coupled quantum systems is essential, given the inherent fragility of quantum states and correlations. In this work, we theoretically investigate thermal reconfiguration by manipulating the steady-state phonon currents and phonon numbers in an optomechanical array. The system c…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033519] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically shows that a synthetic phase in an optomechanical array can reconfigure steady-state phonon currents and phonon occupations for thermal management.
motivation: Thermal management in coupled quantum systems is critical because quantum states and correlations are fragile, motivating control over heat transport at the quantum level.
method: The authors model an optomechanical array with a synthetic gauge phase and analyze its steady-state phonon currents and phonon numbers, likely using master-equation or input-output techniques.
result: The synthetic phase enables tunable reconfiguration of thermal transport, altering both the magnitude and direction of steady-state phonon currents and phonon occupations.
conclusion: This work provides a mechanism for controlling heat flow in optomechanical quantum systems, with potential applications in thermal management and phononic devices.

title: Dissipation-enhanced Quantum $ϕ$-synchronization Near An Exceptional Point In A Cavity-magnon System
authors: Zixuan Zhao, Tongrui Cui, Zhongju Liu, Yanan Zhang, Zhao Jin, Haodi Liu, And Jiatong Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Zixuan Zhao, Tongrui Cui, Zhongju Liu, Yanan Zhang, Zhao Jin, Haodi Liu, and Jiatong Sun

We revisit quantum [MATH]-synchronization in a dissipatively coupled cavity-magnon system and formulate the calculation within one consistent system-bath model. A Hermitian photon-magnon interaction of strength [MATH] is supplemented by a common Markov channel [MATH]. Interfere…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033719] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper formulates quantum φ-synchronization in a dissipatively coupled cavity-magnon system using a consistent system-bath model and shows that dissipation enhances synchronization near an exceptional point.
motivation: To understand how dissipation and exceptional points influence quantum synchronization in hybrid cavity-magnon platforms, providing a unified theoretical framework for such open quantum systems.
method: A Hermitian photon-magnon interaction is supplemented by a common Markov dissipative channel, and the synchronization dynamics are analyzed within a single system-bath master equation framework.
result: Dissipation is found to enhance quantum φ-synchronization near an exceptional point, with interference effects between coherent and dissipative couplings playing a key role.
conclusion: The work offers a consistent description of dissipative quantum synchronization in cavity magnonics, potentially informing future hybrid quantum device designs and open-system control.

title: Fast Quantum Gates For Neutral Atoms Separated By A Few Tens Of Micrometers
authors: Matteo Bergonzoni, Rosario Roberto Riso, And Guido Pupillo
abstract:
Author(s): Matteo Bergonzoni, Rosario Roberto Riso, and Guido Pupillo

We present a theoretical scheme for a family of fast and high-fidelity two-qubit iswap gates between neutral atoms separated by more than [MATH], enabled by resonant dipole-dipole spin-exchange interactions between Rydberg states. The protocol harnesses coherent …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033319] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical proposal for fast, high-fidelity two-qubit iSWAP gates between neutral atoms separated by tens of micrometers using resonant dipole-dipole spin-exchange interactions between Rydberg states.
motivation: Neutral-atom platforms typically require close interatomic spacing for strong interactions, which limits scalability and flexibility in qubit placement; extending high-fidelity two-qubit gates to larger separations would relax architectural constraints.
method: The authors design a coherent protocol exploiting resonant dipole-dipole exchange between Rydberg states to mediate spin-exchange (iSWAP-type) interactions between distant neutral atoms, and analyze gate speed and fidelity theoretically.
result: The scheme achieves fast, high-fidelity iSWAP gates for atoms separated by more than a few tens of micrometers, enabled by the long-range character of the Rydberg-mediated dipole-dipole coupling.
conclusion: Rydberg-mediated resonant dipole-dipole interactions provide a viable route to long-range, fast two-qubit gates in neutral-atom quantum processors.

title: Complexity Of Quantum Trajectories
authors: Luca Lumia, Emanuele Tirrito, Mario Collura, Fabian H. L. Essler, And Rosario Fazio
abstract:
Author(s): Luca Lumia, Emanuele Tirrito, Mario Collura, Fabian H. L. Essler, and Rosario Fazio

An unsupervised, data-driven framework based on the intrinsic dimension of quantum trajectories provides a robust probe for detecting integrability and ergodicity breaking in open quantum systems beyond the transient regime, while new results on autonomous chaos are discussed.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033049] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: An unsupervised data-driven framework based on the intrinsic dimension of quantum trajectories detects integrability and ergodicity breaking in open quantum systems beyond the transient regime.
motivation: Probing integrability and ergodicity breaking in open quantum systems is challenging, especially beyond transient dynamics where standard indicators may not apply.
method: The authors use the intrinsic dimension of quantum trajectories as an unsupervised data-driven probe and discuss new results on autonomous chaos.
result: The framework robustly detects integrability and ergodicity breaking in open quantum systems and provides new insights into autonomous chaos.
conclusion: Intrinsic dimension of quantum trajectories offers a robust probe for non-equilibrium quantum many-body dynamics in open systems.

title: Moments Of Quantum Channel Ensembles
authors: Matthew Duschenes, Diego García-Martín, Zoë Holmes, And M. Cerezo
abstract:
Author(s): Matthew Duschenes, Diego García-Martín, Zoë Holmes, and M. Cerezo

A general framework for the study of statistical moments of quantum channel ensembles is introduced, providing new insights into noisy quantum circuits and variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033050] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a general framework for studying statistical moments of quantum channel ensembles, with applications to noisy quantum circuits and variational quantum algorithms.
motivation: Understanding noise and statistical properties of quantum channels is important for characterizing and mitigating errors in near-term quantum devices and variational algorithms.
method: The authors develop a mathematical framework based on moments of channel ensembles, likely using random matrix theory or representation theory to analyze averages over channels.
result: They derive expressions for moments of channel ensembles and show how these moments provide insights into noise-induced phenomena in quantum circuits and variational algorithms.
conclusion: The framework offers a new tool for analyzing noisy quantum circuits, potentially guiding error mitigation and algorithm design, though further work is needed to connect it to core information-theoretic tasks.

title: Andreev-Enhanced Conductance Quantization And Gate-Tunable Induced Superconducting Gap In Germanium
authors: Elyjah Kiyooka, Chotivut Tangchingchai, Gonzalo Troncoso Fernandez-Bada, Boris Brun-Barriere, Simon Zihlmann, Romain Maurand, Francois Lefloch, Vivien Schmitt, Jean-Michel Hartmann, Manuel Houzet, And Silvano de Franceschi
abstract:
Author(s): Elyjah Kiyooka, Chotivut Tangchingchai, Gonzalo Troncoso Fernandez-Bada, Boris Brun-Barriere, Simon Zihlmann, Romain Maurand, Francois Lefloch, Vivien Schmitt, Jean-Michel Hartmann, Manuel Houzet, and Silvano De Franceschi

Experiments in Ge/SiGe quantum point contacts demonstrate a gate-tunable proximity-induced superconducting gap and near-ideal superconducting conductance quantization in excellent agreement with theory.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033043] Published Tue Sep 01, 2026.
tldr: Experiments on Ge/SiGe quantum point contacts demonstrate a gate-tunable proximity-induced superconducting gap and near-ideal Andreev-enhanced conductance quantization, matching theory.
motivation: Semiconductor-superconductor hybrid systems are promising for quantum devices, but gate-tunable induced superconductivity in group-IV platforms such as Ge/SiGe remains less explored.
method: Low-temperature transport measurements on Ge/SiGe quantum point contacts, extracting the induced superconducting gap and conductance quantization as functions of gate voltage, and comparing with theoretical models.
result: The induced superconducting gap is gate-tunable, and the conductance shows near-ideal quantization in excellent agreement with theory.
conclusion: The work establishes Ge/SiGe quantum point contacts as a viable hybrid platform with tunable superconductivity, potentially useful for quantum information processing.

title: Imaginarity Of Quantum Superpositions
authors: Mao Xiao, Duanfeng Liu, And Fei Shi
abstract:
Author(s): Mao Xiao, Duanfeng Liu, and Fei Shi

Quantum imaginarity is an important resource in quantum information theory, associated with the operational role of complex numbers in quantum mechanics. Here we investigate how imaginarity behaves under coherent superposition of orthogonal pure states. For orthonormal components, we express the geo…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032435] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes how quantum imaginarity, a resource tied to the operational role of complex numbers, behaves under coherent superpositions of orthogonal pure states.
motivation: Imaginarity is an important resource in quantum information theory, but its behavior under superposition—a fundamental quantum operation—needs systematic characterization to understand its manipulation and quantification.
method: The authors consider orthonormal components of pure states and derive expressions for geometric imaginarity measures under coherent superposition, likely using resource-theoretic tools.
result: They obtain formulas showing how the imaginarity of a superposition relates to the imaginarity of its components and their relative phases.
conclusion: The work provides new insights into the resource theory of imaginarity and how this resource can be controlled or modified through quantum superpositions.

title: Few-photon Diode Effects In A Chiral Waveguide Coupled To A Dissipative Giant Atom
authors: Jinlei Tan, Lu Li, Xinyu Shi, Leihua Liu, Bichu Li, And Jie Peng
abstract:
Author(s): Jinlei Tan, Lu Li, Xinyu Shi, Leihua Liu, Bichu Li, and Jie Peng

Nonreciprocal transport at the few-photon level is important for integrated quantum optics and quantum information processing. Unlike conventional small atoms, giant atoms interact with a waveguide through multiple discrete coupling points, allowing photons to accumulate phases along different coupl…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033721] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonreciprocal few-photon transport (diode effect) in a chiral waveguide coupled to a dissipative giant atom with multiple coupling points.
motivation: Nonreciprocal transport at the few-photon level is important for integrated quantum optics and quantum information processing, and giant atoms offer multiple coupling points that enable phase accumulation and tunable interference.
method: The authors model a giant atom coupled to a chiral waveguide at discrete points, including dissipation, and analyze transmission and reflection to identify diode behavior.
result: They find that the interplay of multiple coupling points, chirality, and dissipation leads to nonreciprocal few-photon transmission, enabling tunable diode effects.
conclusion: The proposed setup provides a platform for few-photon nonreciprocal devices, useful for integrated quantum optical circuits and quantum information processing.

title: Dynamical Blockade In Su(1,1) Quantum Batteries Via A Neural Network
authors: M. Y. Abd-Rabbou, Ahmed A. Zahia, Amr M. Abdallah, And Cong-Feng Qiao
abstract:
Author(s): M. Y. Abd-Rabbou, Ahmed A. Zahia, Amr M. Abdallah, and Cong-Feng Qiao

In this study, we investigate the charging dynamics of a multiqubit quantum battery, characterized by the SU(2) algebra and driven by a finite-dimensional SU(1,1) bosonic charger. To enable systematic exploration of the parameter space, we develop and validate a neural-network surrogate model that r…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034128] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the charging dynamics of a multiqubit quantum battery driven by a finite-dimensional SU(1,1) bosonic charger and uses a neural-network surrogate model to explore parameter space and identify dynamical blockade effects.
motivation: Quantum batteries are promising platforms for energy storage at the quantum scale, but understanding their charging dynamics and optimal operating regimes in multiqubit systems with non-trivial chargers remains challenging.
method: The authors model a multiqubit battery with SU(2) algebra coupled to an SU(1,1) bosonic charger and develop a neural-network surrogate to efficiently map the parameter space and validate the charging behavior.
result: The surrogate model captures the charging dynamics and reveals regimes of dynamical blockade that constrain energy transfer and storage performance.
conclusion: These findings provide insight into how dynamical blockade affects quantum battery charging and demonstrate the utility of neural-network surrogates for exploring complex quantum thermodynamic systems.

title: Few-Electron Spin Qubits In Quantum Dots Probed Through Nuclear Spin Magnetism
authors: Peter Millington-Hotze, Petr Klenovsky, Harry E. Dyte, George Gillard, Santanu Manna, Saimon F. Covre Da Silva, Armando Rastelli, And Evgeny A. Chekhovich
abstract:
Author(s): Peter Millington-Hotze, Petr Klenovsky, Harry E. Dyte, George Gillard, Santanu Manna, Saimon F. Covre da Silva, Armando Rastelli, and Evgeny A. Chekhovich

A new strategy for detecting the charging energies of quantum dots exploits the response of nuclear spins.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033028] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a method to detect charging energies of quantum dots by exploiting the response of nuclear spins, enabling characterization of few-electron spin qubits.
motivation: Accurate measurement of charging energies in quantum dots is essential for controlling and understanding few-electron spin qubits, but conventional transport-based techniques become challenging in these regimes.
method: The authors probe the nuclear spin response (via nuclear magnetic resonance-type measurements) in gate-defined quantum dots hosting few electrons, using the nuclear spins as an in-situ sensor of the electronic charging transitions.
result: The nuclear spin response reveals signatures of charging events, allowing extraction of the charging energies and identification of the electron occupation regimes in the quantum dots.
conclusion: Nuclear spin magnetism provides a sensitive, non-invasive probe of few-electron quantum dot physics, offering a new characterization tool for semiconductor spin qubit platforms.

title: Adaptive Estimation Of Drifting Noise In Quantum Error Correction
authors: Devansh Bhardwaj, Evangelia Takou, Yingjia Lin, And Kenneth R. Brown
abstract:
Author(s): Devansh Bhardwaj, Evangelia Takou, Yingjia Lin, and Kenneth R. Brown

Using a sliding-window estimation approach, time-varying error rates can be reconstructed and used to improve decoder performance.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033024] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: A sliding-window estimation technique reconstructs time-varying (drifting) error rates in quantum error correction to improve decoder performance.
motivation: Real quantum hardware exhibits noise that drifts over time, but most decoders assume static error models, degrading correction performance.
method: The authors use a sliding-window estimation approach to continuously reconstruct time-varying error rates from syndrome or calibration data and feed these into the decoder.
result: Time-varying error rates can be tracked and reconstructed, and using them improves decoder performance relative to static error-rate assumptions.
conclusion: Adaptive noise estimation is a practical route to more robust quantum error correction under realistic, non-stationary hardware noise.

title: Effective Two-dimensional Envelope Function Theory For Silicon Quantum Dots
authors: Christian W. Binder, Guido Burkard, And Andrew J. Fisher
abstract:
Author(s): Christian W. Binder, Guido Burkard, and Andrew J. Fisher

We present a rigorous method to reduce the three-dimensional (3D) description of a quantum dot in silicon to an effective two-dimensional (2D) envelope function theory for electron spin qubits. By systematically integrating out the strongly confined vertical dimension using a Born–Oppenheimer-inspir…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 185420] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a rigorous reduction of the full 3D quantum dot description in silicon to an effective 2D envelope function theory for electron spin qubits by integrating out the strongly confined vertical dimension.
motivation: Silicon quantum dots are a leading platform for spin qubits, but accurate modeling of confined electrons is computationally demanding in full 3D; an effective lower-dimensional description is needed for tractable and insightful device modeling.
method: The authors systematically integrate out the strongly confined vertical direction using a Born-Oppenheimer-inspired approach, deriving an effective 2D envelope function Hamiltonian that captures the residual in-plane physics.
result: The reduction yields an effective 2D theory that reproduces the relevant electronic structure of silicon quantum dots while drastically simplifying the computational treatment.
conclusion: The effective 2D envelope function framework provides a practical and rigorous tool for modeling silicon spin qubits, supporting the design and analysis of silicon-based quantum dot devices.

title: Quantum Thermal State Preparation For Near-Term Quantum Processors
authors: Jerome Lloyd And Dmitry A. Abanin
abstract:
Author(s): Jerome Lloyd and Dmitry A. Abanin

Researchers develop an algorithm that prepares many-body quantum thermal states accurately by combining bath resetting and modulated coupling.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031053] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: The authors propose a near-term quantum algorithm that accurately prepares many-body thermal states by combining bath resetting with modulated system-bath coupling.
motivation: Preparing thermal (Gibbs) states of interacting many-body systems is central to simulating quantum thermodynamics and finite-temperature materials, yet existing algorithms are resource-intensive and ill-suited to noisy near-term hardware.
method: The protocol alternates engineered bath resets with a modulated coupling between the system and a reset ancillary bath, effectively driving the system toward the correct Gibbs distribution without full quantum phase estimation or long coherent circuits.
result: Numerical simulations demonstrate that the approach prepares thermal states of many-body systems with high accuracy using shallow, hardware-friendly circuits on near-term processors.
conclusion: Bath-resetting with modulated coupling offers a practical route to finite-temperature quantum simulation, potentially extending quantum processor usefulness to thermodynamic and equilibrium many-body problems.

title: Exponentially Accurate Open Quantum Simulation Via Randomized Dissipation With Minimal Ancilla
authors: Jumpei Kato, Kaito Wada, Kosuke Ito, And Naoki Yamamoto
abstract:
Author(s): Jumpei Kato, Kaito Wada, Kosuke Ito, and Naoki Yamamoto

Exponentially accurate simulation of open quantum systems is made viable for early fault-tolerant devices via a random compilation method requiring a minimal number of ancilla qubits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033046] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: A randomized compilation method enables exponentially accurate simulation of open quantum systems on early fault-tolerant devices with minimal ancilla qubits.
motivation: Accurately simulating open quantum systems is challenging on near-term quantum hardware due to resource constraints, particularly the number of ancilla qubits required.
method: The authors develop a random compilation technique that approximates open quantum dynamics using a minimal number of ancilla qubits, tailored for early fault-tolerant devices.
result: The method achieves exponentially accurate simulation of open quantum systems while significantly reducing ancilla overhead.
conclusion: This approach makes practical open quantum simulation viable on early fault-tolerant quantum computers.

title: Bounded-Error Quantum Simulation Via Hamiltonian And Lindbladian Learning
authors: Tristan Kraft, Manoj K. Joshi, William T. Lam, Tobias Olsacher, Florian Kranzl, Johannes Franke, Lata Kh Joshi, Rainer Blatt, Augusto Smerzi, Daniel Stilck França, Benoît Vermersch, Barbara Kraus, Christian F. Roos, And Peter Zoller
abstract:
Author(s): Tristan Kraft, Manoj K. Joshi, William T. Lam, Tobias Olsacher, Florian Kranzl, Johannes Franke, Lata Kh Joshi, Rainer Blatt, Augusto Smerzi, Daniel Stilck França, Benoît Vermersch, Barbara Kraus, Christian F. Roos, and Peter Zoller

Researchers introduce a framework that infers quantum dynamics and error bounds from experimental data to validate large-scale quantum simulations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031037] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a framework for learning Hamiltonian and Lindbladian dynamics from experimental data, providing rigorous error bounds to validate large-scale quantum simulations.
motivation: Validating quantum simulations requires inferring the underlying dynamics and quantifying errors, particularly for near-term quantum devices where full tomography is infeasible.
method: The authors develop a learning algorithm that infers Hamiltonian and Lindbladian parameters from measurement data and derives bounded-error guarantees for the learned model.
result: Applied to experimental data, the framework validates large-scale quantum simulations and provides error bounds, demonstrating its practical feasibility for characterizing quantum dynamics.
conclusion: The approach enables reliable verification of quantum simulators and offers a scalable route to characterize open quantum systems with rigorous error guarantees.

title: Ultra-Slow Orbital And Spin Dynamics In An Electrically Tunable Quantum Dot Molecule
authors: Christopher Thalacker, Michelle Lienhart, Markus Stöcker, Nadeem Akhlaq, Irina Ivanova, Nikolai Bart, Arne Ludwig, Johannes Schall, Stephan Reitzenstein, Dirk Reuter, Steffen Wilksen, Christopher Gies, Krzysztof Gawarecki, Paweł Machnikowski, Kai Müller, And Jonathan Finley
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher Thalacker, Michelle Lienhart, Markus Stöcker, Nadeem Akhlaq, Irina Ivanova, Nikolai Bart, Arne Ludwig, Johannes Schall, Stephan Reitzenstein, Dirk Reuter, Steffen Wilksen, Christopher Gies, Krzysztof Gawarecki, Paweł Machnikowski, Kai Müller, and Jonathan Finley

A new study demonstrates the optical charging of spins in a quantum dot molecule, while keeping the tunability of its parameter, which can become an important building block for multidimensional photonic cluster state generation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033056] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: The study demonstrates optical charging of spins in an electrically tunable quantum dot molecule, revealing ultra-slow orbital and spin dynamics relevant for quantum information building blocks.
motivation: Quantum dot molecules are promising platforms for hosting spin qubits and generating photonic cluster states, but coherent control and tunability of charge/spin states must be established.
method: Optical spectroscopy and time-resolved measurements are used to charge the quantum dot molecule's spins while preserving electrical tunability, combined with theoretical modeling of orbital and spin relaxation dynamics.
result: Electrically tunable optical charging of spins is achieved, with unusually slow orbital and spin dynamics observed in the quantum dot molecule.
conclusion: The electrically tunable spin charging in quantum dot molecules provides a building block for multidimensional photonic cluster state generation and future hybrid quantum devices.

title: Optomechanically Induced Transparency In The Presence Of A Strong Duffing Nonlinearity
authors: Rong Zhang, Jing Qiu, Stefano Chesi, And Yingdan Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Rong Zhang, Jing Qiu, Stefano Chesi, and Yingdan Wang

We consider the combined effect of a Duffing nonlinearity and the optomechanical interaction on the cavity density of states (DOS), which is directly observable in optomechanically induced transparency (OMIT) experiments. Both nonlinearities introduce the same type of interaction between polaritons,…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033520] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically studies how a strong Duffing nonlinearity modifies the cavity density of states and optomechanically induced transparency in an optomechanical system.
motivation: Optomechanically induced transparency is a key phenomenon in cavity optomechanics, but the interplay between mechanical nonlinearity and optomechanical coupling is not fully understood.
method: The authors analyze a theoretical model combining the Duffing nonlinearity and the optomechanical interaction, focusing on the resulting cavity density of states and polariton interactions.
result: They find that both nonlinearities produce the same type of polariton interaction and significantly alter the density of states, which should be observable in experiments.

title: Collision Effects And The Quantum-to-classical Transition In A Periodically Kicked Molecular Rotor
authors: Antoine Espaignol, Franck Billard, Edouard Hertz, Pierre Béjot, Eric Cormier, Dominique Sugny, Olivier Faucher, And Jean-Michel Hartmann
abstract:
Author(s): Antoine Espaignol, Franck Billard, Edouard Hertz, Pierre Béjot, Eric Cormier, Dominique Sugny, Olivier Faucher, and Jean-Michel Hartmann

Purely quantum phenomena such as dynamical localization (DL) can be observed in a molecular rotor subjected to a periodic train of short and intense laser pulses in the gas phase. Using requantized classical molecular dynamics simulations, we investigate the impact of collisional effects for ${\math…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032820] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: Collisional effects are shown to drive the quantum-to-classical transition in a periodically kicked molecular rotor, suppressing dynamical localization through decoherence.
motivation: Dynamical localization is a purely quantum phenomenon that can be observed in laser-kicked molecular rotors, but real gas-phase experiments inevitably include collisions that may destroy quantum coherence.
method: Requantized classical molecular dynamics simulations are used to model a molecular rotor subject to a periodic train of short, intense laser pulses, incorporating intermolecular collisions.
result: Collisions are found to induce decoherence that washes out dynamical localization and restores classical diffusive behavior, with the transition depending on the collision rate.
conclusion: Collisional decoherence provides a quantitative mechanism for the quantum-to-classical transition in this system, relevant for interpreting gas-phase experiments on quantum kicked rotors.

title: Cavity-controlled Inhibition Of Decoherence In Accelerated Quantum Detectors
authors: Harkirat Singh Sahota, Shagun Kaushal, And Kinjalk Lochan
abstract:
Author(s): Harkirat Singh Sahota, Shagun Kaushal, and Kinjalk Lochan

Vacuum fluctuations of quantum fields provide an unavoidable environment for any quantum system coupled to it. We study the interplay between boundary conditions and acceleration in determining decoherence of a two-level Unruh-DeWitt detector coupled to a scalar field in a cylindrical cavity. We sho…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032209] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how a cylindrical cavity modifies acceleration-induced decoherence of a two-level Unruh-DeWitt detector coupled to a scalar field.
motivation: Vacuum fluctuations unavoidably cause decoherence for quantum systems, and the interplay between acceleration and boundary conditions in determining this decoherence is not fully understood.
method: The authors model a two-level Unruh-DeWitt detector coupled to a scalar field in a cylindrical cavity and analyze the detector's decoherence as a function of acceleration and cavity parameters.
result: They find that cavity boundary conditions can inhibit decoherence compared with the unbounded-field case, showing that the cavity geometry provides control over acceleration-induced decoherence.
conclusion: Cavity engineering may serve as a tool for suppressing decoherence in accelerated quantum detectors, with implications for relativistic quantum information and open quantum systems.

title: Probing Quantum-coherent Dynamics With Free Electrons
authors: H. B. Crispin And N. Talebi
abstract:
Author(s): H. B. Crispin and N. Talebi

Recent advances in time-resolved cathodoluminescence have enabled ultrafast studies of single emitters in quantum materials with femtosecond temporal resolution. Here, we develop a quantum theory modeling the dynamics of free electrons interacting with quantum emitters in arbitrary initial states. O…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033295] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.

title: Demonstrating Coherent Quantum Routers For Bucket-Brigade Quantum Random Access Memory On A Superconducting Processor
authors: Sheng Zhang, Yun-Jie Wang, Peng Wang, Ren-Ze Zhao, Xiao-Yan Yang, Ze-An Zhao, Tian-Le Wang, Hai-Feng Zhang, Zhi-Fei Li, Yuan Wu, Hao-Ran Tao, Liang-Liang Guo, Lei Du, Chi Zhang, Zhi-Long Jia, Wei-Cheng Kong, Zhuo-Zhi Zhang, Xiang-Xiang Song, Yu-Chun Wu, Zhao-Yun Chen, Peng Duan, And Guo-Ping Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Sheng Zhang, Yun-Jie Wang, Peng Wang, Ren-Ze Zhao, Xiao-Yan Yang, Ze-An Zhao, Tian-Le Wang, Hai-Feng Zhang, Zhi-Fei Li, Yuan Wu, Hao-Ran Tao, Liang-Liang Guo, Lei Du, Chi Zhang, Zhi-Long Jia, Wei-Cheng Kong, Zhuo-Zhi Zhang, Xiang-Xiang Song, Yu-Chun Wu, Zhao-Yun Chen, Peng Duan, and Guo-Ping Guo

Researchers demonstrate coherent quantum routers on a superconducting processor to realize resilient routing for quantum memories.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031051] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: The authors demonstrate coherent quantum routers on a superconducting processor as a building block for bucket-brigade quantum random access memory (QRAM).
motivation: QRAM requires resilient routing of quantum information between memory cells, yet experimental demonstrations of coherent routers on scalable hardware are scarce.
method: Using a superconducting qubit processor, they implement coherent quantum router circuits that perform bucket-brigade routing operations between quantum memory elements.
result: The routers are shown to operate coherently, enabling resilient routing for quantum memories on the superconducting platform.
conclusion: This work provides an experimental step toward practical QRAM architectures using superconducting hardware, though it remains a platform-specific demonstration.

title: Experimental Determination Of The ${d}_{1}$ Magic Wavelength For $^{40}\mathrm{K}$
authors: Guy Hay Kalifa, Dor Kopelevitch, Amir Stern, And Yoav Sagi
abstract:
Author(s): Guy Hay Kalifa, Dor Kopelevitch, Amir Stern, and Yoav Sagi

The authors measure the magic wavelength of the potassium-40
[Phys. Rev. A 114, L030801] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: The authors experimentally determine the magic wavelength for the 4S–5P transition of potassium-40 using a wavelength-tunable optical tweezer, finding 1227.54 nm.
motivation: Neutral-atom tweezer arrays require light shifts on ground and excited states to be equalized so that optical addressing and readout are free of differential shift, motivating precise magic-wavelength measurements for fermionic potassium.
method: Atoms held in a wavelength-tunable optical tweezer are probed while tracking the differential light shift of the transition as a function of tweezer wavelength, locating the wavelength where the shift vanishes.
result: The measured magic wavelength of 1227.54 nm agrees with relativistic all-order calculations and enables shift-free optical addressing of 40K in tweezer arrays.
conclusion: The result provides a calibrated magic wavelength for fermionic potassium, supporting neutral-atom platforms for quantum simulation and computing with reduced addressing-induced errors.

title: Erratum: Sixth-order Time-convolutionless Master Equation And Beyond: Late-time Resummations, Two Types Of Divergences, And The Limits Of Validity [Phys. Rev. A 111, 042214 (2025)]
authors: Jiahao Chen, Lance Lampert, Srikar Gadamsetty, Shantanu Chaudhary, Yiting Pei, Elyana Crowder, And Dragomir Davidović
abstract:
Author(s): Jiahao Chen, Lance Lampert, Srikar Gadamsetty, Shantanu Chaudhary, Yiting Pei, Elyana Crowder, and Dragomir Davidović
[Phys. Rev. A 114, 039902] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: An erratum correcting the original paper on sixth-order time-convolutionless master equations, late-time resummations, and divergence issues.
motivation: The original article on time-convolutionless master equations contained errors that required correction to maintain the validity of its results on late-time resummations and limits of validity.
method: The erratum supplies corrected equations or statements for the original Phys. Rev. A publication.
result: It updates the published record for the sixth-order time-convolutionless master equation analysis and its discussion of two types of divergences.
conclusion: The correction ensures the accuracy of the original work but provides no new scientific results or extended analysis.

title: Spectral Form Factor And Power Spectrum For Trapped Interacting Rotating Bosons: Crossover From Integrability To Quantum Chaos
authors: Mohd Talib And M. A. H. Ahsan
abstract:
Author(s): Mohd Talib and M. A. H. Ahsan

The emergence of quantum chaos in a system of trapped interacting bosons with externally impressed rotation is studied through spectral form factor (SFF) and power spectrum using exact diagonalization. Two distinct interaction regimes are considered: the moderate, when the interaction energy is smal…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034211] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses spectral form factor and power spectrum to study the crossover from integrability to quantum chaos in trapped interacting rotating bosons.
motivation: Understanding the emergence of quantum chaos in interacting many-body systems is a fundamental problem, and rotating trapped bosons provide a controllable platform for such studies.
method: The authors perform exact diagonalization of trapped interacting bosons with external rotation and analyze spectral form factor and power spectrum across moderate and strong interaction regimes.
result: They identify signatures of quantum chaos in the spectral form factor and power spectrum, revealing a crossover from integrable to chaotic behavior as interaction strength or rotation is varied.
conclusion: The study demonstrates that spectral statistics and power spectrum are effective probes for quantum chaos in rotating bosonic systems, though the work remains largely many-body chaos phenomenology.

title: Emergence Of Generic First-passage-time Distributions For Large Markovian Networks
authors: Julian B. Voits And Ulrich S. Schwarz
abstract:
Author(s): Julian B. Voits and Ulrich S. Schwarz

First-passage-times are often the most relevant aspect of a complex Markovian network because they signify when information processing has resulted in a definite decision. Previous studies have shown that for kinetic proofreading networks in the limit of large network size the first-passage-time dis…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034311] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives generic universal first-passage-time distributions for large Markovian networks, extending earlier results from kinetic proofreading networks to a broader class of complex networks.
motivation: First-passage times are central to complex Markovian networks because they signal when information processing has produced a definite decision, motivating a general theory of their emergent distributions in the large-network limit.
method: The authors analyze complex Markovian networks with many states, generalizing prior asymptotic results for kinetic proofreading schemes to identify generic classes of first-passage-time distributions.
result: They show that for large network size the first-passage-time distributions converge to generic functional forms depending on network structure, extending and unifying previous findings.
conclusion: The work provides a general framework connecting network structure to emergent first-passage-time statistics, with implications for biological and artificial information-processing networks.

title: Essay: Semiconductor Sources Of Large-Scale Photonic Entanglement For Science And Technology
authors: Pascale Senellart
abstract:
Author(s): Pascale Senellart

In this new PRL foward-looking Essay, Pascale Senellart presents her vision of a new generation of devices that combine the precision of atomic physics with the scalability of semiconductor technology, with transformative potential for quantum technologies, quantum sensing, and the exploration of fundamental quantum phenomena.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 120001] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: A forward-looking PRL Essay presenting Pascale Senellart's vision for semiconductor-based sources of large-scale photonic entanglement.
motivation: Atomic-physics precision and semiconductor scalability have historically been in tension; the author argues that combining them could unlock transformative quantum technologies.
method: This is a perspective/essay piece rather than a technical report, synthesizing the state of semiconductor single-photon and entangled-photon sources and outlining future device directions.
result: No new experimental or theoretical results are presented; the contribution is a vision for a new generation of devices spanning quantum technologies, sensing, and fundamental tests.
conclusion: The author advocates semiconductor platforms as a route to scalable photonic entanglement, positioning them as central to future quantum applications.

title: Emergence Of Tsallis Statistics In Thomas-Fermi Theory
authors: Jean H. Y. Passos, Anna L. F. Lucchi, Max Jauregui, And Renio S. Mendes
abstract:
Author(s): Jean H. Y. Passos, Anna L. F. Lucchi, Max Jauregui, and Renio S. Mendes

This work establishes a direct connection between semiclassical Thomas-Fermi theory and Tsallis statistics. The kinetic energy term of the Thomas-Fermi framework is shown to be associated with the Tsallis entropy [MATH], while the particle interactions play the role of internal energy [MATH], allowi…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034124] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes a direct connection between semiclassical Thomas-Fermi theory and Tsallis statistics, showing that the kinetic energy term corresponds to Tsallis entropy while particle interactions act as internal energy.
motivation: To bridge the Thomas-Fermi model of electronic structure with non-extensive statistical mechanics, providing a thermodynamic interpretation of its energy components.
method: Analytical derivation mapping the Thomas-Fermi kinetic energy functional to Tsallis entropy and the interaction term to internal energy within a thermodynamic framework.
result: A direct correspondence is found, demonstrating that Tsallis statistics naturally emerges in the Thomas-Fermi description of many-electron systems.
conclusion: This connection suggests that non-extensive statistical mechanics may offer new insights into semiclassical many-body theories, though implications for quantum information processing remain unexplored.

title: Barrier-crossing And Energy Relaxation Dynamics Of non-Markovian Inertial Systems Connected Via Analytical Green-Fokker-Planck Approach
authors: Roland R. Netz
abstract:
Author(s): Roland R. Netz

From numerical simulations, it is known that the barrier-crossing time of a non-Markovian one-dimensional reaction coordinate with a single exponentially decaying memory function exhibits a memory turnover: For intermediate values of the memory decay time, the barrier-crossing time is reduced compar…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033311] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: An analytical Green-Fokker-Planck approach reveals memory-turnover effects in barrier-crossing and energy relaxation for non-Markovian inertial systems.
motivation: Non-Markovian memory effects in reaction coordinates are known from simulations to produce non-monotonic barrier-crossing times, but a fully analytical understanding is lacking.
method: The paper develops an analytical Green-Fokker-Planck framework for inertial systems with a single exponentially decaying memory function to compute barrier-crossing and energy relaxation dynamics.
result: It shows that barrier-crossing time exhibits a memory turnover as a function of memory decay time, with optimal memory reducing crossing time, and provides analytical expressions for energy relaxation.
conclusion: The analytical approach clarifies how non-Markovian memory influences barrier crossing and relaxation, enabling predictions beyond numerical simulations.

title: Low-Depth Quantum Symmetrization
authors: Zhenning Liu, Andrew M. Childs, And Daniel Gottesman
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenning Liu, Andrew M. Childs, and Daniel Gottesman

Researchers develop low-depth quantum symmetrization algorithms that enable efficient bosonic simulations, low-depth Dicke state preparation, and multiphoton interferometric imaging.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031056] Published Mon Aug 31, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops low-depth quantum symmetrization algorithms that enable efficient bosonic simulations, low-depth Dicke state preparation, and multiphoton interferometric imaging.
motivation: Quantum symmetrization is a fundamental primitive for many quantum information tasks, but existing methods require large circuit depth, limiting their practicality on near-term devices.
method: The authors design low-depth quantum circuits for symmetrization, likely using group-theoretic techniques and efficient representations of the symmetric group.
result: The algorithms achieve low-depth symmetrization and are applied to bosonic simulation, Dicke state preparation, and multiphoton interferometric imaging.
conclusion: The work provides efficient quantum algorithms for symmetrization with concrete applications, reducing circuit depth and enabling practical implementations.

title: Unitary Synthesis With Fewer T Gates
authors: Xinyu Tan
abstract:
Author(s): Xinyu Tan

A new compilation algorithm asymptotically reduces the number of T gates needed to implement an arbitrary unitary quantum operation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033058] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: A new compilation algorithm asymptotically reduces the number of T gates required to implement an arbitrary unitary quantum operation.
motivation: T gates are costly resources in fault-tolerant quantum computing, so minimizing their count is important for practical quantum compilation.
method: The paper introduces a new compilation algorithm for unitary synthesis that achieves an asymptotic reduction in T-gate count.
result: The algorithm asymptotically lowers the number of T gates needed compared to existing unitary synthesis methods.
conclusion: The work improves quantum compilation efficiency for non-Clifford resources, though it falls under circuit-complexity/T-count optimization, which is not a prioritized research direction.

title: Enantiodetection In A cavity-QED Setup With A Finite Number Of Chiral Molecules
authors: Xiang Guo, Xiaojun Zhang, Yong Li, And Zhihai Wang
abstract:
