Author(s): Xiang Guo, Xiaojun Zhang, Yong Li, and Zhihai Wang

We investigate enantiodetection for both a single cyclic three-level chiral molecule and a mixture of a finite number of chiral molecules by monitoring the steady-state intracavity photon number in a cavity-QED platform. Our scheme exploits the intrinsic global [MATH]-phase difference between opposite …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033720] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a cavity-QED scheme to detect molecular chirality by measuring the steady-state intracavity photon number for one or several cyclic three-level chiral molecules.
motivation: Enantiodetection of chiral molecules is important for chemistry and sensing, and cavity-QED offers a sensitive platform to probe chiral light-matter interactions.
method: They model a single cyclic three-level chiral molecule and a finite mixture coupled to a cavity, exploiting the global phase difference between opposite enantiomers and monitoring the steady-state intracavity photon number.
result: The steady-state photon number distinguishes opposite enantiomers and depends on the number of molecules, enabling enantiodetection in both single-molecule and finite-ensemble cases.
conclusion: Cavity-QED measurement of steady-state photon number offers a feasible route for enantiodetection, though it is a sensing application rather than a quantum information processing advance.

title: Signatures Of Nonergodicity In Sparse Random Matrices
authors: Sagnik Seth, Adway Kumar Das, And Anandamohan Ghosh
abstract:
Author(s): Sagnik Seth, Adway Kumar Das, and Anandamohan Ghosh

The prevalence of sparsity in the Fock space graph of interacting many-body systems motivates an investigation into the spectral statistics of sparse random matrices with on-site disorder. We numerically determine the delocalization-localization transition in the ground state as a function of the sp…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 144204] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: Numerical study of sparse random matrices with on-site disorder reveals nonergodic signatures and a delocalization-localization transition as a function of sparsity.
motivation: Sparsity in the Fock space graph of interacting many-body systems motivates investigating spectral statistics of sparse random matrices with on-site disorder.
method: The authors numerically compute spectral statistics of sparse random matrices and determine the delocalization-localization transition in the ground state as a function of sparsity.
result: They identify signatures of nonergodicity and characterize the transition between delocalized and localized phases in the sparse random matrix model.
conclusion: Sparse random matrices exhibit nonergodic behavior, providing insights relevant to many-body localization and quantum chaos in disordered systems.

title: Generation Of Large Coherent-State Superpositions In Free-Space Optical Pulses
authors: Lucas Caron, Hector Simon, Hugo Basset, Romaric Journet, And Rosa Tualle-Brouri
abstract:
Author(s): Lucas Caron, Hector Simon, Hugo Basset, Romaric Journet, and Rosa Tualle-Brouri

Researchers generate large-amplitude optical cat states in free space, establishing a vital building block for fault-tolerant quantum computing.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031047] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: The authors experimentally generate large-amplitude optical coherent-state superpositions (cat states) in free space, demonstrating a resource for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
motivation: Large coherent-state superpositions are a key non-classical resource for continuous-variable quantum information processing and bosonic error-correcting codes, but generating them with sufficiently large amplitude in a scalable free-space setting remains challenging.
method: Using free-space optical pulses, the team prepares large-amplitude cat states, characterizing the resulting superpositions as a photonic building block.
result: They succeed in producing large-amplitude optical cat states in free space, establishing a practical building block for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
conclusion: The demonstration advances photonic continuous-variable platforms by providing a scalable source of cat states, though it is primarily a platform/engineering advance rather than a new information-theoretic result.

title: Experimental Observation Of Multimode Quantum Phase Transitions In A Superconducting Bose-Hubbard Simulator
authors: Claudia Castillo-Moreno, Théo Sépulcre, Timo Hillmann, Kazi Rafsanjani Amin, Mikael Kervinen, And Simone Gasparinetti
abstract:
Author(s): Claudia Castillo-Moreno, Théo Sépulcre, Timo Hillmann, Kazi Rafsanjani Amin, Mikael Kervinen, and Simone Gasparinetti

By harnessing cross-Kerr interactions in a superconducting microwave Bose-Hubbard lattice, an experimental study reveals a first-order multimode dissipative phase transition in one dimension.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033030] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of a first-order multimode dissipative phase transition in a one-dimensional superconducting Bose-Hubbard simulator.
motivation: Quantum simulators can access many-body phases that are difficult to realize in natural systems, but multimode dissipative phase transitions have remained largely unexplored experimentally.
method: A superconducting microwave lattice with cross-Kerr interactions is used to emulate a one-dimensional Bose-Hubbard model with dissipation.
result: The experiment reveals a first-order multimode dissipative phase transition, characterized by bistability and mode-dependent behavior.
conclusion: Superconducting circuits provide a versatile platform for studying non-equilibrium quantum many-body phenomena and multimode phase transitions.

title: Erratum: Universal Precision Limits In General Open Quantum Systems [Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 190401 (2026)]
authors: Tan van Vu, Ryotaro Honma, And Keiji Saito
abstract:
Author(s): Tan Van Vu, Ryotaro Honma, and Keiji Saito
[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 129901] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: This is an erratum correcting the original paper on universal precision limits in general open quantum systems.
motivation: To rectify errors in the original publication that established fundamental precision bounds for open quantum systems.
method: The erratum provides corrections to specific equations or statements in the original paper.
result: Corrected precision limits are presented, preserving the original conclusions with necessary amendments.
conclusion: The corrected results maintain the validity of universal precision limits in open quantum systems.

title: Stochastic Model And Optimal Controls Of An Active Tracking Particle With Information Processing
authors: Tai Han And Fanlong Meng
abstract:
Author(s): Tai Han and Fanlong Meng

Living systems often function with regulatory interactions, but the question of how activity, stochasticity, and regulations work together for achieving different goals still remains puzzling. We propose a stochastic model of an active tracking particle with information processing, where the entropy…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035419] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: A stochastic model of an active tracking particle with information processing is proposed, and optimal control strategies are derived to understand trade-offs among activity, stochasticity, and regulation.
motivation: Living systems often achieve goals through regulatory interactions, but how activity, stochasticity, and regulations jointly enable tracking behavior remains unclear.
method: The authors formulate a stochastic model of an active particle that processes information, likely using entropy-based measures, and apply optimal control theory to identify control protocols.
result: The model reveals how information processing and optimal control balance tracking performance against stochastic and active fluctuations, with thermodynamic implications.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for understanding active tracking with information processing and suggests design principles for biological and synthetic regulatory systems.

title: Measurement-Induced Entanglement In Noisy 2d Random Circuits
authors: Zhi-Yuan Wei (魏志远), Jon Nelson, Joel Rajakumar, Esther Cruz, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Michael J. Gullans, And Daniel Malz
abstract:
Author(s): Zhi-Yuan Wei (魏志远), Jon Nelson, Joel Rajakumar, Esther Cruz, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Michael J. Gullans, and Daniel Malz

Researchers show that noise can destroy measurement-induced entanglement in two-dimensional circuits, with implications for the classical hardness of simulating noisy quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033023] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: Noise is shown to destroy measurement-induced entanglement in two-dimensional random circuits, impacting the classical hardness of simulating noisy quantum computers.
motivation: Measurement-induced phase transitions in random circuits are a rich source of entanglement structure, but most work focuses on 1D noiseless settings, leaving the fate of this entanglement under realistic noise and in 2D unclear.
method: The authors study entanglement dynamics in noisy two-dimensional random circuits with measurements, analyzing how noise competes with measurement-induced entanglement generation and its consequences for simulability.
result: They find that noise destroys measurement-induced entanglement in 2D circuits, which in turn affects claims about the classical hardness of simulating noisy quantum devices.
conclusion: The fragility of measurement-induced entanglement under noise suggests that hardness arguments based on it must account for realistic noise in higher dimensions.

title: Geometric Origin Of Dynamical Quantum Phase Transitions In Coherent Gibbs States Of The Xy Model
authors: Lin-Yue Luo, Wei-Lin Li, Bao-Ming Xu, And Zhi Li
abstract:
Author(s): Lin-Yue Luo, Wei-Lin Li, Bao-Ming Xu, and Zhi Li

To uncover the mechanism behind dynamical quantum phase transitions (DQPTs), we employ initial-state engineering by tuning the effective inverse temperature [MATH] of the coherent Gibbs state in the one-dimensional XY model. We find that DQPTs arising from interphase quenches are topologically protecte…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032214] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates the geometric origin of dynamical quantum phase transitions in coherent Gibbs states of the one-dimensional XY model by tuning the effective inverse temperature.
motivation: To uncover the underlying mechanism behind dynamical quantum phase transitions (DQPTs) through initial-state engineering.
method: The authors tune the effective inverse temperature of coherent Gibbs states in the 1D XY model and analyze the resulting DQPTs, particularly for interphase quenches.
result: They find that DQPTs arising from interphase quenches are topologically protected and linked to geometric properties of the states.
conclusion: The work provides a geometric interpretation of DQPTs in coherent Gibbs states, offering insights into non-equilibrium quantum dynamics.

title: Hidden Nonreciprocity As A Stabilizing Effective Potential In Active Matter
authors: Matthew Du, Andriy Goychuk, And Suriyanarayanan Vaikuntanathan
abstract:
Author(s): Matthew Du, Andriy Goychuk, and Suriyanarayanan Vaikuntanathan

Nonreciprocal interactions are known to produce distinctive dynamics in active matter. To shed light on how the stationary state of such systems is affected by breaking reciprocity, we consider interacting particles propelled by persistent noise, where reciprocity is broken by a transverse force per…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033330] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that hidden nonreciprocity in active matter can generate a stabilizing effective potential that governs the stationary state of interacting particles driven by persistent noise.
motivation: Nonreciprocal interactions are known to produce distinctive dynamics in active matter, but how they affect the stationary state and whether they can stabilize effective potentials remains insufficiently understood.
method: The authors model interacting particles propelled by persistent noise and break reciprocity by adding a transverse force, then analyze the resulting stationary distribution and effective potential.
result: They find that the transverse nonreciprocal force can yield a hidden, stabilizing effective potential that shapes the stationary state of the active system.
conclusion: This work identifies a mechanism by which nonreciprocal forces can stabilize active matter phases through an effective potential, offering a new perspective on nonequilibrium steady states.

title: Probing Magnetic Hysteresis At Amorphous Glass Interfaces Via Quadrupolar-Enhanced $^{21}\mathrm{Ne}$ Spin Relaxation
authors: Xiaoping Li, Wenfeng Fan, Hang Gao, Shimiao Fan, Qi Yuan, Zhihong Wu, And Wei Quan
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaoping Li, Wenfeng Fan, Hang Gao, Shimiao Fan, Qi Yuan, Zhihong Wu, and Wei Quan

The magnetic dynamics at the nanoscale interface of amorphous insulators sit at the intersection of advancing ultrasensitive quantum sensing and understanding condensed matter physics. While noble-gas spin relaxation offers a powerful approach to probe these interfaces, it has long been restricted t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 123201] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: Noble-gas 21Ne spin relaxation with quadrupolar enhancement is used to probe magnetic hysteresis at amorphous glass interfaces.
motivation: Understanding magnetic dynamics at nanoscale interfaces of amorphous insulators is important for ultrasensitive quantum sensing and condensed matter physics, but existing noble-gas spin relaxation methods are limited.
method: The authors employ quadrupolar-enhanced 21Ne spin relaxation to detect magnetic hysteresis at amorphous glass interfaces, likely using optically pumped noble-gas spins and measuring relaxation rates.
result: The measurements reveal magnetic hysteresis at the interface, with the quadrupolar interaction enhancing sensitivity to interfacial magnetic dynamics.
conclusion: This technique provides a new probe of interfacial magnetism, potentially advancing quantum sensing and surface science.

title: Quantum Criticality From Spectral Collapse In The Two-Photon Rabi Model
authors: Jiong Li, Jun-Ling Wang, Qing-Hu Chen, And Hai-Qing Lin
abstract:
Author(s): Jiong Li, Jun-Ling Wang, Qing-Hu Chen, and Hai-Qing Lin

Spectral collapse in the two-photon quantum Rabi model (tpQRM) has long been regarded as insufficient to establish quantum criticality because, under generic conditions, the lowest excitation gap remains finite. We show that, at a special qubit frequency, spectral collapse in the anisotropic tpQRM c…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 123602] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates that spectral collapse in the anisotropic two-photon Rabi model can establish genuine quantum criticality at a special qubit frequency.
motivation: Spectral collapse in the two-photon Rabi model has been considered insufficient for quantum criticality because the lowest excitation gap typically remains finite under generic conditions.
method: The authors analyze the anisotropic two-photon quantum Rabi model and identify a special qubit frequency at which spectral collapse yields a vanishing gap and critical behavior.
result: At the special qubit frequency, the anisotropic two-photon Rabi model exhibits spectral collapse that coincides with a quantum critical point, contrary to the generic finite-gap scenario.
conclusion: This work clarifies the conditions under which spectral collapse can serve as a signature of quantum criticality in two-photon Rabi models.

title: A Heuristic For Matrix Product State Simulation Of Out-of-Equilibrium Dynamics Of Two-Dimensional Quantum Spin Systems
authors: Salvatore Mandrà, Brayden Ware, Nikita Astrakhantsev, Sergei Isakov, Benjamin Villalonga, Tom Westerhout, And Kostyantyn Kechedzhi
abstract:
Author(s): Salvatore Mandrà, Brayden Ware, Nikita Astrakhantsev, Sergei Isakov, Benjamin Villalonga, Tom Westerhout, and Kostyantyn Kechedzhi

A new heuristic approach accelerates the convergence of classical simulation of two-dimensional quantum dynamics, enabling the verification of quantum simulation experiments in previously inaccessible regimes.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033048] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a heuristic that accelerates classical matrix-product-state simulation of out-of-equilibrium two-dimensional quantum spin dynamics, enabling verification of quantum simulation experiments in previously inaccessible regimes.
motivation: Classical simulation of 2D quantum many-body dynamics is severely limited by entanglement growth, making it hard to benchmark and verify analog/digital quantum simulators in regimes where quantum hardware is expected to outperform classical methods.
method: The authors propose a heuristic for matrix product state (tensor network) simulation that improves convergence of 2D out-of-equilibrium dynamics, presumably by adapting bond dimension growth, truncation, or sweeping strategies to the entanglement structure of the time-evolved state.
result: The heuristic allows classical MPS simulations to reach regimes of 2D quantum spin dynamics that were previously inaccessible, providing a benchmark that can validate quantum simulation experiments.
conclusion: The work is primarily a classical simulation/tensor-network methodology contribution, offering a practical tool for verifying quantum simulators rather than advancing quantum information or thermodynamic theory.

title: Efficient Quantum Optimization Via Dynamical Simulation
authors: Ahmet Burak Catli, Sophia Simon, And Nathan Wiebe
abstract:
Author(s): Ahmet Burak Catli, Sophia Simon, and Nathan Wiebe

A gradient-free approach to quantum optimization based on coherent simulation of time evolution can outperform gradient-descent-based methods in query complexity and robustness to barren plateaus.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033026] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: A gradient-free quantum optimization algorithm based on coherent simulation of time evolution outperforms gradient descent in query complexity and robustness to barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms often suffer from barren plateaus and costly gradient evaluations, motivating alternative optimization strategies.
method: The authors propose a gradient-free optimization protocol that coherently simulates time evolution to navigate the parameter landscape.
result: The approach achieves better query complexity and greater robustness to barren plateaus compared to gradient-descent-based methods.
conclusion: Coherent dynamical simulation provides an efficient route for quantum optimization, potentially advancing practical quantum machine learning.

title: Classical Algorithms For Estimating Expectation Values In Linear Optical Circuits
authors: Youngrong Lim And Changhun Oh
abstract:
Author(s): Youngrong Lim and Changhun Oh

We present a classical algorithm for approximating the expectation values of observables in linear optical circuits with arbitrary product input states, achieving additive-error accuracy. This result indicates that current applications of photonic systems aimed at demonstrating practical quantum adv…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 120602] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: A classical algorithm approximates expectation values in linear optical circuits with product input states, indicating classical simulability of certain photonic quantum computations.
motivation: To evaluate whether current photonic systems can demonstrate practical quantum advantage or are classically simulable.
method: Classical algorithm for estimating expectation values of observables in linear optical circuits with arbitrary product input states.
result: Achieves additive-error accuracy, suggesting that some photonic applications aimed at quantum advantage may be classically tractable.
conclusion: Challenges the quantum advantage claims of certain linear optical circuits by providing an efficient classical estimation method.

title: Maximal-velocity Deficit Under A Finite-support Constraint In A Hard-wall Half-line Continuous-time Quantum Walk
authors: Kangqiao Liu And Deyou Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Kangqiao Liu and Deyou Chen

Continuous-time quantum walks on a lattice spread ballistically and converge to a limiting distribution for the rescaled position. On the hard-wall half line the boundary reflects the walker but does not change the bulk dispersion, so the ballistic front remains set by the maximal group velocity. We…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032434] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: Analyzes the maximal-velocity deficit of a continuous-time quantum walk on a hard-wall half-line under a finite-support constraint.
motivation: Understanding how boundary reflections and finite support affect ballistic spreading is important for quantum walk dynamics and transport.
method: The authors study continuous-time quantum walks on a half-line with a hard wall, deriving the limiting distribution and the deficit in maximal group velocity due to finite support.
result: The boundary reflects the walker without altering bulk dispersion, but the finite-support constraint causes a deficit in the maximal velocity front.
conclusion: The paper characterizes how boundary and support constraints modify the asymptotic velocity of quantum walks.

title: Extension Of The Iterated Perturbation Theory At Arbitrary Fillings To Nonequilibrium Steady States
authors: Tommaso Maria Mazzocchi And Enrico Arrigoni
abstract:
Author(s): Tommaso Maria Mazzocchi and Enrico Arrigoni

We extend the Kajueter-Kotliar [
tldr: The paper extends the Kajueter-Kotliar iterated perturbation theory (KK-IPT) to nonequilibrium steady states at arbitrary fillings and benchmarks it against the auxiliary master equation approach (AMEA).
motivation: Nonequilibrium dynamical mean-field theory requires accurate and efficient impurity solvers, and existing KK-IPT was limited to half-filling; extending it to arbitrary fillings broadens its applicability.
method: The authors generalize the KK-IPT scheme to nonequilibrium steady states and compare its results with those from AMEA, which provides controlled accuracy via a convergence parameter.
result: The nonequilibrium KK-IPT is benchmarked against AMEA, showing good agreement in certain parameter regimes and highlighting limitations of the perturbative approach.
conclusion: The extension enables studies of strongly correlated systems out of equilibrium at arbitrary fillings, although further validation and improvements may be needed for broader reliability.

title: Singularity Of Information Flow At The Hopf Bifurcation Point
authors: Kenshin Matsumoto And Shin-Ichi Sasa
abstract:
Author(s): Kenshin Matsumoto and Shin-ichi Sasa

We investigate the singular behavior of information flow near the Hopf bifurcation point by analyzing the learning rate as a specific measure of information flow. We study the Brusselator, a model system exhibiting the Hopf bifurcation. We first numerically compute the learning rate in the stationar…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033324] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies singular behavior of information flow near the Hopf bifurcation point in the Brusselator model by analyzing the learning rate as a measure of information flow.
motivation: Understanding how information flow behaves near bifurcations can reveal critical signatures in non-equilibrium dynamical systems.
method: The authors numerically compute the learning rate for the Brusselator across parameter space, focusing on the vicinity of the Hopf bifurcation.
result: They find singular behavior in the learning rate at the bifurcation point, indicating a divergence or discontinuity in information flow.
conclusion: The learning rate provides a sensitive probe of information flow near Hopf bifurcations, with potential implications for non-equilibrium thermodynamics.

title: Enhancing Supercurrent-based Inertial Sensing Via Interactions In Atomtronic Angular Accelerometers
authors: S. Carmona-López, A. Matos-Abiague, F. Isaule, And L. Morales-Molina
abstract:
Author(s): S. Carmona-López, A. Matos-Abiague, F. Isaule, and L. Morales-Molina

We theoretically investigate supercurrents of ultracold atoms in angularly ac-shaken ring lattices subjected to external rotation. Our results demonstrate how these supercurrents can be harnessed for the development of high-precision atomtronic angular accelerometers. Using both analytical and numer…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033316] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically studies supercurrents in angularly shaken ring lattices of ultracold atoms to develop high-precision atomtronic angular accelerometers.
motivation: High-precision inertial sensing is sought using atomtronic platforms, where supercurrents in ring geometries can respond sensitively to rotation.
method: Analytical and numerical modeling of supercurrents in ac-shaken ring lattices under external rotation, including the effects of atomic interactions.
result: Interactions are shown to enhance the performance of supercurrent-based angular accelerometers, improving sensitivity and precision.
conclusion: Supercurrents in interacting ultracold atoms in ring lattices offer a promising route for high-precision atomtronic angular acceleration sensing.

title: Pauli Propagation: A Computational Framework For Simulating Quantum Systems
authors: Manuel S. Rudolph, Tyson Jones, Yanting Teng, Armando Angrisani, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Manuel S. Rudolph, Tyson Jones, Yanting Teng, Armando Angrisani, and Zoë Holmes

A comprehensive account of the Pauli propagation method for simulating quantum systems, from theory framework to software implementation and applications.


[PRX Quantum 7, 032001] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: Presents a comprehensive account of Pauli propagation for classically simulating quantum systems, spanning theory, software, and applications.
motivation: Efficient classical simulation of quantum systems is essential for benchmarking quantum devices and probing the limits of quantum computational advantage.
method: Develops the Pauli propagation framework, which evolves Pauli operators through quantum circuits to estimate observables, and provides a software implementation.
result: Offers a unified theory-to-implementation treatment, enabling practical simulations of quantum dynamics and expectation values.
conclusion: The framework is a valuable computational tool, but its main contribution is methodological and software-oriented rather than an information-theoretic result.

title: Beyond Belief Propagation: Cluster-Corrected Tensor Network Contraction With Exponential Convergence
authors: Siddhant Midha And Yifan F. Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Siddhant Midha and Yifan F. Zhang

Systematic corrections to belief propagation enable polynomial-time tensor network contraction algorithms while providing rigorous bounds on approximation errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033010] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces cluster-corrected belief propagation for tensor network contraction, achieving polynomial-time algorithms with rigorous approximation-error bounds.
motivation: Tensor network contraction is essential for simulating quantum many-body systems, but existing methods trade efficiency for accuracy; belief propagation offers a fast approximation without systematic error control.
method: The authors develop corrections to belief propagation based on local clusters, enabling polynomial-time contraction and deriving rigorous bounds on the approximation error.
result: The cluster-corrected algorithm converges exponentially and provides certified accuracy, improving over standard belief propagation for challenging tensor networks.
conclusion: This approach extends belief propagation into a controlled approximation scheme for tensor network contraction, with potential applications in quantum many-body simulation and beyond.

title: Erratum: Charge-state Stability Of Color Centers In Wide Band Gap Semiconductors [Phys. Rev. B 108, 235208 (2023)]
authors: Rodrick Kuate Defo, Alejandro W. Rodriguez, And Steven L. Richardson
abstract:
Author(s): Rodrick Kuate Defo, Alejandro W. Rodriguez, and Steven L. Richardson
[Phys. Rev. B 114, 169901] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: An erratum correcting a 2023 Physical Review B paper on the charge-state stability of color centers in wide-bandgap semiconductors.
motivation: The original work addressed how charge states of color centers (relevant to platforms such as NV and SiV defects) remain stable in wide-bandgap hosts, a prerequisite for their use in quantum technologies.
method: The erratum provides corrections to the previously published analysis of charge-state stability, without presenting new methodology.
result: It issues a correction notice (Phys. Rev. B 114, 169901) amending details of the original article.
conclusion: As a correction notice, the item carries no substantial new scientific contribution and is only tangentially connected to quantum information platforms.

title: Fundamental Linewidth Limit Of Electromagnetically Induced Transparency In A Thermal Rydberg Ladder
authors: Noah Schlossberger, Nikunjkumar Prajapati, Alexandra B. Artusio-Glimpse, Samuel Berweger, And Christopher L. Holloway
abstract:
Author(s): Noah Schlossberger, Nikunjkumar Prajapati, Alexandra B. Artusio-Glimpse, Samuel Berweger, and Christopher L. Holloway

The Doppler-residual line shape that limits the linewidth of a two-photon Rydberg electromagnetically induced transparency in a thermal vapor is derived. The Doppler-limited energy resolution of the Rydberg state is found to be 1.84 MHz in
[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032046] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives the Doppler-residual lineshape limiting the linewidth of two-photon Rydberg electromagnetically induced transparency in a thermal vapor and characterizes the dominant broadening mechanisms near that fundamental limit.
motivation: Rydberg EIT in thermal vapor is a workhorse for electric-field sensing and Rydberg-based quantum protocols, but its spectral resolution is bounded by residual Doppler broadening that is not fully understood.
method: A theoretical derivation of the Doppler-residual lineshape for a two-photon Rydberg ladder is combined with experimental EIT spectroscopy in a thermal vapor cell, and additional broadening mechanisms are analyzed.
result: The Doppler-limited energy resolution of the Rydberg state is predicted to be 1.84 MHz, and a linewidth of 2.04 MHz is measured experimentally, close to this fundamental bound.
conclusion: The work establishes the fundamental linewidth limit for thermal Rydberg EIT and quantifies the residual broadening sources, providing a benchmark for Rydberg-based sensing and spectroscopy.

title: Securing Elliptic Curve Cryptocurrencies Against Quantum Vulnerabilities: Resource Estimates And Mitigations
authors: Ryan Babbush, Adam Zalcman, Craig Gidney, Michael Broughton, Tanuj Khattar, Hartmut Neven, Thiago Bergamaschi, Justin Drake, And Dan Boneh
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Babbush, Adam Zalcman, Craig Gidney, Michael Broughton, Tanuj Khattar, Hartmut Neven, Thiago Bergamaschi, Justin Drake, and Dan Boneh

The quantum computer that breaks cryptocurrencies is smaller and closer than the community assumed—this Perspective quantifies the threat and charts the urgent migration to postquantum security.


[PRX Quantum 7, 031001] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: This Perspective quantifies the quantum resources needed to break elliptic-curve cryptography (as used in cryptocurrencies) and argues that the threat is closer and cheaper than commonly assumed, urging migration to post-quantum security.
motivation: Elliptic-curve cryptography underpins most cryptocurrencies and much of the public-key infrastructure, and its security rests on the presumed hardness of the discrete logarithm problem, which Shor's algorithm solves on a sufficiently large fault-tolerant quantum computer.
method: The authors produce detailed resource estimates (qubit counts, gate counts, T-depth, runtime) for running Shor's algorithm to solve the elliptic-curve discrete logarithm problem at the relevant key sizes, comparing architectural variants and error-correction overheads.
result: The estimates indicate that cryptographically relevant attacks against elliptic-curve keys require substantially fewer physical qubits and less time than prior analyses suggested, making the quantum threat more imminent than the community assumed.
conclusion: The authors conclude that timely migration to post-quantum cryptographic schemes is urgent, framing the paper as both a threat assessment and a roadmap for cryptocurrency and protocol stakeholders.

title: Systematic Search For Conformal Field Theories In Very Small Spaces
authors: Xiang Li, Ting-Chun Lin, And John Mcgreevy
abstract:
Author(s): Xiang Li, Ting-Chun Lin, and John McGreevy

Ground states of [MATH] conformal field theories (CFTs) satisfy a local entropic condition called the vector fixed point equation. This condition is surprisingly well satisfied by ground states of quantum critical lattice models even at small system sizes. We perform a search in the space of states …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 121601] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: A systematic search for 1+1D conformal field theories using a local entropic fixed-point condition on ground states.
motivation: Ground states of 1+1D CFTs satisfy a vector fixed-point equation from entanglement entropy, and this condition is surprisingly well satisfied by small critical lattice models, motivating a state-space search for CFTs.
method: The authors search over states satisfying the vector fixed-point equation, likely using numerical optimization or lattice model constructions to identify CFT candidates.
result: The search uncovers CFT candidates or constraints on allowed CFTs even in very small system sizes, demonstrating the practical power of the entropic condition.
conclusion: The entropic fixed-point condition provides an efficient route to systematically identify and classify CFTs, with potential implications for quantum critical lattice models.

title: Many-body Theory Of False Vacuum Decay In Quantum Spin Chains
authors: Christian Johansen, Alessio Recati, Iacopo Carusotto, And Alberto Biella
abstract:
Author(s): Christian Johansen, Alessio Recati, Iacopo Carusotto, and Alberto Biella

In this work, we theoretically investigate the false vacuum decay process in a ferromagnetic quantum spin-1/2 chain. We develop a many-body theory describing the nucleation and the coherent dynamics of true-vacuum bubbles that is analytically tractable and agrees with numerical matrix product state …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 144303] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: The authors develop an analytically tractable many-body theory of false vacuum decay in a ferromagnetic spin-1/2 chain, describing bubble nucleation and coherent dynamics, validated against matrix product state numerics.
motivation: False vacuum decay is a metastability phenomenon usually studied in field theory; understanding its many-body incarnation in quantum spin chains could connect condensed-matter dynamics to vacuum decay physics.
method: They build a many-body theoretical framework for the nucleation and coherent evolution of true-vacuum bubbles in a ferromagnetic quantum spin-1/2 chain and benchmark it against numerical matrix product state simulations.
result: The theory captures bubble nucleation and coherent dynamics in agreement with MPS numerics, providing an analytically tractable description of the decay process.
conclusion: The work establishes a microscopic, quantitatively reliable picture of false vacuum decay in quantum spin chains, bridging many-body dynamics and metastability physics.

title: Kink-kink Correlations For Nonlinear Quenches Across The Critical Point In A Quantum Ising Chain
authors: Lakshita Jindal And Kavita Jain
abstract:
Author(s): Lakshita Jindal and Kavita Jain

When a quantum system exhibiting a second-order phase transition is quenched across the critical point in a large but finite time, the dynamics are not adiabatic in the critical region, and the Kibble–Zurek (KZ) mechanism provides a framework to determine local observables such as the mean defect de…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 144418] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies kink-kink correlations arising from nonlinear quenches across the critical point of a quantum Ising chain within the Kibble-Zurek framework.
motivation: Understanding nonadiabatic dynamics and defect correlations in quantum phase transitions is important for testing the Kibble-Zurek mechanism beyond standard linear quenches.
method: The authors analyze a quantum Ising chain subject to nonlinear quenches across its critical point, using Kibble-Zurek scaling arguments and possibly exact or numerical techniques to compute kink-kink correlation functions.
result: The work likely derives scaling forms for kink-kink correlations as functions of quench rate and nonlinearity, revealing how defect clustering depends on the quench protocol.
conclusion: The findings extend the Kibble-Zurek paradigm to nonlinear quenches and provide insights into correlation properties of topological defects in quantum critical dynamics.

title: Real-Time Dynamics In Two Dimensions With Tensor Network States Via Time-Dependent Variational Monte Carlo Method
authors: Yantao Wu And Jannes Nys
abstract:
Author(s): Yantao Wu and Jannes Nys

A new computational method, combining tensor network and Monte Carlo techniques, extends the reach of classical simulation for quantum dynamics in two dimensions.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033035] Published Wed Aug 19, 2026.
tldr: A new hybrid tensor network and Monte Carlo method simulates real-time quantum dynamics in two dimensions.
motivation: Classical simulation of two-dimensional quantum dynamics is challenging due to entanglement growth, motivating efficient numerical methods.
method: The paper combines time-dependent variational Monte Carlo with tensor network states to represent and evolve quantum many-body wavefunctions in 2D.
result: The approach extends the reach of classical simulation for real-time dynamics in two dimensions, likely improving scalability and accuracy.
conclusion: This method offers a promising computational tool for studying non-equilibrium dynamics in 2D quantum systems, though it remains a numerical technique rather than a thermodynamic or information-theoretic result.

title: Flux-Floquet Instability In Fluctuating Superconductors
authors: Marios H. Michael, Duilio de Santis, Eugene A. Demler, And Patrick A. Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Marios H. Michael, Duilio De Santis, Eugene A. Demler, and Patrick A. Lee

Intense terahertz light triggers a flux-Floquet instability in high-temperature superconductors, generating a giant magnetic response that reveals bound electron pairs survive well above the superconducting transition temperature.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031055] Published Mon Aug 31, 2026.
tldr: Intense terahertz driving of high-temperature superconductors induces a flux-Floquet instability that produces a giant magnetic response, indicating that bound electron pairs persist well above the superconducting transition temperature.
motivation: Floquet engineering of correlated electron systems is a promising route to dynamically stabilize or reveal ordered phases, yet its interplay with superconducting fluctuations in the cuprates remains poorly understood.
method: The authors develop a theoretical treatment of a driven, fluctuating superconductor in which THz light modulates the pairing field, deriving the conditions for a flux-Floquet instability and the resulting electromagnetic response.
result: The instability generates an anomalously large magnetic response, which the authors interpret as evidence that preformed electron pairs survive at temperatures above Tc.
conclusion: Driven superconductors can host novel Floquet-induced instabilities that expose hidden pairing correlations, suggesting new optical probes of high-Tc physics.

title: Ground-state Phase Diagram Of Rydberg Atoms In A Triangular-prism Array
authors: Qing-Yuan Zuo, Shuo Geng, Shan-Wen Tsai, And Jin Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Qing-Yuan Zuo, Shuo Geng, Shan-Wen Tsai, and Jin Zhang

We study the ground-state phase diagram of Rydberg atoms in a triangular-prism optical tweezer array using the density matrix renormalization group. Unlike two-leg Rydberg ladders with [MATH] leg-exchange symmetry, the triangular prism possesses [MATH] symmetry, giving rise t…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 175128] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses DMRG to map the ground-state phase diagram of Rydberg atoms in a triangular-prism optical tweezer array, revealing how the prism geometry and symmetry affect many-body phases.
motivation: Rydberg atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum simulation, and understanding the role of lattice geometry in their ground-state phases is important for realizing novel quantum many-body states.
method: The authors model Rydberg atoms in a triangular-prism optical tweezer array and apply the density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) to compute the ground-state phase diagram.
result: They find that the triangular-prism geometry, which possesses a different symmetry than two-leg Rydberg ladders, leads to distinct ground-state phases and phase boundaries.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical characterization of Rydberg many-body phases in a three-dimensional-like prism array, offering guidance for future experiments with optical tweezers.

title: Non-Hermitian Symmetry Breaking And Lee-Yang Theory For Quantum $xyz$ And Clock Models
authors: Tian-Yi Gu And Gaoyong Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Tian-Yi Gu and Gaoyong Sun

Lee-Yang theory offers a unifying framework for understanding classical phase transitions and dynamical quantum phase transitions through the analysis of partition functions and Loschmidt echoes. Recently, this framework was extended to characterize quantum phase transitions of quantum Ising models …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034119] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper extends Lee-Yang theory to characterize non-Hermitian symmetry breaking and quantum phase transitions in quantum XYZ and clock models via partition functions and Loschmidt echoes.
motivation: Lee-Yang theory has recently been applied to quantum phase transitions of Ising-type models, and the authors aim to generalize this framework to more complex non-Hermitian systems such as XYZ and clock models.
method: They analyze partition functions and Loschmidt echoes to identify Lee-Yang zeros and their associated non-Hermitian symmetry-breaking transitions in quantum XYZ and clock models.
result: The framework reveals non-Hermitian symmetry-breaking signatures and transition points in these models, extending the applicability of Lee-Yang theory beyond the Ising case.
conclusion: Lee-Yang theory provides a unifying tool for detecting quantum criticality and symmetry breaking in a broader class of non-Hermitian quantum models.

title: Rydberg States With A Liquid Core
authors: Juan Carlos Acosta Matos, P. Giannakeas, And Jan M. Rost
abstract:
Author(s): Juan Carlos Acosta Matos, P. Giannakeas, and Jan M. Rost

We develop a self-consistent approach that provides an explicit potential for a Rydberg electron whose ionic core consists of a polarizable medium, typically realized with superfluid droplets. The electron’s motion remains separable in spherical coordinates, but the radial force exerted by the dropl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 123402] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: The authors develop a self-consistent theoretical model for a Rydberg electron orbiting an ionic core that consists of a polarizable liquid (superfluid droplet) medium.
motivation: Rydberg states in and on superfluid helium droplets are experimentally accessible yet lack a quantitative theoretical framework that accounts for the polarizable, spatially extended ionic core.
method: They construct an explicit effective potential for the Rydberg electron by self-consistently coupling the electron's separable spherical motion to the dielectric/polarization response of the droplet core, solving the radial problem with the induced force from the medium.
result: The approach yields a modified Rydberg series (energies and wavefunctions) whose level structure and radial distributions depend on the droplet radius and polarizability, differing from ordinary atomic Rydberg spectra.
conclusion: Rydberg states with a liquid core constitute a distinct class of hybrid bound states, providing a tractable potential framework for interpreting and predicting spectroscopy of electron–droplet systems.

title: Observation Of A Topological Phase Transition In Random Coaxial Cable Structures With Chiral Symmetry
authors: D. M. Whittaker, Maxine M. Mccarthy, And Qingqing Duan
abstract:
Author(s): D. M. Whittaker, Maxine M. McCarthy, and Qingqing Duan

We report an experimental study of the disordered Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model, implemented in a system of coaxial cables, whose radio frequency properties map onto the SSH Hamiltonian. By measuring multiple chains with random hopping terms, we demonstrate the presence of a topologically protect…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 144203] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: An experimental realization of the disordered Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model in coaxial cable chains demonstrates a topologically protected phase transition governed by chiral symmetry.
motivation: The SSH model is a canonical platform for studying topological phases, and mapping it onto radio-frequency coaxial cable circuits allows controllable experimental study of disorder effects on chiral-symmetry-protected topology.
method: Multiple coaxial cable chains with randomly chosen hopping terms were fabricated so that their RF transmission properties map onto the SSH Hamiltonian, and their topological phase behavior was probed via impedance/transmission measurements.
result: A topological phase transition persists in the presence of disorder, with chiral symmetry protecting the topological phase and edge-state signatures observed in the random-hopping structures.
conclusion: The work establishes disordered coaxial cable networks as a versatile classical testbed for topological phase transitions, confirming robustness of chiral-symmetry-protected topology against random couplings.

title: Strain-Tunable Anomalous Hall Effect In Hexagonal MnTe
authors: Zhaoyu Liu, Sijie Xu, Jonathan M. Destefano, Elliott Rosenberg, Tingjun Zhang, Jinyulin Li, Matthew B. Stone, Feng Ye, Wei Tian, Sarah Edwards, Rong Cong, Siyu Pan, Ching-Wu Chu, Liangzi Deng, Emilia Morosan, Rafael M. Fernandes, Jiun-Haw Chu, And Pengcheng Dai
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyu Liu, Sijie Xu, Jonathan M. DeStefano, Elliott Rosenberg, Tingjun Zhang, Jinyulin Li, Matthew B. Stone, Feng Ye, Wei Tian, Sarah Edwards, Rong Cong, Siyu Pan, Ching-Wu Chu, Liangzi Deng, Emilia Morosan, Rafael M. Fernandes, Jiun-Haw Chu, and Pengcheng Dai

Uniaxial strain applied to the hexagonal altermagnet
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031033] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: Uniaxial strain on hexagonal altermagnet MnTe isolates a single magnetic domain, producing a sharp anomalous Hall effect whose sign can be reversed via strain-induced modifications to the electronic Berry curvature.
motivation: Altermagnets host momentum-dependent spin splitting that is promising for spintronics, but multi-domain configurations obscure their transport signatures, motivating domain control to expose intrinsic Berry-curvature effects.
method: Single crystals of hexagonal MnTe were subjected to uniaxial strain to select a single magnetic domain, and the anomalous Hall response was measured (with neutron scattering and thermodynamic characterization) to probe the electronic Berry curvature.
result: Strain yields a sharp anomalous Hall signal that reverses sign as the strain is tuned, indicating strain control over the Berry curvature contribution to the Hall response.
conclusion: The work establishes strain as a knob for manipulating Berry-curvature-driven transport in altermagnets, offering a route toward tunable spintronic functionality in MnTe.

title: Nonlinear Layer Hall Effect And Detection Of The Hidden Berry Curvature Dipole In $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric Antiferromagnetic Insulators
authors: Zhuo-Hua Chen, Hou-Jian Duan, Cong Xiao, Ji-Jun Zhao, Ming-Xun Deng, And Rui-Qiang Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhuo-Hua Chen, Hou-Jian Duan, Cong Xiao, Ji-Jun Zhao, Ming-Xun Deng, and Rui-Qiang Wang

Recent experimental and theoretical studies have revealed the emergence of a linear layer Hall effect (LHE) induced by hidden Berry curvature in [MATH] thin films. This phenomenon underscores the layer degree of freedom as a mechanism for generating Hall transport in …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L171110] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper predicts a nonlinear layer Hall effect driven by a hidden Berry curvature dipole in PT-symmetric antiferromagnetic insulator thin films.
motivation: Recent work revealed a linear layer Hall effect from hidden Berry curvature in antiferromagnetic thin films, motivating a search for higher-order (nonlinear) layer-resolved Hall responses as a probe of layer degrees of freedom.
method: Symmetry analysis and model/band-structure calculations (likely tight-binding or effective low-energy models) are used to identify the Berry curvature dipole and the resulting nonlinear layer Hall conductivity in PT-symmetric antiferromagnetic insulators.
result: The authors show that a nonlinear layer Hall effect arises and provides a detectable signature of the hidden Berry curvature dipole, offering a transport probe of layer-contrasted Berry curvature.
conclusion: Nonlinear layer Hall transport is proposed as a viable means to detect hidden Berry curvature dipoles in PT-symmetric antiferromagnetic insulators, extending layer-Hall physics beyond the linear regime.

title: Exact Nematic And Mixed Magnetic Phases Driven By Competing Orders On The Pyrochlore Lattice
authors: Niccolò Francini, Lukas Schmidt, Lukas Janssen, And Daniel Lozano-Gómez
abstract:
Author(s): Niccolò Francini, Lukas Schmidt, Lukas Janssen, and Daniel Lozano-Gómez

Analysis of a frustrated pyrochlore spin model demonstrates that thermal fluctuations and parameter-dependent symmetries suppress conventional order to stabilize a magnetic nematic phase.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031070] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: A frustrated pyrochlore spin model is studied, showing that thermal fluctuations and parameter-dependent symmetries suppress conventional magnetic order in favor of an exotic nematic phase.
motivation: Frustrated magnets with competing interactions host unconventional phases, and understanding how thermal fluctuations and symmetry constraints select among candidate orders is a central question in condensed-matter physics.
method: The authors analyze a pyrochlore-lattice spin model, likely using classical/statistical mechanics techniques such as Landau theory or Monte Carlo simulations, to map the phase diagram as a function of competing coupling parameters.
result: They find that conventional ordering is suppressed, and a magnetic nematic phase as well as mixed magnetic phases emerge from the interplay of competing orders, tuned by parameter-dependent symmetries and thermal fluctuations.
conclusion: The work establishes the pyrochlore lattice as a platform for stabilizing nematic and mixed magnetic phases, highlighting the role of frustration and fluctuations in generating unconventional order.

title: Tomographic Characterization Of Non-Hermitian Hamiltonians In Reciprocal Space
authors: Francesco Di Colandrea, Fabrizio Pavan, Sarvesh Bansal, Paola Savarese, Grazia Di Bello, Giulio de Filippis, Carmine Antonio Perroni, Donato Farina, And Filippo Cardano
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Di Colandrea, Fabrizio Pavan, Sarvesh Bansal, Paola Savarese, Grazia Di Bello, Giulio De Filippis, Carmine Antonio Perroni, Donato Farina, and Filippo Cardano

Non-Hermitian Hamiltonians enrich quantum physics by extending conventional phase diagrams, enabling novel topological phenomena, and realizing exceptional points with applications in quantum sensing. Here, we present a programmable liquid-crystal-based photonic platform for implementing nonunitary …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 126603] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a programmable liquid-crystal photonic platform to tomographically reconstruct non-Hermitian Hamiltonians in reciprocal (momentum) space, enabling characterization of exceptional points and non-Hermitian topological phenomena.
motivation: Non-Hermitian Hamiltonians extend conventional phase diagrams and realize exceptional points useful for topological phenomena and quantum sensing, but experimentally reconstructing them in reciprocal space remains challenging.
method: A reconfigurable liquid-crystal-based photonic setup is used to implement nonunitary evolution, and a tomographic protocol is applied to fully characterize the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian in reciprocal space.
result: The platform successfully reconstructs non-Hermitian Hamiltonians in momentum space, capturing their spectra and exceptional-point structure.
conclusion: This provides a versatile programmable photonic tool for studying non-Hermitian topology and related sensing applications, though it does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, or network questions.

title: Gauge Anomaly And Visible Dissipation Bounds In Active Matter
authors: Hai Pham-Van
abstract:
Author(s): Hai Pham-Van

We formulate a nonequilibrium gauge theory for active many-body steady states and derive rigorous, data-accessible lower bounds on dissipation. The setting is an overdamped translational sector on an extended one-particle state space, where internal variables may encode orientations, species, or oth…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034123] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a nonequilibrium gauge theory for active many-body steady states and derives data-accessible lower bounds on dissipation.
motivation: Active matter systems continuously dissipate energy to sustain their nonequilibrium steady states, motivating a systematic framework for quantifying dissipation.
method: An overdamped translational gauge theory is formulated on an extended one-particle state space where internal variables (orientations, species) act as gauge degrees of freedom, yielding rigorous dissipation bounds.
result: Visible, experimentally accessible lower bounds on dissipation are derived from the gauge-anomaly structure of active steady states.
conclusion: The gauge-theoretic framework links symmetry anomalies to observable dissipation, providing practical bounds for active matter systems.

title: Topological Flat Bands And Fractional Chern Insulators In Rashba Systems With Tunable Superlattice Potentials
authors: Bokai Liang, Wei Qin, And Zhenyu Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Bokai Liang, Wei Qin, and Zhenyu Zhang

Fractional Chern insulators are interaction-driven topological states that realize the lattice analog of the fractional quantum Hall effect without external magnetic fields. Here we propose a programmable platform for engineering topological flat bands by combining a Zeeman field with a tunable elec…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 126604] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: The authors propose a programmable platform for realizing topological flat bands and fractional Chern insulators by combining a Zeeman field with tunable superlattice potentials in Rashba spin-orbit coupled systems.
motivation: Fractional Chern insulators realize lattice analogs of the fractional quantum Hall effect without external magnetic fields, but engineering robust topological flat bands with appropriate interactions remains a central materials-design challenge.
method: The work combines a Zeeman field with an electrically tunable superlattice potential in a Rashba spin-orbit coupled system, computing band structures, Chern numbers, and flatness ratios to identify parameters supporting interaction-driven topological states.
result: The proposed setup yields topological flat bands with nonzero Chern numbers and tunable bandwidth, with signatures indicating stable fractional Chern insulator phases in the strong-interaction regime.
conclusion: Tunable superlattice engineering in Rashba systems provides a flexible and experimentally realizable route toward programmable fractional Chern insulators and correlated topological phases.

title: Universal Quantum Spatial Search Via Controlled Intermittent Quantum Walks
authors: Guanzhong Li, Jingquan Luo, And Lvzhou Li
abstract:
Author(s): Guanzhong Li, Jingquan Luo, and Lvzhou Li

In this work we propose a quantum-walk model, named controlled intermittent quantum walks (CIQWs), where one performs a continuous quantum walk for a period of time under a certain control signal and then adjusts the control signal and performs a continuous quantum walk for another period of time un…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032440] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces controlled intermittent quantum walks (CIQWs) and applies them to universal quantum spatial search.
motivation: Quantum spatial search is a fundamental algorithmic primitive, and new quantum-walk models may offer broader or more flexible search capabilities.
method: The authors define CIQWs by alternating continuous-time quantum walks under a control signal and adjusting that signal between walk segments, then analyze their use for spatial search.
result: The proposed CIQW model is shown to support universal quantum spatial search, likely achieving efficient search on various graphs.
conclusion: CIQWs provide a generalized quantum-walk framework for spatial search, though the work sits outside the researcher's core interests in quantum information theory, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems.

title: Boundary Time Crystal As A Light Source For Collectively Enhanced Sensing
authors: Malik Jirasek, Igor Lesanovsky, And Albert Cabot
abstract:
Author(s): Malik Jirasek, Igor Lesanovsky, and Albert Cabot

Modern precision measurements, such as interferometry for detecting gravitational waves, rely on the estimation of optical phases encoded in light fields. Here we propose to exploit the collectively enhanced output field of a driven-dissipative many-body quantum system as a light source in order to …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032611] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: Proposes using the collectively enhanced output field of a driven-dissipative boundary time crystal as a light source for improved optical phase sensing.
motivation: Precision measurements such as gravitational-wave interferometry rely on estimating optical phases, and there is a need for light sources with quantum-enhanced properties.
method: The authors analyze a driven-dissipative many-body quantum system exhibiting boundary time crystal behavior and use its collective output field for phase estimation, likely via quantum Fisher information or related metrological tools.
result: The collective emission from the boundary time crystal is expected to provide enhanced sensitivity for optical phase estimation compared to conventional light sources.
conclusion: Boundary time crystals could serve as practical quantum light sources for metrology, though further study is needed to assess feasibility and implementation challenges.

title: Stochastically Perturbed Billiards: Fingerprints Of Chaos And Universality Classes
authors: Roberto Artuso And Matteo Burlo
abstract:
Author(s): Roberto Artuso and Matteo Burlo

Billiards tables—a minimal model for particles moving in a confined region—are known to present different classical (and quantum) features according to their shape, ranging from strongly chaotic to integrable dynamics. Here, we consider the role of a stochastic perturbation of the elastic reflection…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033312] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how stochastic perturbations affect the chaotic and quantum features of billiard systems, identifying fingerprints of chaos and universality classes.
motivation: Billiards serve as minimal models for understanding the transition between integrable and chaotic dynamics, and the role of noise in such systems remains an important open question in nonlinear and quantum dynamics.
method: The authors introduce a stochastic perturbation to the elastic reflection law in classical billiards and analyze its impact on classical and quantum signatures, such as spectral statistics and dynamical indicators.
result: They find that stochastic perturbations leave characteristic fingerprints on the chaotic dynamics and can classify different universality classes of billiard systems.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of noise effects in billiard dynamics but is not directly tied to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Chiral Quantum Transport With Perfect Circulation: From Floquet Engineering To Anyonic Dynamics
authors: Chaorong Guo, Hongzheng Wu, Zenong Zhou, Ai-Xi Chen, And Xiaobing Luo
abstract:
Author(s): Chaorong Guo, Hongzheng Wu, Zenong Zhou, Ai-Xi Chen, and Xiaobing Luo

Perfect chiral circulation, the sequential transfer of a quantum state around a closed loop with unit fidelity, has been achieved in specific few-site systems, yet the universal physical conditions underlying this phenomenon remain unclear. We prove that discrete translational invariance and an equi…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033322] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes universal conditions for perfect chiral circulation in few-site quantum systems and extends the phenomenon from Floquet engineering to anyonic dynamics.
motivation: Perfect chiral circulation—unit-fidelity sequential quantum state transfer around a closed loop—had been observed in specific systems, but the general physical requirements were not understood.
method: The authors theoretically prove conditions based on discrete translational invariance and an equispaced spectral structure, and they analyze their implications for Floquet-engineered systems and anyonic dynamics.
result: They identify universal physical conditions for perfect chiral circulation and demonstrate how these conditions can be realized in Floquet setups and anyonic systems.
conclusion: The work provides a unified framework for chiral quantum transport and connects Floquet engineering with anyonic physics, though it falls outside the four prioritized research directions.

title: Atom- And Spin-resolved Imaging In A Single Shot
authors: Tobias Hammel, Maximilian Kaiser, Daniel Dux, Matthias Weidemüller, And Selim Jochim
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Hammel, Maximilian Kaiser, Daniel Dux, Matthias Weidemüller, and Selim Jochim

We report on an imaging scheme for quantum gases that enables simultaneous detection of two spin states with single-atom resolution. It utilizes the polarization of the emitted photons during fluorescence by choosing appropriate internal states of lithium-6 atoms in a magnetic field. This scheme can…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033320] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: A single-shot imaging scheme for quantum gases that simultaneously detects two spin states with single-atom resolution using polarization of fluorescence photons from lithium-6.
motivation: Single-atom-resolved detection of spin states is crucial for quantum simulation and many-body physics, but simultaneous spin-resolved imaging remains challenging.
method: The authors utilize the polarization of emitted photons during fluorescence by choosing appropriate internal states of lithium-6 atoms in a magnetic field to achieve simultaneous spin-state detection.
result: The scheme achieves single-atom resolution and simultaneous detection of two spin states in a single shot.
conclusion: This technique provides a powerful tool for probing spin correlations and dynamics in quantum gases.

title: Phase-controlled Transport Of Floquet-driven Compact Topological Photonic States
authors: Gabriel Cáceres-Aravena, Paloma Vildoso, Helena Drüeke, And Rodrigo A. Vicencio
abstract:
Author(s): Gabriel Cáceres-Aravena, Paloma Vildoso, Helena Drüeke, and Rodrigo A. Vicencio

The Aharonov-Bohm (AB) effect remains a cornerstone of fundamental and applied physics. In this work, we utilize the AB caging effect originated from an effective magnetic field induced by multiorbital interactions, creating an all flat band (FB) lattice system. Normally, FB states are known for bei…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033515] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies phase-controlled transport of Floquet-driven compact topological photonic states in an all-flat-band lattice arising from Aharonov-Bohm caging.
motivation: The Aharonov-Bohm effect and flat-band systems are of broad interest, and controlling topological photonic transport via phase offers a route to manipulate light in engineered lattices.
method: The authors use an effective magnetic field generated by multiorbital interactions to create an all-flat-band lattice and combine it with Floquet driving to realize compact topological photonic states.
result: They demonstrate phase-controlled transport of these Floquet-driven compact topological photonic states, showing how the AB caging and driving parameters govern the propagation.
conclusion: The work provides a photonic platform for phase-controlled topological transport, with potential applications in reconfigurable photonic devices and topological light manipulation.

title: Enhanced Density Fluctuations Near A Disordered Chiral Topological Transition
authors: Hai-Tao Ding, Sen Mu, Leong-Chuan Kwek, Gabriel Lemarié, And Jiangbin Gong
abstract:
Author(s): Hai-Tao Ding, Sen Mu, Leong-Chuan Kwek, Gabriel Lemarié, and Jiangbin Gong

The universal statistics of density fluctuations of localized quantum states may offer unprecedented opportunities to probe and understand quantum transport in connection with dimensionality, coherence, symmetry, and disorder. To date, the possible role of topological phase transitions in the fluctu…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 134204] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates enhanced density fluctuations of localized quantum states near a disordered chiral topological transition, connecting fluctuation statistics to quantum transport and topology.
motivation: Understanding how topological phase transitions influence universal density fluctuations of localized states and quantum transport in disordered systems remains an open question.
method: The authors analyze density fluctuations in a disordered chiral topological model, using statistical measures and scaling analysis across the topological transition.
result: They find enhanced density fluctuations near the transition, revealing universal statistics tied to dimensionality, coherence, symmetry, and disorder.
conclusion: Density fluctuations may serve as a sensitive probe of topological transitions and quantum transport in disordered quantum systems.

title: Hall Viscosity Of The Laughlin State On Noisy Quantum Computers
authors: Ammar Kirmani, Andrew A. Allocca, Jian-Xin Zhu, Armin Rahmani, Sriram Ganeshan, And Pouyan Ghaemi
abstract:
Author(s): Ammar Kirmani, Andrew A. Allocca, Jian-Xin Zhu, Armin Rahmani, Sriram Ganeshan, and Pouyan Ghaemi

Hall viscosity is a quantized nondissipative stress response of a fractional quantum Hall (FQH) fluid to adiabatic geometric deformations. Despite strong theoretical interest, its experimental observation in the FQH state has remained elusive, making it a demanding target for realization on current …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 185121] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper computes the Hall viscosity of the Laughlin fractional quantum Hall state on noisy quantum computers, aiming to realize a quantized geometric response that is experimentally elusive.
motivation: Hall viscosity is a quantized nondissipative stress response of fractional quantum Hall fluids, but its direct experimental observation remains challenging, motivating its simulation on current quantum hardware.
method: The authors implement the Laughlin state on noisy quantum computers and extract the Hall viscosity through adiabatic geometric deformations, likely using error mitigation or variational techniques.
result: They obtain estimates of the Hall viscosity from the noisy quantum simulation, demonstrating the feasibility of probing this topological response on near-term devices.
conclusion: The work provides a proof-of-principle for using noisy quantum computers to study geometric and topological properties of fractional quantum Hall states, though it remains a specialized condensed-matter simulation.

title: Digital-analog Concept For Superconducting Perceptron-like Neural Networks
authors: Andrey E. Schegolev, Vsevolod I. Ruzhickiy, Georgy I. Gubochkin, Alexander S. Ionin, Ivan A. Nazhestkin, Mikhail Y. Fominskii, Lyudmila V. Filippenko, Igor I. Soloviev, Maxim V. Tereshonok, And Nikolay V. Klenov
abstract:
Author(s): Andrey E. Schegolev, Vsevolod I. Ruzhickiy, Georgy I. Gubochkin, Alexander S. Ionin, Ivan A. Nazhestkin, Mikhail Y. Fominskii, Lyudmila V. Filippenko, Igor I. Soloviev, Maxim V. Tereshonok, and Nikolay V. Klenov

A promising route to superconducting artificial neural networks is a hybrid digital-analog architecture that combines digital single-flux-quantum (SFQ) communication with compact analog nonlinear processing. The study focused on the dynamic conversion of a discrete signal passing through a digital-t…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035306] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a hybrid digital-analog architecture for superconducting perceptron-like neural networks that combines digital single-flux-quantum (SFQ) communication with compact analog nonlinear processing.
motivation: Superconducting artificial neural networks could offer ultra-fast, low-power computation, motivating architectures that efficiently move signals between digital and analog domains.
method: The authors study the dynamic conversion of discrete SFQ pulses into analog signals and back, analyzing the nonlinear processing elements used to realize perceptron-like neuron behavior in superconducting circuits.
result: They characterize the digital-to-analog and analog-to-digital conversion dynamics and demonstrate a viable scheme for compact superconducting perceptron-like units.
conclusion: The digital-analog hybrid approach offers a promising route toward scalable superconducting neural networks, though its relevance lies in classical neuromorphic superconducting electronics rather than quantum information processing.

title: Neural-network Quantum States For Solving Few-body Problems: Application To Efimov Physics
authors: Sora Yokoi, Shimpei Endo, And Hiroki Saito
abstract:
Author(s): Sora Yokoi, Shimpei Endo, and Hiroki Saito

Neural-network quantum states have been developed as an efficient method for solving quantum many-body problems, not only in lattice systems but also in systems of particles in continuous space. Here, we apply this approach to strongly interacting few-body problems in continuous space at unitarity: …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033335] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper applies neural-network quantum states to strongly interacting few-body systems in continuous space, focusing on Efimov physics at unitarity.
motivation: Neural-network quantum states have proven effective for many-body problems, and the authors aim to extend them to strongly interacting few-body continuous-space systems where Efimov effects appear.
method: The authors use neural-network quantum states as a variational ansatz to solve few-body Schrödinger equations in continuous space at unitarity.
result: The approach is demonstrated on few-body problems in the unitary regime, targeting Efimov physics, though the abstract is truncated and specific numerical findings are not fully detailed.
conclusion: Neural-network quantum states can be adapted to study strongly interacting few-body continuous systems and Efimov phenomena.

title: Symmetries Of Anisotropic Spin Interaction Models
authors: Arist Zhenyuan Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Arist Zhenyuan Yang

We show that anisotropic spin interactions do not merely break spin-space group (SSG) symmetries, but instead twist them through cohomology invariants, yielding symmetry classes beyond subgroups of [MATH]. This requires redefining the spin-only group ${}_{0…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033327] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that anisotropic spin interactions twist spin-space group symmetries via cohomology invariants, producing symmetry classes beyond ordinary subgroups.
motivation: Anisotropic spin interactions are typically assumed to simply break spin-space group symmetries, but the author argues this picture is incomplete and misses nontrivial cohomological structure.
method: A group-theoretic and cohomological framework is developed, redefining the spin-only group and classifying the resulting 'twisted' symmetry classes of anisotropic spin Hamiltonians.
result: Anisotropic spin interactions generate symmetry classes that are not subgroups of the conventional spin-space group, characterized by cohomology invariants acting as twists.
conclusion: The classification extends standard symmetry analysis of magnetic models, with implications for understanding ordering and degeneracies in anisotropic spin systems.

title: Diffuse Laser Cooling Based On The $6{\mathrm{P}}_{3/2}$ Excited State Of Rubidium Atoms Via 420 Nm Blue Light
authors: Jia Zhang, Xun Gao, Zheng Xiao, Xiaolei Guan, Ruihang Chen, Mengyuan Han, Tiantian Shi, And Jingbiao Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Jia Zhang, Xun Gao, Zheng Xiao, Xiaolei Guan, Ruihang Chen, Mengyuan Han, Tiantian Shi, and Jingbiao Chen

To date, the laser cooling of rubidium atoms has inevitably relied on 780 nm cooling light corresponding to the first excited state [MATH]. Here, we demonstrate diffuse laser cooling of [MATH] atoms using the 420 nm [MATH] transition with…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033293] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates diffuse laser cooling of rubidium atoms using the 420 nm transition associated with the 6P3/2 excited state, instead of the conventional 780 nm cooling light.
motivation: Laser cooling of rubidium atoms has conventionally relied on the 780 nm transition to the first excited state, limiting available cooling wavelengths and schemes.
method: The authors perform diffuse laser cooling on rubidium atoms via the 420 nm blue-light transition involving the 6P3/2 excited state.
result: Cooling of rubidium atoms is achieved using the 420 nm transition, expanding the range of laser cooling wavelengths for rubidium.
conclusion: The work shows the feasibility of blue-light diffuse laser cooling in rubidium atoms, which may enable new atomic physics experiments and cooling protocols.

title: Quantum Simulation Of Electronic Structure Via Quantum Fast Multipole Method
authors: Dominic W. Berry, Kianna Wan, Andrew D. Baczewski, Elliot C. Eklund, Arkin Tikku, And Ryan Babbush
abstract:
Author(s): Dominic W. Berry, Kianna Wan, Andrew D. Baczewski, Elliot C. Eklund, Arkin Tikku, and Ryan Babbush

An algorithm for fast summation of the Coulomb potential enables quantum simulation of electronic structure with the lowest known asymptotic complexity in particle number.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033025] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a quantum fast multipole method for summing Coulomb potentials, achieving the lowest known asymptotic complexity for quantum simulation of electronic structure in particle number.
motivation: Simulating electronic structure quantumly requires efficient treatment of long-range Coulomb interactions, whose naive summation scales poorly with particle number and dominates the cost of quantum chemistry algorithms.
method: The authors develop a quantum analogue of the classical fast multipole method that hierarchically approximates and sums Coulomb potentials, and integrate it into a quantum algorithm for electronic structure simulation.
result: The resulting algorithm attains the best known asymptotic scaling in particle number for quantum simulation of electronic structure, improving on prior approaches.
conclusion: Quantum fast multipole summation provides a route to more efficient quantum chemistry simulation, though the work is algorithmic and applied rather than addressing information-theoretic or thermodynamic questions.

title: Ultrafast Demagnetization Governed By Spin Fluctuations In ${\mathrm{CaRuO}}_{3}/{\mathrm{SrTiO}}_{3}$ Superlattice
authors: Yu-Han Gao, Wen-Xiao Shi, Yuan-Sha Chen, Ji-Rong Sun, Qing-Lin Yang, Xu Yang, Zhuo Deng, Peng-Tao Yang, Zheng Chang, Hong-Mei Feng, Wei He, Xiang-Qun Zhang, And Zhao-Hua Cheng
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Han Gao, Wen-Xiao Shi, Yuan-Sha Chen, Ji-Rong Sun, Qing-Lin Yang, Xu Yang, Zhuo Deng, Peng-Tao Yang, Zheng Chang, Hong-Mei Feng, Wei He, Xiang-Qun Zhang, and Zhao-Hua Cheng

Contrary to expectations, the magnetization dynamics of a ferromagnet can be accelerated by increasing temperature, laser excitation, or magnetic field—a behavior that holds promise for high-speed spintronics.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 126903] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: Ultrafast demagnetization in CaRuO3/SrTiO3 superlattices is governed by spin fluctuations, revealing an unusual temperature- and field-enhanced magnetization dynamics.
motivation: The magnetization dynamics of ferromagnets can be accelerated by increasing temperature, laser excitation, or magnetic field, contrary to typical expectations, which may enable high-speed spintronics.
method: The authors investigate the ultrafast magnetization dynamics of CaRuO3/SrTiO3 superlattices, likely using time-resolved magneto-optical Kerr effect or similar pump-probe techniques.
result: Spin fluctuations are identified as the governing mechanism behind the observed acceleration of demagnetization with increasing temperature, laser fluence, and magnetic field.
conclusion: The findings establish spin fluctuations as a key driver of ultrafast demagnetization in oxide superlattices, with implications for high-speed spintronic devices.

title: Non-Hermitian Topological Beam Splitting And Beam Encoding
authors: Tian Tian, Shizhen Wang, Yingnan Yan, Tianhan Zhong, Xiaojun Jia, And Heng Shen
abstract:
Author(s): Tian Tian, Shizhen Wang, Yingnan Yan, Tianhan Zhong, Xiaojun Jia, and Heng Shen

Non-Hermitian physics has attracted significant interest due to its exotic phenomena. However, non-Hermitian effects at topological interfaces and their potential applications remain largely unexplored. Here, based on an interface skin-effect model, we theoretically propose a non-Hermitian topologic…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 120601] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically proposes non-Hermitian topological interface effects based on an interface skin-effect model and applies them to beam splitting and beam encoding.
motivation: Non-Hermitian physics exhibits exotic phenomena, but non-Hermitian effects at topological interfaces and their practical applications remain largely unexplored.
method: The authors construct an interface skin-effect model to theoretically analyze non-Hermitian topological interfaces and design beam-splitting/beam-encoding functionality.
result: They demonstrate non-Hermitian topological beam splitting and beam encoding enabled by the interface skin effect.
