conclusion: The work extends non-Hermitian topological phenomena to interface-based photonic functionalities, suggesting applications in beam manipulation and encoding.

title: Quantum-Geometry-Driven Exact Ferromagnetic Ground State In A Nearly Flat Band
authors: Taisei Kitamura, Hiroki Nakai, Hosho Katsura, And Ryotaro Arita
abstract:
Author(s): Taisei Kitamura, Hiroki Nakai, Hosho Katsura, and Ryotaro Arita

We construct a Hubbard model with a nearly flat band whose quantum geometry can be tuned independent of the energy dispersion and the Coulomb interaction. We show that, when the nearly flat band is half filled, the exact ground state of the model exhibits ferromagnetism and that this ferromagnetism …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 126502] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper constructs a Hubbard model with a nearly flat band and shows an exact ferromagnetic ground state at half filling, driven by quantum geometry.
motivation: Flat-band ferromagnetism is a longstanding theme in condensed matter, and quantum geometry has recently emerged as a key ingredient in flat-band physics.
method: They design a Hubbard model whose quantum geometry can be tuned independently of the band dispersion and Coulomb interaction, then analyze its half-filled ground state.
result: The exact ground state of the model exhibits ferromagnetism, demonstrating that quantum geometry alone can drive ferromagnetic order in a nearly flat band.
conclusion: Quantum geometry provides a controllable route to exact ferromagnetic ground states in flat-band systems, with implications for correlated electron physics.

title: Giant And Helical Exciton Dipole From Berry Curvature In Flat Chern Bands
authors: Kaijie Yang, Huiyuan Zheng, Xiaodong Xu, Di Xiao, And Ting Cao
abstract:
Author(s): Kaijie Yang, Huiyuan Zheng, Xiaodong Xu, Di Xiao, and Ting Cao

Berry curvature in twisted molybdenum ditelluride drives the oppositely charged particles in an exciton in opposite transverse directions, producing a dipole moment of approximately 150 Debye.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 126602] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: Berry curvature in flat Chern bands of twisted molybdenum ditelluride generates a giant helical exciton dipole of approximately 150 Debye.
motivation: The paper aims to understand how nontrivial band geometry in moiré flat Chern bands affects exciton properties, particularly the spatial separation of electrons and holes.
method: The authors analyze exciton states in twisted MoTe2 where Berry curvature drives oppositely charged particles in opposite transverse directions, likely using theoretical modeling or first-principles calculations.
result: They find that the Berry curvature induces a large dipole moment of about 150 Debye with helical character in the exciton.
conclusion: Berry curvature can produce giant exciton dipoles in flat Chern bands, suggesting new opportunities for moiré exciton physics and optoelectronic applications.

title: Non-Abelian Route To ${z}_{2}$ Non-Hermitian Skin Effects
authors: Huiyan Tang, Yaxuan Zhang, Ziteng Wang, Liqin Tang, Daohong Song, Jingjun Xu, Weixuan Zhang, Hrvoje Buljan, Xiangdong Zhang, And Zhigang Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Huiyan Tang, Yaxuan Zhang, Ziteng Wang, Liqin Tang, Daohong Song, Jingjun Xu, Weixuan Zhang, Hrvoje Buljan, Xiangdong Zhang, and Zhigang Chen

The non-Hermitian skin effect (NHSE), characterized by extensive boundary accumulation of eigenstates under open boundary conditions, has emerged as a central phenomenon in non-Hermitian physics. Established routes to the NHSE are usually based on Abelian nonreciprocal mechanisms, including an equiv…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 126605] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a non-Abelian mechanism for realizing Z2 non-Hermitian skin effects, extending the conventional Abelian nonreciprocal routes.
motivation: The non-Hermitian skin effect is a central phenomenon in non-Hermitian physics, but established routes to it rely on Abelian nonreciprocal mechanisms, motivating a search for non-Abelian generalizations.
method: The authors construct a theoretical framework using non-Abelian nonreciprocal couplings or gauge structures to generate Z2 non-Hermitian skin effects, likely in a lattice model.
result: They demonstrate that a non-Abelian route can produce Z2 non-Hermitian skin effects, characterized by boundary accumulation of eigenstates under open boundary conditions.
conclusion: The work broadens the understanding of non-Hermitian skin effects beyond Abelian paradigms, opening new directions in non-Hermitian topology.

title: Orbit-Resolved Imaging Of Paired Resonances In A Wave-Chaotic Microcavity
authors: Ruo-Kai Zheng, Qi-Tao Cao, Qihuang Gong, And Yun-Feng Xiao
abstract:
Author(s): Ruo-Kai Zheng, Qi-Tao Cao, Qihuang Gong, and Yun-Feng Xiao

Orbit-resolved paired resonances, sharing the same orbital period but arising from distinct phase-space structures, provide a direct probe of wave localization in chaotic microcavities. Here, we report the orbit-resolved visualization of paired resonances in a chaotic optical microcavity using a mul…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 123801] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports orbit-resolved imaging of paired resonances in a wave-chaotic optical microcavity, revealing distinct phase-space structures with the same orbital period.
motivation: Understanding wave localization in chaotic microcavities can probe the correspondence between ray dynamics and wave phenomena, with potential implications for optical mode control.
method: The authors use a multimode optical microcavity and an imaging technique to spatially resolve resonances associated with specific periodic orbits in phase space.
result: They experimentally visualize paired resonances that share the same orbital period but originate from different phase-space structures, demonstrating orbit-resolved mode identification.
conclusion: The work provides a direct probe of wave localization in chaotic cavities and may inform the design of microcavity-based photonic devices.

title: Analog Quantum Simulation Of Chiral Magnetic Dynamics Using Optical Superlattices
authors: Sabhyata Gupta And Luis Santos
abstract:
Author(s): Sabhyata Gupta and Luis Santos

We propose an analog quantum simulation of chiral magnetic dynamics using ultracold atoms in an optical superlattice. The massive Schwinger model in the zero gauge coupling limit maps onto the Rice-Mele model, with the fermion mass and topological angle encoded in the superlattice parameters. We stu…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033321] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: Proposes an analog quantum simulation of chiral magnetic dynamics using ultracold atoms in an optical superlattice, mapping the massive Schwinger model to the Rice-Mele model.
motivation: To simulate lattice gauge theories and topological phenomena that are challenging to study in high-energy physics experiments.
method: Ultracold atoms in a one-dimensional optical superlattice, with fermion mass and topological angle encoded in superlattice parameters; the dynamics are studied via time evolution.
result: The mapping enables the observation of chiral magnetic dynamics and topological effects accessible through time-resolved measurements.
conclusion: Optical superlattices provide a tunable platform for analog quantum simulation of chiral magnetic phenomena, bridging cold-atom and high-energy physics.

title: Unified Quantum Walk Model For Internal Crystal Effects In Dynamical Diffraction
authors: Owen Lailey, Dusan Sarenac, David G. Cory, Michael G. Huber, And Dmitry A. Pushin
abstract:
Author(s): Owen Lailey, Dusan Sarenac, David G. Cory, Michael G. Huber, and Dmitry A. Pushin

The theory of dynamical diffraction (DD) in perfect crystals is the backbone of high-precision neutron and x-ray diffraction experiments, enabling accurate determination of crystal-structure factors and the realization of perfect-crystal interferometers. In practice, however, real crystals exhibit d…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032210] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a unified quantum walk model to account for internal crystal effects in dynamical diffraction for neutron and x-ray interferometry.
motivation: Dynamical diffraction theory is central to high-precision neutron and x-ray experiments, but real crystals exhibit internal imperfections that complicate data interpretation.
method: The authors formulate a quantum walk framework to model internal crystal effects in dynamical diffraction, mapping the diffraction process onto a discrete-time quantum walk.
result: The model unifies and explains internal crystal effects observed in dynamical diffraction experiments.
conclusion: This approach may improve accuracy in crystal-structure factor determination and perfect-crystal interferometry.

title: Quantum Metric Senses A Persistent Spin Helix
authors: Awadhesh Narayan
abstract:
Author(s): Awadhesh Narayan

Persistent spin helices are a manifestation of symmetry-protected spin textures in systems with balanced spin-orbit coupling. They enable long-lived spin structures that are of interest for spintronics and coherent spin manipulation. The quantum metric has recently emerged as a promising tool for ch…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L171405] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that the quantum metric can identify and characterize persistent spin helices arising from balanced spin-orbit coupling.
motivation: Persistent spin helices are symmetry-protected spin textures that enable long-lived spin structures for spintronics and coherent spin manipulation, and the quantum metric has emerged as a useful probe of quantum geometry.
method: The work theoretically analyzes how the quantum metric encodes the persistent spin helix texture in systems with balanced spin-orbit coupling, likely using quantum-geometric and symmetry-based arguments.
result: The quantum metric is found to provide a geometric signature of the persistent spin helix, linking quantum geometry to symmetry-protected spin textures.
conclusion: Quantum geometry, via the quantum metric, can serve as a diagnostic for persistent spin helices, with potential implications for spintronic and coherent spin-manipulation applications.

title: Nonequilibrium Angular Momentum Selectivity And Filtering In Chiral Carbon Nanotubes
authors: Sergio Shmayev, D. R. Da Costa, And D. A. Bahamon
abstract:
Author(s): Sergio Shmayev, D. R. da Costa, and D. A. Bahamon

Carbon nanotubes (CNTs) constitute a highly tunable platform for probing the interplay between structural chirality and quantum transport in quasi-one-dimensional systems. Here, we perform a systematic study of the nonequilibrium orbital response across a broad set of metallic and semiconducting chi…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 165416] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper systematically studies nonequilibrium orbital response and angular momentum selectivity/filtering in chiral carbon nanotubes across metallic and semiconducting species.
motivation: Chiral carbon nanotubes provide a highly tunable quasi-one-dimensional platform for exploring the interplay between structural chirality and quantum transport.
method: The authors perform a theoretical/computational study of nonequilibrium orbital response for a broad set of chiral carbon nanotubes, considering both metallic and semiconducting cases.
result: They find chirality-dependent angular momentum selectivity and filtering effects in the nonequilibrium orbital transport properties.
conclusion: The results highlight chiral carbon nanotubes as promising systems for orbital angular momentum filtering and chirality-controlled quantum transport, though the work is primarily condensed-matter transport rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Jittery Quantum Boomerang Effect
authors: Pedro Dornelas And Gerson J. Ferreira
abstract:
Author(s): Pedro Dornelas and Gerson J. Ferreira

We study the dynamics of a spin-polarized wave packet in a disordered Rashba two-dimensional (2D) electron gas and identify a jittery quantum boomerang effect in which longitudinal and transverse motion return to the origin through fundamentally distinct mechanisms. Starting from an initial state wi…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L140203] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper identifies a jittery quantum boomerang effect in a spin-polarized wave packet propagating in a disordered Rashba 2D electron gas, with longitudinal and transverse returns to the origin governed by distinct mechanisms.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how disorder and Rashba spin-orbit coupling affect the quantum boomerang effect, a phenomenon where wave packets partially return to their starting point due to quantum interference.
method: They study the dynamics of a spin-polarized wave packet in a disordered Rashba two-dimensional electron gas, likely using numerical simulations and analytical modeling of the time evolution.
result: They find a jittery quantum boomerang effect in which the longitudinal and transverse components of the wave packet return to the origin through fundamentally different mechanisms.
conclusion: The work reveals the rich interplay between spin-orbit coupling, disorder, and quantum interference in wave packet dynamics, extending the quantum boomerang effect to spin-dependent 2D systems.

title: Polar Chiral Active Matter As A Motile, Disordered Josephson Array: Information Supercurrents And Goldstone Spin Waves
authors: Magnus F Ivarsen
abstract:
Author(s): Magnus F Ivarsen

We consider a minimalist model of polar chiral active matter: overdamped, self-propelled agents coupled through a localized Kuramoto-Sakaguchi interaction, which causes alignment. Intrinsic frustration drawn from a broad distribution constitutes a temperature for the ensemble. In the comoving frame …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035417] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: A minimal model of polar chiral active matter is mapped to a disordered Josephson array, exhibiting information supercurrents and Goldstone spin waves.
motivation: To describe collective behavior in active matter with alignment interactions and intrinsic frustration by analogy with superconducting Josephson junction arrays.
method: Overdamped self-propelled agents with Kuramoto-Sakaguchi alignment and a broad distribution of intrinsic frustration, interpreted as a temperature, are analyzed in the comoving frame.
result: The model produces emergent information supercurrents and Goldstone spin-wave modes, linking active matter to Josephson array physics.
conclusion: The work provides a novel analogy for chiral active matter but does not address quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Diffusion With Conserved Marginal Distributions And Information Theory In Fracton Hydrodynamics
authors: Vaibhav Mohanty And Sunghan Ro
abstract:
Author(s): Vaibhav Mohanty and Sunghan Ro

Diffusion with multipole-moment conservation gives rise to transport laws that generalize Fick's law and has attracted growing attention following experimental advances in strongly tilted optical lattices. It was recently shown that conserving complete multipole-moment groups leads to subdiffusive d…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034129] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies diffusion with conserved marginal distributions and applies information theory to fracton hydrodynamics, showing subdiffusive transport from multipole-moment conservation.
motivation: Recent experiments in strongly tilted optical lattices have renewed interest in transport laws beyond Fick's law, particularly in systems with multipole-moment conservation.
method: The authors develop a hydrodynamic framework for diffusion with conserved marginal distributions and use information-theoretic analysis to characterize the resulting dynamics.
result: They find that conserving complete multipole-moment groups leads to subdiffusive behavior and generalized transport laws.
conclusion: The work connects information theory with fracton hydrodynamics, offering insights into anomalous diffusion in constrained many-body systems.

title: Stationary Densities In A Weakly Nonconserving Asymmetric Exclusion Process With Finite Resources
authors: Sourav Pal And Abhik Basu
abstract:
Author(s): Sourav Pal and Abhik Basu

Inspired by the phenomenologies of an open totally asymmetric simple exclusion process (TASEP) with Langmuir kinetics (Lk) and finite resources that dynamically control the entry and exit rates of the TASEP lane, we study the stationary densities and phase transitions in a TASEP with Lk connected to…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034121] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies stationary densities and phase transitions in a classical TASEP with Langmuir kinetics and finite resources.
motivation: Motivated by open TASEP with Langmuir kinetics and finite resources that dynamically control the entry and exit rates of the transport lane.
method: Analyzes a weakly nonconserving asymmetric exclusion process with finite resources to determine stationary density profiles and phase transitions.
result: Derives stationary densities and identifies phase transitions in the model.
conclusion: Provides insights into nonequilibrium classical transport with finite resources, but is not directly relevant to quantum information or information thermodynamics.

title: Gauge-invariant Quantum Minimally Entangled Typical Thermal States Algorithm With Mutually Unbiased Physical Bases For ${\mathbb{Z}}_{2}$ Lattice Gauge Theories At Finite Temperature And Density
authors: Reita Maeno
abstract:
Author(s): Reita Maeno

In quantum computations of gauge theories at finite temperature and finite density, enforcing Gauss's law for all states contributing to the thermal ensemble is a nontrivial challenge. In this work, we adapt the quantum minimally entangled typical thermal states (QMETTS) algorithm to ${}_{…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033306] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper adapts the quantum minimally entangled typical thermal states (QMETTS) algorithm for gauge-invariant quantum simulation of Z2 lattice gauge theories at finite temperature and density.
motivation: Enforcing Gauss's law in thermal ensembles for quantum computations of gauge theories at finite temperature and density is a nontrivial challenge.
method: The authors extend QMETTS with mutually unbiased physical bases to maintain gauge invariance in the thermal state preparation for Z2 lattice gauge theories.
result: The proposed algorithm enables gauge-invariant quantum computations of thermal properties for Z2 lattice gauge theories at finite temperature and density.
conclusion: This work provides a viable quantum algorithm for simulating lattice gauge theories in regimes relevant to high-energy and nuclear physics.

title: Anomalous Wave-packet Dynamics In One-dimensional non-Hermitian Lattices
authors: Yanyan He And Tomoki Ozawa
abstract:
Author(s): Yanyan He and Tomoki Ozawa

In a disorder-free non-Hermitian lattice with an entirely real spectrum and without any external force, a moving wave packet can exhibit sudden jumps or oscillations. Near a boundary, a wave packet can reflect with delay or advance in time, which is the temporal analogue of the Goos-Hänchen shift.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032044] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies anomalous wave-packet dynamics in disorder-free one-dimensional non-Hermitian lattices with real spectra, including sudden jumps and temporal Goos-Hänchen shifts at boundaries.
motivation: Non-Hermitian lattices with real spectra can exhibit unusual transport without external forces, motivating a detailed investigation of wave-packet propagation and boundary reflection.
method: The authors analyze wave-packet dynamics in one-dimensional non-Hermitian lattice models with entirely real spectra, focusing on center-of-mass motion and reflection behavior at boundaries.
result: Moving wave packets can display sudden jumps or oscillations, and near a boundary they can reflect with a time delay or advance analogous to the Goos-Hänchen shift.
conclusion: Non-Hermitian lattices can host anomalous wave-packet phenomena even in the absence of disorder or external force, broadening the understanding of non-Hermitian transport.

title: Scalable Quantum Algorithm For Meson Scattering In A Lattice Gauge Theory
authors: Yahui Chai, Yibin Guo, And Stefan Kühn
abstract:
Author(s): Yahui Chai, Yibin Guo, and Stefan Kühn

Scattering processes are essential for understanding the structure of matter, yet their real-time dynamics remain challenging to simulate classically. Quantum computers offer a promising path toward efficient simulation of such physical systems. Here, we present a general and scalable framework for …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033298] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a scalable quantum algorithm for simulating meson scattering in a lattice gauge theory.
motivation: Real-time scattering dynamics in lattice gauge theories are classically intractable, motivating quantum simulation approaches.
method: The authors develop a general and scalable quantum algorithm framework to simulate meson scattering processes in a lattice gauge theory.
result: The framework enables efficient quantum simulation of meson scattering, potentially overcoming classical limitations.
conclusion: This work advances quantum algorithms for high-energy physics simulations but is not directly related to the researcher's quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems interests.

title: Hong-Ou-Mandel Two-photon X-ray States
authors: Liam T. Powers And Stephen M. Durbin
abstract:
Author(s): Liam T. Powers and Stephen M. Durbin

Hong-Ou-Mandel interference has now been observed with pairs of indistinguishable x-rays from a high-brightness synchrotron source, using a thin silicon crystal beam splitter.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032042] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: Researchers observed Hong-Ou-Mandel interference between indistinguishable X-ray photon pairs using a thin silicon crystal beam splitter.
motivation: Hong-Ou-Mandel interference is a fundamental quantum optics phenomenon that had not been demonstrated at X-ray wavelengths; extending it could enable new quantum-enhanced X-ray techniques.
method: A high-brightness synchrotron source generated X-ray photon pairs, and a thin silicon crystal served as the beam splitter to measure two-photon interference.
result: They observed Hong-Ou-Mandel interference, demonstrating two-photon X-ray states and quantum interference at X-ray energies.
conclusion: This opens possibilities for X-ray quantum optics and metrology, but is not directly aligned with the researcher's interests in quantum information theory, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Quantum-informed Reduction Algorithm For The Maximum Independent Set Problem
authors: Martin J. A. Schuetz, Romina Yalovetzky, Ruben S. Andrist, Grant Salton, Yue Sun, Rudy Raymond, Shouvanik Chakrabarti, Atithi Acharya, Ruslan Shaydulin, Marco Pistoia, And Helmut G. Katzgraber
abstract:
Author(s): Martin J. A. Schuetz, Romina Yalovetzky, Ruben S. Andrist, Grant Salton, Yue Sun, Rudy Raymond, Shouvanik Chakrabarti, Atithi Acharya, Ruslan Shaydulin, Marco Pistoia, and Helmut G. Katzgraber

We propose and implement a quantum-informed reduction algorithm for the maximum independent set problem that integrates classical kernelization techniques with information extracted from quantum devices. Our larger framework consists of dedicated application, algorithm, and hardware layers, and easi…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033296] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a quantum-informed reduction algorithm for the maximum independent set problem that combines classical kernelization with information extracted from quantum devices.
motivation: To leverage quantum devices for reducing the size of combinatorial optimization problems before classical solving, potentially improving performance on maximum independent set instances.
method: The approach integrates classical kernelization techniques with information obtained from quantum hardware, organized into application, algorithm, and hardware layers.
result: The authors implement and demonstrate the framework, showing that quantum-derived information can guide reductions, though specific performance improvements are not detailed in the abstract.
conclusion: Quantum-informed reductions may serve as a useful preprocessing step for maximum independent set and related graph problems, but the work remains largely applied and outside the scope of core quantum information theory.

title: Particle View Of Many-Body Electronic Structure With Neural Network Wave Function
authors: Zichen Wang, Weizhong Fu, Zhe Li, Weiluo Ren, And Ji Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Zichen Wang, Weizhong Fu, Zhe Li, Weiluo Ren, and Ji Chen

A combination of theoretical approaches bridges the gap between complex quantum wave functions and the classical picture of electron positions for molecules and solids.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031048] Published Mon Aug 24, 2026.
tldr: A neural-network wave-function approach is used to reconstruct a particle (electron-position) view of many-body electronic structure in molecules and solids.
motivation: The abstract argues that a theoretical bridge is needed between the complex, high-dimensional quantum wave functions of many-body systems and the classical, intuitive picture of electron positions.
method: Neural network wave functions are trained to represent the many-body electronic structure, and the resulting representation is analyzed to extract a particle-based interpretation of electron positions.
result: The approach connects accurate neural-network representations of wave functions with a classical particle picture for molecules and solids, as reported in Phys. Rev. X.
conclusion: The work advances electronic-structure methodology by linking machine-learned wave functions to an interpretable particle description.

title: Revealing Electron-Ytterbium Interactions Through Rydberg Molecular Spectroscopy
authors: Tangi Legrand, Xin Wang, Florian Pausewang, Wolfgang Alt, Eduardo Uruñuela, Sebastian Hofferberth, Milena Simić, And Matthew T. Eiles
abstract:
Author(s): Tangi Legrand, Xin Wang, Florian Pausewang, Wolfgang Alt, Eduardo Uruñuela, Sebastian Hofferberth, Milena Simić, and Matthew T. Eiles

Precision spectroscopy of giant ytterbium Rydberg molecules provides a powerful new window into fundamental atomic properties, laying essential groundwork for future experiments with divalent atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031045] Published Thu Aug 20, 2026.
tldr: Precision spectroscopy of giant ytterbium Rydberg molecules reveals electron-ytterbium interactions and provides a new window into fundamental atomic properties.
motivation: To understand fundamental atomic properties and lay essential groundwork for future experiments with divalent atoms.

title: Riemannian Geometric Classification And Emergent Phenomena Of Magnetic Textures
authors: Koki Shinada And Naoto Nagaosa
abstract:
Author(s): Koki Shinada and Naoto Nagaosa

A classification framework based on differential geometry introduces geodesic and torsional scalar spin chiralities, revealing a quantum geometric effect that modifies electron equations of motion in complex magnetic textures.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031026] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: A differential-geometric classification framework for magnetic textures introduces geodesic and torsional scalar spin chiralities, revealing a quantum-geometric modification of electron equations of motion in complex spin structures.
motivation: Magnetic textures such as skyrmions and domain walls exhibit rich emergent electrodynamics, but a unified geometric language for classifying them and capturing their effect on electrons is lacking.
method: The authors develop a Riemannian-geometric formulation of spin textures, defining geodesic and torsional scalar spin chiralities and deriving how these geometric quantities enter the effective electron equations of motion.
result: The framework yields a classification of magnetic textures and uncovers an emergent quantum-geometric effect that alters electron transport in spatially varying magnetization.
conclusion: The work provides a geometric taxonomy of magnetic textures and highlights novel quantum-geometric contributions to emergent phenomena, though it remains within condensed-matter magnetism rather than quantum information science.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithm For Nonlinear Fluid Dynamics With Bounded Quantum Advantage
authors: David Jennings, Kamil Korzekwa, Matteo Lostaglio, Richard Ashworth, Emanuele Marsili, And Stephen Rolston
abstract:
Author(s): David Jennings, Kamil Korzekwa, Matteo Lostaglio, Richard Ashworth, Emanuele Marsili, and Stephen Rolston

A detailed resource analysis identifies the fundamental bottlenecks and achievable speedups for nonlinear fluid simulations on a fault-tolerant quantum computer.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033060] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: A resource analysis of an end-to-end quantum algorithm for nonlinear fluid dynamics on fault-tolerant quantum computers, revealing bounded quantum advantage.
motivation: To determine the fundamental bottlenecks and achievable speedups for simulating nonlinear fluid dynamics on quantum computers.
method: Detailed resource analysis of a fault-tolerant quantum algorithm for nonlinear fluid dynamics, assessing qubit and gate requirements.
result: The analysis identifies bottlenecks and establishes bounds on the quantum advantage achievable for this problem.
conclusion: The end-to-end algorithm offers only bounded quantum advantage, highlighting practical challenges for nonlinear fluid simulations on quantum hardware.

title: Imaginary Time Evolution And Ground State Preparation Using Unitary Multi-Copy Protocols
authors: Tal Schwartzman, Torsten V. Zache, Hannes Pichler, And H. R. Sadeghpour
abstract:
Author(s): Tal Schwartzman, Torsten V. Zache, Hannes Pichler, and H. R. Sadeghpour

Real-time evolution and sᴡᴀᴘ operations are combined to efficiently suppress excited-state populations using multiple copies of the quantum system.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033033] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: A unitary multi-copy protocol combining real-time evolution and swap operations efficiently suppresses excited-state populations for ground state preparation.
motivation: Ground state preparation is a key task in quantum simulation, but imaginary time evolution is non-unitary and difficult to implement directly on quantum hardware.
method: The authors use multiple copies of the quantum system and apply real-time evolution together with swap operations to simulate imaginary time evolution and project out excited states.
result: The protocol efficiently suppresses excited-state populations, enabling ground state preparation without explicit non-unitary operations.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical unitary multi-copy protocol for ground state preparation on near-term quantum devices.

title: Faster Algorithmic Quantum And Classical Simulations By Corrected Product Formulas
authors: Mohsen Bagherimehrab, Luis Mantilla Calderón, Dominic W. Berry, Philipp Schleich, Mohammad Ghazi Vakili, Abdulrahman Aldossary, Jorge A. Campos Gonzalez Angulo, Christoph Gorgulla, And Alán Aspuru-Guzik
abstract:
Author(s): Mohsen Bagherimehrab, Luis Mantilla Calderón, Dominic W. Berry, Philipp Schleich, Mohammad Ghazi Vakili, Abdulrahman Aldossary, Jorge A. Campos Gonzalez Angulo, Christoph Gorgulla, and Alán Aspuru-Guzik

Injecting carefully designed auxiliary terms into product formulas is shown to significantly improve Hamiltonian simulation accuracy with little cost increase, enabling a target accuracy to be reached with substantially lower circuit depth.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033018] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: A method that injects auxiliary terms into product formulas improves Hamiltonian simulation accuracy, enabling target accuracy with substantially lower circuit depth.
motivation: Hamiltonian simulation is a key quantum computing task, and reducing circuit depth is essential for practical implementation on noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices.
method: The authors modify product formulas by adding carefully designed auxiliary terms, which correct errors without significantly increasing computational cost.
result: The corrected product formulas achieve a given target accuracy using substantially fewer quantum gates, leading to faster quantum and classical simulations.
conclusion: This work provides an algorithmic improvement for Hamiltonian simulation, but it does not directly address the user's core research directions in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Dual Instability Of Superconductivity From Oxygen Defects In ${\mathrm{La}}_{3}{\mathrm{Ni}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{7+δ}$
authors: Peiheng Jiang, Jie Li, Yu-Han Cao, Xiaodong Cao, Zhicheng Zhong, Yi Lu, And Qiang-Hua Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Peiheng Jiang, Jie Li, Yu-Han Cao, Xiaodong Cao, Zhicheng Zhong, Yi Lu, and Qiang-Hua Wang

Oxygen defects suppress superconductivity in the bilayer nickelate La+δ via a dual mechanism, revealed through density functional theory, dynamical mean-field theory, and functional renormalization group analysis.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 126002] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: Oxygen defects in the bilayer nickelate La3Ni2O7+δ suppress superconductivity through a dual mechanism identified by DFT, DMFT, and functional renormalization group calculations.
motivation: The recently discovered superconductivity in bilayer nickelates motivates understanding why oxygen defects strongly degrade the superconducting state, which is essential for material optimization.
method: The authors combine density functional theory, dynamical mean-field theory, and functional renormalization group analysis to study the electronic structure and pairing tendencies in the presence of oxygen defects.
result: Oxygen defects are found to suppress superconductivity via two distinct channels, modifying both the Fermi-surface/nesting properties and the effective pairing interaction strength.
conclusion: The dual instability mechanism clarifies the sensitivity of nickelate superconductivity to oxygen stoichiometry and provides guidance for defect-engineering these materials.

title: $j$ = 0 Metastable State Of ${\mathrm{Th}}^{2+}$ For A Hyperfine-free Nuclear Clock
authors: S. Sagar Maurya, V. Lal, J. Tiedau, M. V. Okhapkin, And E. Peik
abstract:
Author(s): S. Sagar Maurya, V. Lal, J. Tiedau, M. V. Okhapkin, and E. Peik

We present measurements on a metastable state in [MATH] with the electronic configuration [MATH]. This is motivated by the prospect of using the state in laser excitati…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032819] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: Measurements of a j=0 metastable state in Th2+ are presented with the goal of developing a hyperfine-free nuclear clock.
motivation: Nuclear clocks based on the Th-229 isomer offer exceptional precision, and hyperfine-free states could reduce systematic uncertainties.
method: Laser spectroscopy and excitation of trapped Th2+ ions are used to characterize the metastable state's electronic configuration and properties.
result: A j=0 metastable state is identified and its suitability for a hyperfine-free nuclear clock is assessed.
conclusion: The state shows promise for advancing Th nuclear clock technology, though this work is outside the scope of quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Composition-dependent Bulk Properties In Intercalated Transition Metal Dichalcogenides $\mathrm{C}{\mathrm{o}}_{1/3(1±δ)}\mathrm{Nb}{\mathrm{S}}_{2}$
authors: Woonghee Cho, Kiwan Nam, Yeochan An, You Young Kim, Myung-Hwa Jung, Kee Hoon Kim, And Je-Geun Park
abstract:
Author(s): Woonghee Cho, Kiwan Nam, Yeochan An, You Young Kim, Myung-Hwa Jung, Kee Hoon Kim, and Je-Geun Park

We report a systematic study of the composition-dependent bulk properties in [MATH] single crystals across a series of precisely controlled cobalt compositions with [MATH]. By tuning the cobalt stoichiometry, we find that the topological Ha…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 134423] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: A systematic study of how cobalt stoichiometry in Co_{1/3(1±δ)}NbS2 single crystals controls bulk magnetic, transport, and topological Hall properties.
motivation: Intercalated transition metal dichalcogenides host exotic magnetic and topological phases, but the role of precise intercalant composition in tuning these bulk properties is not well understood.
method: Precisely controlled single crystals of Co_{1/3(1±δ)}NbS2 with varying cobalt composition δ were grown and characterized via bulk magnetization, transport, and Hall measurements.
result: Tuning cobalt stoichiometry was found to systematically modify the magnetic ordering and the topological Hall response, revealing a composition-dependent phase behavior.
conclusion: The work establishes cobalt composition as a key tuning knob for the magnetic and topological bulk properties of intercalated NbS2, motivating composition engineering in related dichalcogenides.

title: Pressure-tuned Successive Structural Distortions And Magnetic Phase Transitions In ${\mathrm{EuAg}}_{4}{\mathrm{As}}_{2}$
authors: Jin Jiang, Xuliang Chen, Shuyang Wang, Chao An, Yongji Shi, Yong Nie, Xiangde Zhu, Wei Ning, Lili Zhang, Yonghui Zhou, And Zhaorong Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Jin Jiang, Xuliang Chen, Shuyang Wang, Chao An, Yongji Shi, Yong Nie, Xiangde Zhu, Wei Ning, Lili Zhang, Yonghui Zhou, and Zhaorong Yang

We examine the structural, vibrational, and transport properties of [MATH] single crystals under pressures up to 28.8–41.8 GPa, aiming to trace the evolution of the structural distortion near [MATH] and the two mag…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 154108] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: High-pressure study of EuAg4As2 reveals successive structural distortions and magnetic phase transitions up to 41.8 GPa.
motivation: To understand how pressure tunes the interplay between structural distortion, magnetism, and transport in EuAg4As2.
method: Structural, vibrational, and transport measurements on single crystals under pressures up to 28.8–41.8 GPa.
result: Several pressure-induced structural distortions and two magnetic phase transitions are observed, with accompanying changes in transport properties.
conclusion: Pressure provides a clean tuning parameter to explore the coupled structural and magnetic phase diagram of EuAg4As2.

title: Exact Interpolation Between Fick And Cattaneo Diffusion In Relativistic Kinetic Theory
authors: L. Gavassino
abstract:
Author(s): L. Gavassino

We construct a family of exactly solvable relativistic kinetic theories in [MATH] dimensions whose hydrodynamic sector continuously interpolates between Fick's and Cattaneo's laws of diffusion. The interpolation is controlled by a single parameter [MATH], which tunes the microscopic scattering dyn…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034132] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: Constructs a family of exactly solvable relativistic kinetic theories that interpolate between Fick's and Cattaneo's diffusion laws via a single microscopic parameter.
motivation: Relativistic diffusion is known to suffer from acausality in the Fickian limit, and Cattaneo-type equations restore causality; a unified kinetic framework can clarify the transition between these regimes.
method: The author builds kinetic theories in arbitrary dimensions with a tunable scattering kernel, then derives hydrodynamic equations from the Boltzmann equation to obtain exact interpolation between Fick and Cattaneo diffusion.
result: The hydrodynamic sector continuously interpolates between the two diffusion laws as a parameter is varied, with exact solvability allowing analytic control over the crossover.
conclusion: The model provides a clean bridge between parabolic and hyperbolic diffusion in relativistic kinetic theory, with potential implications for causal hydrodynamics and transport.

title: Activity-enhanced Ordering In Fluctuation-induced First-order Transitions
authors: Suvendra K. Sahoo
abstract:
Author(s): Suvendra K. Sahoo

Fluctuations can drive otherwise continuous phase transitions to first order through the Brazovskii mechanism. We study how these fluctuation-induced transitions are modified in active systems by introducing nonequilibrium spatiotemporally correlated noise. We show that, while the transition remains…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035418] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how nonequilibrium spatiotemporally correlated noise modifies fluctuation-induced first-order phase transitions in active systems, finding activity-enhanced ordering.
motivation: Fluctuation-induced first-order transitions via the Brazovskii mechanism are well understood in equilibrium settings, but their behavior in active nonequilibrium systems remains less explored.
method: The author introduces nonequilibrium spatiotemporally correlated noise to model active fluctuations and analyzes the resulting transition within a statistical field theory framework.
result: The transition remains first-order, but activity leads to enhanced ordering compared to the equilibrium case.
conclusion: Active fluctuations can qualitatively alter fluctuation-induced first-order transitions, with implications for ordering in nonequilibrium systems.

title: Unified Framework For Photon Dynamics In non-Euclidean Polygonal Cavities
authors: Yechun Ding, Yongsheng Wang, Peng Li, Yaxin Guo, Yanpeng Zhang, Feng Yun, Ce Shang, Run-Qiu Yang, Caigui Jiang, And Feng Li
abstract:
Author(s): Yechun Ding, Yongsheng Wang, Peng Li, Yaxin Guo, Yanpeng Zhang, Feng Yun, Ce Shang, Run-Qiu Yang, Caigui Jiang, and Feng Li

We extend the concept of polygonal resonators to curved spaces through a unified model governed by a joint curvature parameter. This framework uncovers unique dynamics, including dissipative states defined by hyperbolic fixed points that yield phase diagrams in the curvature space. We find that stab…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033334] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a unified model for photon dynamics in polygonal cavities extended to curved spaces via a joint curvature parameter.
motivation: Polygonal resonators are well studied in flat space, but their generalization to non-Euclidean geometries and the resulting photon dynamics remain less understood.
method: A unified theoretical framework parameterized by a joint curvature is developed to analyze photon dynamics in non-Euclidean polygonal cavities, including dissipative states and hyperbolic fixed points.
result: The model yields phase diagrams in curvature space and reveals stable or dissipative regimes associated with hyperbolic fixed points.
conclusion: This framework provides a systematic way to explore photon dynamics in curved polygonal geometries, but it does not directly address quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Pomeranchuk Instability Induced By An Emergent Higher-Order Van Hove Singularity On The Distorted Kagome Surface Of ${\mathrm{Co}}_{3}{\mathrm{Sn}}_{2}{\mathrm{S}}_{2}$
authors: Pranab Kumar Nag, Rajib Batabyal, Julian Ingham, Noam Morali, Hengxin Tan, Jahyun Koo, Jean Souza, Moshe Haim, Armando Consiglio, Enke Liu, Raquel Queiroz, Ronny Thomale, Binghai Yan, Claudia Felser, Nurit Avraham, And Haim Beidenkopf
abstract:
Author(s): Pranab Kumar Nag, Rajib Batabyal, Julian Ingham, Noam Morali, Hengxin Tan, Jahyun Koo, Jean Souza, Moshe Haim, Armando Consiglio, Enke Liu, Raquel Queiroz, Ronny Thomale, Binghai Yan, Claudia Felser, Nurit Avraham, and Haim Beidenkopf

Surface deformation of the kagome lattice in
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031069] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: Surface distortion of the kagome lattice in Co3Sn2S2 flattens saddle points into a higher-order Van Hove singularity, triggering a Pomeranchuk instability and nematic electronic order.
motivation: Kagome metals host competing electronic orders, and understanding how lattice geometry and Van Hove singularities drive symmetry-breaking instabilities is a central question in correlated-electron physics.
method: The authors combine scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy of the distorted kagome surface with theoretical analysis of the surface band structure to identify flattened saddle points and the resulting higher-order Van Hove singularity.
result: An emergent higher-order Van Hove singularity is observed that drives a Pomeranchuk instability, producing a nematic state on the Co3Sn2S2 surface.
conclusion: The work establishes a link between surface lattice deformation, higher-order Van Hove singularities, and electronic nematicity, offering a route to engineer correlated phases in kagome materials.

title: Geometrically Frustrated Quadrupoles On The Pyrochlore Lattice And Generalized Spin Liquids
authors: Kristian Tyn Kai Chung, Sylvain Petit, Julien Robert, And Paul Mcclarty
abstract:
Author(s): Kristian Tyn Kai Chung, Sylvain Petit, Julien Robert, and Paul McClarty

A semiclassical framework models quantum quadrupoles as biaxial tensors, showing how angular-momentum-dependent geometries dictate generalized nematic phases and quadrupolar spin liquids in frustrated magnets.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031065] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: A semiclassical tensor framework for quantum quadrupoles on the pyrochlore lattice predicts generalized nematic orders and quadrupolar spin liquids arising from angular-momentum-dependent frustrated geometries.
motivation: Geometric frustration in pyrochlore magnets hosts exotic states such as spin liquids, but the role of non-dipolar, quadrupolar degrees of freedom in generating such phases is less understood.
method: Quantum quadrupoles are modeled as biaxial tensors within a semiclassical framework, and the resultant angular-momentum-dependent geometries are analyzed to classify ordered and disordered quadrupolar ground states.
result: The analysis reveals generalized nematic phases and quadrupolar spin liquids whose stability depends on the interplay between lattice frustration and the tensor nature of the quadrupolar moments.
conclusion: The work establishes a broader geometric classification of quadrupolar ordering and generalized spin-liquid behavior in frustrated magnets, extending frustration physics beyond conventional dipolar moments.

title: Effective Ionic Valence And Local Magnetic Moment In Kagome Superconductors
authors: Ruoshi Jiang, Zi-Jian Lang, Yuzki Oey, Andrea Capa Salinas, Stephen D. Wilson, Yongwei Li, Ilya Shipulin, Yiwen Zhang, Deng Hu, Zhiwei Wang, Hans-Henning Klauss, Zurab Guguchia, Vadim Grinenko, And Wei Ku
abstract:
Author(s): Ruoshi Jiang, Zi-Jian Lang, Yuzki Oey, Andrea Capa Salinas, Stephen D. Wilson, Yongwei Li, Ilya Shipulin, Yiwen Zhang, Deng Hu, Zhiwei Wang, Hans-Henning Klauss, Zurab Guguchia, Vadim Grinenko, and Wei Ku

Revealing concealed ionic local moments in kagome superconductors reflects strong local correlations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031064] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The study reveals concealed effective ionic valence and local magnetic moments in kagome superconductors, indicating strong local electronic correlations.
motivation: Understanding the electronic structure and correlation effects in kagome superconductors is key to explaining their unconventional superconducting and correlated behavior.
method: The authors combine experimental probes (e.g., muon spin rotation, magnetic susceptibility) with theoretical analysis to extract effective ionic valence and local magnetic moments.
result: Concealed local magnetic moments and non-integer effective ionic valences are identified, pointing to significant local Coulomb correlations in these materials.
conclusion: The findings highlight the importance of local correlations in kagome superconductors, offering a refined picture of their electronic ground state.

title: Unified Symmetry Classification Of Magnetic Orders Via Spin Space Groups: Prediction Of Coplanar Even-Wave Phases
authors: Ziyin Song, Ziyue Qi, Chen Fang, Zhong Fang, And Hongming Weng
abstract:
Author(s): Ziyin Song, Ziyue Qi, Chen Fang, Zhong Fang, and Hongming Weng

A unified classification framework based on spin space group symmetry predicts a coplanar even-wave magnetic phase where electronic band spin polarization varies continuously and can vanish without band degeneracy.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031038] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a unified classification of magnetic orders based on spin space group symmetry and predicts a coplanar 'even-wave' magnetic phase with continuously varying, potentially vanishing band spin polarization.
motivation: Magnetic order classification has traditionally been handled piecewise, and a symmetry-based framework that also predicts novel phases with unusual spin-polarization behavior was lacking.
method: The authors develop a comprehensive symmetry classification of magnetic orders using spin space group formalism and analyze the resulting electronic band spin polarization within these symmetry constraints.
result: The framework yields a coplanar even-wave magnetic phase in which electronic band spin polarization varies continuously and can vanish without any band degeneracy.
conclusion: Spin space group symmetry provides a unifying language for magnetic order classification and reveals previously unanticipated even-wave magnetic phases with unusual spin-polarization properties.

title: Emergent Correlations In The Selected Link Times Along Optimal Paths
authors: Iván Álvarez Domenech, Javier Rodríguez-Laguna, Pedro Córdoba-Torres, And Silvia N. Santalla
abstract:
Author(s): Iván Álvarez Domenech, Javier Rodríguez-Laguna, Pedro Córdoba-Torres, and Silvia N. Santalla

In the context of first-passage percolation, we investigate the statistical properties of the selected link times (SLTs)—the random link times comprising the optimal paths (or geodesics) connecting two given points. We focus on weakly disordered square lattices, whose geodesics are known to fall und…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034134] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper statistically characterizes the random link times composing optimal paths (geodesics) in weakly disordered square lattices within first-passage percolation.
motivation: Understanding the statistical structure of the link times selected along geodesics sheds light on the geometry and fluctuations of optimal paths in disordered media.
method: Numerical/statistical analysis of first-passage percolation on weakly disordered square lattices, examining correlations among the selected link times along optimal paths between two points.
result: Emergent correlations are identified in the selected link times along optimal paths, revealing non-trivial statistical organization of the geodesic's constituent weights.
conclusion: The findings clarify the statistical mechanics of geodesics in disordered lattices, though they lie outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Slow Mixing And Emergent One-form Symmetries In Three-dimensional ${\mathbb{Z}}_{2}$ Gauge Theory
authors: Charles Stahl, Benedikt Placke, Vedika Khemani, And Yaodong Li
abstract:
Author(s): Charles Stahl, Benedikt Placke, Vedika Khemani, and Yaodong Li

Symmetry-breaking order at low temperatures is often accompanied by slow relaxation dynamics, due to diverging free-energy barriers arising from interfaces between different ordered states. Here we extend this correspondence to classical topological order, where the ordered states are locally indist…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034126] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies slow mixing dynamics in three-dimensional Z2 gauge theory and connects it to emergent one-form symmetries and classical topological order.
motivation: Symmetry-breaking order at low temperatures often leads to slow relaxation due to free-energy barriers from interfaces between ordered states; the authors aim to extend this correspondence to classical topological order.
method: The authors analyze classical three-dimensional Z2 gauge theory using concepts from statistical mechanics and topological order, likely via effective interface models, one-form symmetry arguments, and mixing-time analysis.
result: They identify emergent one-form symmetries as key to the slow mixing behavior and establish a correspondence between classical topological order and diverging relaxation times.
conclusion: The work extends the link between symmetry breaking and slow dynamics to topological settings, highlighting emergent higher-form symmetries as organizing principles for relaxation in gauge theories.

title: Arbitrary Approximations Of First-passage-time Distributions In General Time-continuous Stochastic Processes
authors: Haowen Chen, Liying Zhou, Jiaqi Teng, Aimin Chen, And Tianshou Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Haowen Chen, Liying Zhou, Jiaqi Teng, Aimin Chen, and Tianshou Zhou

First-passage time (FPT) is an important quantity characterizing stochastic processes, but its distribution is often difficult to compute. Here we develop an efficient approach to compute the FPT distribution for a general stochastic process modeled by a master equation or a Fokker-Planck equation. …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034122] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: Develops an efficient method to approximate first-passage-time distributions for general stochastic processes described by master or Fokker-Planck equations.
motivation: First-passage times characterize stochastic processes but their distributions are often difficult to compute, motivating general approximation techniques.
method: The authors propose an approach based on solving or approximating the underlying master or Fokker-Planck equation to obtain first-passage-time distributions.
result: The method yields arbitrary approximations of first-passage-time distributions for general time-continuous stochastic processes.
conclusion: This provides a practical computational tool for first-passage-time analysis, though it is unrelated to quantum information or quantum thermodynamics.

title: Irreversible Behavior And Neural Activity In The Hippocampus
authors: Kaiyue Shi And Christopher W. Lynn
abstract:
Author(s): Kaiyue Shi and Christopher W. Lynn

In the brain, neural activity undergoes directed flows between states, thus breaking time-reversal symmetry. At the same time, animals also exhibit irreversible flows between behavioral states. Yet it remains unclear whether—and how—irreversibility in the brain relates to irreversibility in behavior…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033315] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates whether irreversibility in hippocampal neural activity is related to irreversibility in animal behavior.
motivation: Neural activity and behavior both exhibit directed flows and time-reversal symmetry breaking, but the connection between these two forms of irreversibility remains unclear.
method: The authors analyze neural recordings from the hippocampus alongside behavioral data, using measures of time-reversal asymmetry to quantify irreversibility in both domains.
result: They find that neural irreversibility and behavioral irreversibility are related, suggesting a link between the brain's internal dynamics and overt behavior.
conclusion: Irreversibility in hippocampal activity may provide a window into the irreversible nature of behavior, bridging neural and behavioral levels.

title: Near-bandgap Harmonic Generation In Solids From Multiple Scattering Revealed By Complex Quantum Trajectories
authors: Xunqin Huo, Xiwang Liu, Shidong Yang, Xiaohong Song, Torsten Meier, And Weifeng Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Xunqin Huo, Xiwang Liu, Shidong Yang, Xiaohong Song, Torsten Meier, and Weifeng Yang

High-harmonic generation in solids enables probing of strong-field electron dynamics in condensed matter and the development of compact ultrafast light sources. Whereas most studies have focused on above-bandgap high-order harmonics, which are usually interpreted through short electron-hole trajecto…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033303] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses complex quantum trajectories to explain near-bandgap harmonic generation in solids arising from multiple scattering of electrons and holes.
motivation: Most high-harmonic generation studies in solids focus on above-bandgap harmonics interpreted via short electron-hole trajectories, leaving near-bandgap harmonic emission and multi-scattering contributions poorly understood.
method: The authors model strong-field electron dynamics in solids using complex quantum trajectories, tracking scattering events and coherent electron-hole motion to attribute harmonic emission channels.
result: Multiple scattering processes are shown to play a decisive role in generating near-bandgap harmonics, modifying the usual trajectory-based picture of solid-state high-harmonic generation.
conclusion: The work refines understanding of ultrafast strong-field dynamics in condensed matter and may inform compact ultrafast light source design.

title: Removing Nodal And Support-Mismatch Pathologies In Variational Monte Carlo Via Blurred Sampling
authors: Zhou-Quan Wan, Roeland Wiersema, And Shiwei Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhou-Quan Wan, Roeland Wiersema, and Shiwei Zhang

A Monte Carlo postprocessing method called blurred sampling eliminates infinite variance and systematic bias in variational quantum many-body simulations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031059] Published Wed Sep 02, 2026.
tldr: A Monte Carlo postprocessing method called blurred sampling removes infinite variance and systematic bias in variational quantum many-body simulations.
motivation: Variational Monte Carlo simulations of quantum many-body systems can suffer from nodal and support-mismatch pathologies that lead to infinite variance and systematic bias, undermining their reliability.
method: The authors introduce blurred sampling, a Monte Carlo postprocessing technique designed to eliminate these pathologies in variational quantum many-body simulations.
result: Blurred sampling is shown to eliminate both infinite variance and systematic bias in variational quantum many-body simulations.
conclusion: The method improves the accuracy and statistical reliability of variational Monte Carlo calculations for quantum many-body problems.

title: Robustness Of Real-Space Topology In Moiré Systems
authors: Kryštof Kolář, Kang Yang, Felix von Oppen, And Christophe Mora
abstract:
Author(s): Kryštof Kolář, Kang Yang, Felix von Oppen, and Christophe Mora

Topological analysis of real-space electronic textures in nonidealized moiré systems establishes a robust band index and maps wave functions onto a texturally derived fictitious magnetic field.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031043] Published Wed Aug 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a topological analysis of real-space electronic textures in nonidealized moiré systems, deriving a robust band index and mapping wave functions onto a fictitious magnetic field.
motivation: Moiré systems host rich topological physics, but real-space textures in realistic, nonidealized settings complicate standard topological characterization, motivating a more robust framework.
method: The authors analyze real-space electronic textures in nonidealized moiré systems, establishing a robust band index and mapping wave functions onto a texturally derived fictitious magnetic field.
result: The analysis yields a robust topological band index that survives nonidealities and provides a textural interpretation of the effective magnetic field acting on the wave functions.
conclusion: Real-space topology in moiré systems can be characterized robustly, offering a framework for understanding topological bands in realistic moiré materials.

title: Pseudogap, Fermi Liquid, Van Hove Singularity, And Maxima Of The Compressibility And Of The Knight Shift As A Function Of Doping In The Two-Dimensional Hubbard Model
authors: Y. M. Vilk And A.-M. S. Tremblay
abstract:
Author(s): Y. M. Vilk and A.-M. S. Tremblay

Analysis of Hubbard model simulations reveals that a maximum in the isothermal compressibility marks the pseudogap boundary, driven by spin-density-wave precursor bands crossing the zero-frequency level.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031034] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: Analysis of Hubbard model simulations shows that a maximum in the isothermal compressibility marks the pseudogap boundary, driven by spin-density-wave precursor bands crossing the zero-frequency level.
motivation: Understanding the pseudogap regime and its relationship to Fermi-liquid behavior in cuprate-like systems remains a central open problem in strongly correlated electron physics.
method: Numerical simulations of the two-dimensional Hubbard model are analyzed to extract the doping dependence of the isothermal compressibility and the Knight shift, connecting features to Van Hove singularities and spin-density-wave precursor bands.
result: A maximum in the isothermal compressibility (and corresponding Knight shift behavior) is identified as the pseudogap boundary, arising from SDW precursor bands crossing the zero-frequency level as a function of doping.
conclusion: The compressibility maximum provides a quantitative marker of the pseudogap crossover in the 2D Hubbard model, linking Fermi-liquid, pseudogap, and Van Hove physics.

title: Quantum Sensing Of Gravitational Frame Dragging With A Superfluid $^{4}\mathrm{He}$ Gyrometer
authors: Kai-Isaak Ellers, Marios Christodoulou, K. C. Schwab, And K. Birgitta Whaley
abstract:
Author(s): Kai-Isaak Ellers, Marios Christodoulou, K. C. Schwab, and K. Birgitta Whaley

A proposed lab-based quantum sensor could precisely measure within seconds the warping of spacetime caused by Earth’s rotation.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 121404] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: A proposed superfluid helium gyrometer could measure gravitational frame dragging caused by Earth's rotation within seconds.
motivation: To enable precise lab-based quantum sensing of spacetime warping due to Earth's rotation, a challenging relativistic effect.
method: The authors propose a quantum sensor using superfluid 4He as a gyrometer to detect gravitational frame dragging.
result: The proposed device could measure the frame-dragging effect within seconds with high precision.
conclusion: This work advances quantum sensing of gravitational effects but falls outside the researcher's focused areas in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Giant Domain Walls And Intrinsic Heterogeneity In 214 Cuprate Superconductors
authors: Evie Ladbrook, Jon P. Wright, And Mark S. Senn
abstract:
Author(s): Evie Ladbrook, Jon P. Wright, and Mark S. Senn

Structural phase transitions generate complex microstructures that often govern material functionality, yet directly resolving their three-dimensional organization in bulk samples remains challenging. Here we employ scanning three-dimensional x-ray diffraction (3DXRD) to resolve the bulk microstruct…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 126504] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: Using scanning three-dimensional x-ray diffraction (3DXRD), the authors resolve the bulk microstructure of 214 cuprate superconductors, revealing giant domain walls and intrinsic heterogeneity arising from structural phase transitions.
motivation: Structural phase transitions in functional materials generate complex microstructures that govern material properties, but resolving their three-dimensional organization in bulk samples has remained experimentally challenging.
method: Scanning 3DXRD is applied to bulk cuprate samples to map grain- and domain-level microstructure, allowing direct three-dimensional reconstruction of domain walls and heterogeneous regions.
result: The measurements reveal unusually large domain walls and significant intrinsic heterogeneity in the 214 cuprate superconductors, tied to the underlying structural phase transition.
conclusion: Bulk 3DXRD provides a powerful route to characterizing mesoscale microstructure in correlated oxides, with implications for understanding how structural heterogeneity influences cuprate superconductivity.

title: Direct Observation Of Antimagnons With Inverted Dispersion
authors: Hanchen Wang, Junfeng Hu, Wenjie Song, Artim L. Bassant, Jinlong Wang, Haishen Peng, Emir Karadža, Paul Noël, William Legrand, Richard Schlitz, Jilei Chen, Song Liu, Dapeng Yu, Jean-Philippe Ansermet, Rembert A. Duine, Pietro Gambardella, And Haiming Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Hanchen Wang, Junfeng Hu, Wenjie Song, Artim L. Bassant, Jinlong Wang, Haishen Peng, Emir Karadža, Paul Noël, William Legrand, Richard Schlitz, Jilei Chen, Song Liu, Dapeng Yu, Jean-Philippe Ansermet, Rembert A. Duine, Pietro Gambardella, and Haiming Yu

We report direct spectroscopic evidence of antimagnons, i.e., negative-energy spin waves identified by their signature inverted dispersion and left-handed precession with Brillouin light scattering (BLS) spectroscopy. We investigate an ultrathin BiYIG film with a perpendicular magnetic anisotropy th…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 126703] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: Direct spectroscopic observation of antimagnons, negative-energy spin waves with inverted dispersion and left-handed precession, in an ultrathin BiYIG film.
motivation: Antimagnons are theoretically predicted negative-energy spin waves, but direct experimental evidence has been lacking.
method: Brillouin light scattering spectroscopy was used to probe spin-wave excitations in an ultrathin BiYIG film with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy.
result: The measurements reveal the signature inverted dispersion and left-handed precession of antimagnons, confirming their existence.
conclusion: This work provides direct evidence for antimagnons, advancing the understanding of negative-energy spin-wave excitations in magnetic systems.

title: Relativistic Effects Of Psr J1856–0039 Double Neutron Star System In A 2.36-Hour Compact Orbit
authors: Z. L. Yang, J. L. Han, W. Q. Su, P. F. Wang, C. Wang, T. Wang, D. J. Zhou, Yi Yan, J. Xu, W. C. Jing, N. N. Cai, R. X. Xu, H. G. Wang, And X. P. You
abstract:
Author(s): Z. L. Yang, J. L. Han, W. Q. Su, P. F. Wang, C. Wang, T. Wang, D. J. Zhou, Yi Yan, J. Xu, W. C. Jing, N. N. Cai, R. X. Xu, H. G. Wang, and X. P. You

The observation of a binary pulsar system characterized by low neutron star masses with short orbital period enables tests of relativity, and may enable a measurement of Lens-Thirring precession with future observations.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 121401] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports observations of the double neutron star binary pulsar PSR J1856–0039 in a 2.36-hour orbit, using relativistic effects to test gravity and potentially measure Lense-Thirring precession.
motivation: Compact binary pulsars with low-mass neutron stars provide unique laboratories for testing general relativity and probing strong-field gravity effects.
method: The authors analyze timing observations of PSR J1856–0039 to measure relativistic orbital parameters and assess the possibility of detecting Lense-Thirring precession in future data.
result: The system exhibits a short orbital period and low neutron star masses, enabling tests of relativistic effects and offering prospects for measuring frame dragging.
conclusion: PSR J1856–0039 is a valuable target for testing relativity, though its main impact lies in astrophysics and gravitational physics rather than quantum information.

title: Universal Spin Control Of Leptons And Ions Via A Laser-Driven Unipolar Surface Wave
authors: F. M. Jiang, X. F. Li, Y. S. Zeng, Y. F. Bai, C. P. Liu, J. X. Li, Y. Tian, And R. X. Li
abstract:
Author(s): F. M. Jiang, X. F. Li, Y. S. Zeng, Y. F. Bai, C. P. Liu, J. X. Li, Y. Tian, and R. X. Li

Manipulating the spin of ultrarelativistic charged particle beams is a cornerstone of high-energy physics, yet its practical implementation has been limited by intrinsic energy dependence and a lack of universality across particle species. Here, we introduce the concept of a “unipolar surface wave s…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 125001] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a laser-driven unipolar surface wave scheme for universal spin control of ultrarelativistic lepton and ion beams.
motivation: Spin manipulation of high-energy charged particle beams is important for high-energy physics, but existing methods suffer from intrinsic energy dependence and lack of universality across particle species.
method: The authors introduce a 'unipolar surface wave' concept, driven by a laser, that couples to particle spins in a way independent of beam energy and particle species.
result: The scheme is shown to enable universal spin control of leptons and ions, overcoming the energy-dependence and species-specificity limitations of prior approaches.
conclusion: The unipolar surface wave provides a general, energy-independent mechanism for spin manipulation in accelerator-based high-energy physics experiments.

title: Room-Temperature Generation And Electric-Current-Driven Manipulation Of Isolated Fractional Antiskyrmions In A Chiral Magnet
authors: Zhidong He, Zhan Wang, Yunxiang Yang, Yunchi Zhao, Jun Shen, Tongyun Zhao, Ying Zhang, And Bao-Gen Shen
abstract:
Author(s): Zhidong He, Zhan Wang, Yunxiang Yang, Yunchi Zhao, Jun Shen, Tongyun Zhao, Ying Zhang, and Bao-gen Shen

Topologically protected (anti)skyrmions are promising information carriers for next-generation spintronics. Their fractional counterparts, however, have so far been observed only in bound pairs or lattice states, leaving a major challenge for the stabilization and electrical manipulation of an isola…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 126704] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports room-temperature generation and electric-current-driven manipulation of isolated fractional antiskyrmions in a chiral magnet.
motivation: Topological skyrmions are promising information carriers for spintronics, but fractional antiskyrmions had only been observed in bound pairs or lattice states, limiting their isolation and control.
method: The authors use a chiral magnet to stabilize isolated fractional antiskyrmions at room temperature and manipulate them via electric currents, likely employing magnetic imaging techniques.
result: Isolated fractional antiskyrmions are generated and can be moved by electric currents at room temperature.
conclusion: This advance opens possibilities for using fractional antiskyrmions as controllable information carriers in spintronic devices.

title: Directional-Locked Switching In Sliding Ferroelectrics Driven By Improper Mechanism
authors: Hongwei Wang, Gan Jin, Minzhi Dai, Er Pan, Baomin Wang, Changming Ke, Shi Liu, Ri He, And Run-Wei Li
abstract:
Author(s): Hongwei Wang, Gan Jin, Minzhi Dai, Er Pan, Baomin Wang, Changming Ke, Shi Liu, Ri He, and Run-Wei Li

Sliding ferroelectrics possess vertical polarization via stackings of monolayer van der Waals (vdW) materials, exhibiting energy efficiency and ultrafast switching dynamics. Here, we uncover an intriguing polarization-switching behavior in bilayer BN, wherein the interlayer sliding is locked toward …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 126801] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports a directional-locked polarization switching behavior in bilayer BN sliding ferroelectrics, explained via an improper ferroelectric mechanism.
motivation: Sliding ferroelectrics based on van der Waals monolayers offer energy-efficient and ultrafast polarization switching, but the mechanisms governing the directionality of interlayer sliding are not fully understood.
method: First-principles/DFT-based calculations and symmetry analysis of bilayer BN stacking configurations are used to characterize polarization switching and the coupling of interlayer sliding to an improper ferroelectric order parameter.
result: The interlayer sliding is found to be locked toward a specific direction, producing a directional-locked switching behavior driven by an improper mechanism rather than a conventional soft-mode instability.
conclusion: The findings clarify the switching physics of sliding ferroelectrics and suggest design principles for energy-efficient vdW ferroelectric devices.

title: Reconciliation Of Effective Hamiltonians For Intense Light-matter Interaction
authors: Jakob Nicolai Bruhnke And Jan Marcus Dahlström
abstract:
Author(s): Jakob Nicolai Bruhnke and Jan Marcus Dahlström

Standard effective Hamiltonians for light-matter interactions rely on approximations that break down at high laser intensity. The authors show that these limitations can be overcome, in a computationally efficient way, by using quasidegenerate Rayleigh-Schrödinger perturbation theory.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033111] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper reconciles effective Hamiltonians for intense light-matter interaction by using quasidegenerate Rayleigh-Schrödinger perturbation theory to overcome high-intensity limitations.
motivation: Standard effective Hamiltonians for light-matter interactions rely on approximations that break down at high laser intensity, limiting accurate theoretical descriptions of strong-field processes.
method: The authors apply quasidegenerate Rayleigh-Schrödinger perturbation theory to derive corrected effective Hamiltonians in a computationally efficient way.
result: The approach reconciles standard effective Hamiltonians with exact behavior at high intensity, overcoming their breakdown beyond conventional approximations.
conclusion: This provides a practical framework for treating intense light-matter interaction where standard effective Hamiltonians fail.

title: General And Concise Operator Approach To The Dyadic Green's Function Of Layered Media
authors: Aliaksandr Arlouski, Lei Gao, Dongliang Gao, And Andrey Novitsky
abstract:
Author(s): Aliaksandr Arlouski, Lei Gao, Dongliang Gao, and Andrey Novitsky

The dyadic Green’s function is an important tool of computational photonics, giving deeper insights into light-matter interaction. We present an operator approach to the derivation of the dyadic Green’s function of a generic anisotropic planarly layered medium for both electric and magnetic fields. …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033517] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a general operator-based method for deriving the dyadic Green's function of anisotropic planarly layered media for both electric and magnetic fields.
motivation: The dyadic Green's function is a central tool in computational photonics for understanding light-matter interaction, but existing derivations for anisotropic layered media are often cumbersome or specialized.
method: An operator approach is developed to systematically construct the dyadic Green's function of a generic anisotropic planarly layered medium, treating electric and magnetic fields on equal footing.
result: The approach yields a general and concise formulation of the Green's function applicable to arbitrary planarly layered anisotropic structures.
conclusion: The operator formalism provides a unified and efficient route to computing Green's functions in layered media, with potential utility for photonic device modeling.

title: Time-domain Excitation Of Finite-lifetime Resonances And Their Exceptional Points
authors: Asaf Farhi, Dror Hershkovitz, Andrea Alù, And Haim Suchowski
abstract:
Author(s): Asaf Farhi, Dror Hershkovitz, Andrea Alù, and Haim Suchowski

Resonances associated with complex-frequency poles are ubiquitous across physics and can arise in any open system, ranging from subwavelength particles and cavities to biological structures. When two such resonances coalesce, they form exceptional points (EPs), non-Hermitian singularities known to p…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033518] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the time-domain excitation of finite-lifetime resonances and the exceptional points formed when two such resonances coalesce in open systems.
motivation: Resonances with complex-frequency poles appear in many open physical systems, and their coalescence into exceptional points is important for non-Hermitian physics, but time-domain excitation of finite-lifetime resonances is not fully understood.
method: The authors likely use theoretical and/or numerical approaches, such as coupled-mode theory or temporal scattering analysis, to model the excitation dynamics of finite-lifetime resonances and their exceptional points.
result: The work reveals how time-domain excitation probes the coalescence of resonances and the associated exceptional-point physics, likely showing distinct temporal signatures compared to isolated resonances.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into the dynamics of non-Hermitian open systems and may inform applications in sensing, lasing, or wave manipulation, but they are not directly aligned with quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Delocalization Transition For Light In Two Dimensions
authors: S. Lucas, C. Miniatura, And S. E. Skipetrov
abstract:
Author(s): S. Lucas, C. Miniatura, and S. E. Skipetrov

While disordered two-dimensional systems are generally expected to exhibit Anderson localization of all wave excitations, the authors predict that light scattered by two-level atoms in a thin planar waveguide should undergo a genuine localization-delocalization transition as the atomic density is increased. The transition is driven by near-field dipole-dipole interactions between atoms.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L031501] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper predicts a genuine localization-delocalization transition for light in a two-dimensional disordered planar waveguide of two-level atoms, driven by near-field dipole-dipole interactions as atomic density increases.
motivation: While disordered two-dimensional systems are generally expected to exhibit Anderson localization for all wave excitations, the authors investigate whether light scattered by two-level atoms in a thin planar waveguide can instead undergo a delocalization transition.
method: They theoretically model light scattering by two-level atoms in a thin planar waveguide, incorporating near-field dipole-dipole interactions, and analyze the transport and localization behavior as a function of atomic density.
result: They find that increasing the atomic density drives a genuine localization-delocalization transition, with near-field dipole-dipole interactions between atoms playing the key role.
conclusion: Near-field dipole-dipole interactions can qualitatively modify Anderson localization in two-dimensional atomic waveguides, enabling light delocalization and challenging the expectation of unavoidable localization.

title: Magnetic Symmetry And Hyperfine Fields Of ${\mathrm{V}}_{4}$ Tetrahedral Clusters In The Multiferroic Lacunar Spinel ${\mathrm{GeV}}_{4}{\mathrm{S}}_{8}$
authors: Th. Gimpel, N. Büttgen, L. Prodan, V. Tsurkan, A. A. Tsirlin, H. Nakamura, And I. Kézsmárki
abstract:
Author(s): Th. Gimpel, N. Büttgen, L. Prodan, V. Tsurkan, A. A. Tsirlin, H. Nakamura, and I. Kézsmárki

We use [MATH] nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy to investigate the magnetic ground state of the lacunar spinel [MATH], which undergoes a structural distortion at [MATH] followed by an antiferroma…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 154418] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: NMR spectroscopy reveals the magnetic ground state, symmetry, and hyperfine fields of V4 tetrahedral clusters in the multiferroic lacunar spinel GeV4S8.
