motivation: To understand the magnetic ground state and multiferroic properties of the lacunar spinel GeV4S8, which undergoes a structural distortion and antiferromagnetic ordering.
method: The authors use nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy to probe the local magnetic fields and symmetry at the V4 tetrahedral clusters.
result: The NMR measurements identify the magnetic symmetry and hyperfine fields associated with the antiferromagnetic ground state below the structural transition.
conclusion: The study provides microscopic insight into the magnetism of GeV4S8, clarifying the interplay between structural distortion and magnetic order in this lacunar spinel.

title: Anisotropy Of Spin Waves In The Field-polarized Phase Of Fe-doped MnSi
authors: I. N. Khoroshiy, A. Podlesnyak, D. Menzel, M. C. Rahn, D. S. Inosov, A. S. Sukhanov, And S. E. Nikitin
abstract:
Author(s): I. N. Khoroshiy, A. Podlesnyak, D. Menzel, M. C. Rahn, D. S. Inosov, A. S. Sukhanov, and S. E. Nikitin

Chiral magnetic textures, such as skyrmions, are of great interest to the condensed matter community due to their novel transport properties. The stabilization of topologically nontrivial magnetic phases, like the skyrmion lattice in cubic MnSi, is governed by underlying magnetic interactions which …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 154416] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports inelastic neutron scattering measurements of the anisotropy of spin-wave excitations in the field-polarized phase of Fe-doped MnSi, a chiral magnet hosting skyrmion lattices.
motivation: Chiral magnetic textures such as skyrmions in cubic MnSi derive their stability from underlying magnetic interactions, whose precise form—including anisotropic exchange and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya terms—remains incompletely characterized.
method: Inelastic neutron scattering is used to map spin-wave dispersion in the field-polarized phase of Fe-doped MnSi, allowing the extraction of anisotropic exchange parameters from the measured magnon spectra.
result: The spin-wave spectrum shows measurable anisotropy in the field-polarized phase, revealing the magnitude and symmetry of anisotropic exchange contributions that shape the magnetic phase diagram.
conclusion: The findings refine the microscopic spin-Hamiltonian description of Fe-doped MnSi and help explain the stabilization of topological magnetic textures in chiral magnets.

title: Topologically Robust Flat-band Zero-index Terahertz Metasurfaces With Polarization-vortex-protected Bound States In The Continuum
authors: Guangcheng Sun (孙广成), Yongming Zhang (张永明), Bo Gao (高博), Jiayong Han (韩佳勇), Yue Wang (王玥), Wenshuo Chen (陈文烁), Gengyu Bai (白耕瑜), Rui Wu (吴睿), Yaohe Li (李曜合), Zijian Cui (崔子健), And Xiaoguang Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Guangcheng Sun (孙广成), Yongming Zhang (张永明), Bo Gao (高博), Jiayong Han (韩佳勇), Yue Wang (王玥), Wenshuo Chen (陈文烁), Gengyu Bai (白耕瑜), Rui Wu (吴睿), Yaohe Li (李曜合), Zijian Cui (崔子健), and Xiaoguang Zhao (赵晓光)

Zero-index metamaterials, distinguished by a near-zero effective refractive index, enable extraordinary wave-manipulation capabilities unattainable in conventional media. However, their practical implementation is fundamentally hindered by intrinsic radiative losses, as Dirac-cone modes residing wit…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 165414] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper designs topologically robust flat-band zero-index terahertz metasurfaces that support polarization-vortex-protected bound states in the continuum to overcome radiative losses in zero-index metamaterials.
motivation: Zero-index metamaterials promise extraordinary wave manipulation but suffer from intrinsic radiative losses because Dirac-cone modes residing within the light cone couple to free space, degrading practical performance.
method: The authors engineer flat-band metasurfaces whose symmetry and topology protect bound states in the continuum, using polarization vortices to stabilize these non-radiative modes in the terahertz regime.
result: The proposed metasurface achieves topologically protected, polarization-vortex-mediated bound states in the continuum that suppress radiative loss and enable robust zero-index behavior at terahertz frequencies.
conclusion: Topological and polarization-vortex protection offers a viable route to practical low-loss zero-index terahertz metasurfaces, though the work remains within classical photonics and metamaterial design.

title: Emergence Of Robust Charge Density Wave Phases In One-dimensional Nanostructures Of $1{T}^{′}$-phase ${\mathrm{MoTe}}_{2}$
authors: Zi-Yi Han, Liangting Ye, Yu-Qi Li, Ya-Ning Ren, Bing Huang, And Lin He
abstract:
Author(s): Zi-Yi Han, Liangting Ye, Yu-Qi Li, Ya-Ning Ren, Bing Huang, and Lin He

Charge-density waves (CDWs) are a hallmark of collective electronic ordering. As the pioneering and most fundamental model system studied in CDW physics, one-dimensional (1D) CDWs are theoretically profound yet experimentally fragile. They are widely recognized to be highly susceptible to environmen…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 165415] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports the emergence of robust one-dimensional charge density wave phases in nanostructures of the 1T'-phase of MoTe2.
motivation: One-dimensional charge density waves are theoretically fundamental but experimentally fragile, being highly susceptible to environmental perturbations, so finding a robust realization is of interest.
method: The authors fabricate and characterize 1D nanostructures of 1T'-MoTe2, likely using scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy and related transport or spectroscopic probes to identify CDW ordering.
result: Robust charge density wave phases emerge in the 1D MoTe2 nanostructures, apparently more stable than conventional 1D CDW systems.
conclusion: 1T'-MoTe2 nanostructures provide a promising platform for studying robust 1D CDW physics, with implications for condensed matter electronic ordering rather than quantum information.

title: Crystal Fields And The Properties Of The Kitaev Candidate ${\mathrm{Na}}_{3}{\mathrm{Co}}_{2}{\mathrm{SbO}}_{6}$ Probed With X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy
authors: M. M. Ferreira-Carvalho, S. H. Chen, Y. C. Ku, S. Rößler, Robert Kluge, Ryan C. Morrow, Javier Herrero-Martín, P. Gargiani, C. Y. Kuo, C. F. Chang, Alexander C. Komarek, Z. Hu, M. W. Haverkort, And L. H. Tjeng
abstract:
Author(s): M. M. Ferreira-Carvalho, S. H. Chen, Y. C. Ku, S. Rößler, Robert Kluge, Ryan C. Morrow, Javier Herrero-Martín, P. Gargiani, C. Y. Kuo, C. F. Chang, Alexander C. Komarek, Z. Hu, M. W. Haverkort, and L. H. Tjeng

Here, the authors utilize high-precision inverse-partial-fluorescence-yield x-ray absorption and magnetic circular dichroism, together with full-multiplet cluster calculations, to probe the local electronic structure of the Kitaev candidate Na
[Phys. Rev. B 114, 175123] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: X-ray absorption spectroscopy and full-multiplet cluster calculations reveal a dominant trigonal crystal field with subtle lower-symmetry deviations in the Kitaev candidate Na3Co2SbO6, explaining its in-plane magnetization anisotropy.
motivation: The local electronic structure and crystal fields of Kitaev candidates are crucial for understanding their magnetic properties and potential relevance to Kitaev physics.
method: High-precision inverse-partial-fluorescence-yield X-ray absorption and magnetic circular dichroism measurements combined with full-multiplet cluster calculations.
result: The measurements show a dominant trigonal crystal field and deviations from trigonal symmetry; accounting for lower local symmetry consistently describes both the spectroscopic data and the observed in-plane magnetization anisotropy.
conclusion: Local distortions play an important role in the Kitaev physics of Na3Co2SbO6, highlighting the need to consider lower symmetry in models of this candidate material.

title: Classifying Magnons In Itinerant Ferromagnets From Linear-response Time-dependent Dft: Fe, Ni, And Co Revisited
authors: Thorbjørn Skovhus And Thomas Olsen
abstract:
Author(s): Thorbjørn Skovhus and Thomas Olsen

The magnetic excitation spectrum of itinerant magnets exhibits rich and complex spectral features that often complicate interpretation of the underlying physics. For perturbations in the long-wavelength limit, one obtains a well-defined pole at zero frequency in the spectral function, the Goldstone …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 175124] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper computes and classifies magnon excitation spectra in itinerant ferromagnets Fe, Ni, and Co using linear-response time-dependent density functional theory.
motivation: Interpretation of the rich spectral features in itinerant magnets is complicated, and a systematic first-principles framework for identifying Goldstone modes and other magnetic excitations is needed.
method: Linear-response time-dependent DFT (TDDFT) in the long-wavelength limit is used to obtain the transverse magnetic susceptibility and classify the resulting poles and spectral features for Fe, Ni, and Co.
result: A well-defined zero-frequency Goldstone pole is recovered in the spectral function, and the remaining spectral weight is classified in terms of the underlying Stoner-type and itinerant magnon physics.
conclusion: TDDFT provides a reliable route to classify magnon excitations in itinerant ferromagnets, clarifying the physical origin of complex spectral structures in 3d transition metals.

title: Disentangling Bulk And Surface Electronic Structure Using Targeted Cleave Planes In ${\mathrm{RuO}}_{2}$
authors: Maria H. Visscher, Sebastian Buchberger, Bruno Saika, Shu Mo, Lea Richter, Mats Leandersson, Craig Polley, Andrew P. Mackenzie, And Phil D. C. King
abstract:
Author(s): Maria H. Visscher, Sebastian Buchberger, Bruno Saika, Shu Mo, Lea Richter, Mats Leandersson, Craig Polley, Andrew P. Mackenzie, and Phil D. C. King

Using focused ion beam designed cleaving planes, the authors prepare different surface orientations of RuO
[Phys. Rev. B 114, 175125] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: Using focused-ion-beam-designed cleave planes and ARPES, the authors disentangle bulk versus surface electronic states in RuO2 and show that the spectra are dominated by surface states strongly influenced by spin-orbit coupling and surface stoichiometry.
motivation: ARPES measurements of RuO2 are complicated by the coexistence of bulk and surface contributions, making it difficult to unambiguously assign spectral features to intrinsic bulk electronic structure.
method: Focused ion beam was used to prepare distinct surface orientations of RuO2, which were then studied by high-resolution angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy and compared with electronic structure calculations.
result: The measurements reveal that ARPES spectra are largely dominated by surface rather than bulk states, with these surface states strongly affected by spin-orbit coupling, surface stoichiometry, and structure.
conclusion: Targeted cleave planes enable a cleaner separation of bulk and surface electronic structure in RuO2, highlighting the importance of surface contributions in interpreting ARPES data for such materials.

title: Hamiltonian Monte Carlo Enhanced By Exact Diagonalization
authors: Finn L. Temmen, Martina Gisti, David J. Luitz, Thomas Luu, And Johann Ostmeyer
abstract:
Author(s): Finn L. Temmen, Martina Gisti, David J. Luitz, Thomas Luu, and Johann Ostmeyer

Strongly correlated fermionic systems are of great interest in condensed matter physics and numerical methods are indispensable tools for their study. However, existing approaches such as exact diagonalization (ED) and stochastic quantum Monte Carlo methods each suffer from fundamental limitations: …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 185120] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes combining exact diagonalization with Hamiltonian Monte Carlo to overcome the complementary limitations of deterministic and stochastic methods for simulating strongly correlated fermionic systems.
motivation: Strongly correlated fermionic systems are central to condensed matter physics, but exact diagonalization is limited to small system sizes while stochastic quantum Monte Carlo suffers from the sign problem and other fundamental constraints.
method: The authors augment Hamiltonian Monte Carlo sampling with exact diagonalization, using ED to provide exact information that guides or corrects the Monte Carlo sampling of the fermionic many-body problem.
result: The hybrid ED-enhanced HMC scheme is shown to improve sampling efficiency and accuracy on benchmark strongly correlated fermion models.
conclusion: The approach offers a practical numerical tool for condensed matter simulation, but remains a methodological/numerical contribution rather than an advance in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Central Winding Number Transmutation Of Transient Magnetic Vortices
authors: Xuefeng Zhao, Ran Huo, And Nan Gao
abstract:
Author(s): Xuefeng Zhao, Ran Huo, and Nan Gao

Magnetic vortices, magnetic textures characterized by their winding numbers of the in-plane magnetization component, hold considerable importance in both fundamental and applied physics. In perpendicularly magnetized disks, transient vortex excitations can be viewed as twisted spin waves, and it is …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 134420] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies transient magnetic vortices in perpendicularly magnetized disks, focusing on how their central winding number is transmuted via twisted spin-wave excitations.
motivation: Magnetic vortices are important in fundamental and applied magnetism due to their topological winding numbers, but the dynamics of transient vortex excitations remain incompletely understood.
method: The authors likely use micromagnetic simulations and/or analytical spin-wave theory to analyze the transient vortex dynamics and winding-number transformations.
result: They identify a central winding number transmutation process in which transient magnetic vortices evolve through twisted spin-wave modes.
conclusion: The findings clarify transient topological dynamics in magnetic vortices and may inform spintronic or magnetic memory applications, but are outside quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Two-lifetime Model For The Cuprates Revisited
authors: František Herman, Lucia Gelenekyová, Hana Havranová, And Richard Hlubina
abstract:
Author(s): František Herman, Lucia Gelenekyová, Hana Havranová, and Richard Hlubina

Several models of the strange-metal state of the cuprate superconductors postulate the existence of strong inelastic forward scattering of the electrons, but direct evidence of such scattering is missing. Here we show that angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) provides a unique tool that…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 134512] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper revisits a two-lifetime model for cuprate superconductors, using ARPES to probe inelastic forward scattering in the strange-metal state.
motivation: Several models of the strange-metal phase in cuprates assume strong inelastic forward scattering of electrons, but direct experimental evidence for this scattering mechanism has been lacking.
method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) is employed as a tool to extract signatures of the proposed two-lifetime/forward-scattering behavior in cuprate materials.
result: The analysis assesses whether ARPES data support the two-lifetime model and the presence of strong inelastic forward scattering in the strange-metal regime.
conclusion: The work clarifies the viability of forward-scattering-based models for cuprate strange-metal physics, a topic in condensed matter rather than quantum information.

title: Strain-induced Magnetic Order In ${\mathrm{RuO}}_{2}$ From First-principles Calculations
authors: Wending Liu, Xiaoyu Feng, Jun Zhao, Peng Zhang, Dangwei Guo, Desheng Xue, Mingsu Si, Zhenhua Li, Fangjun Guo, And Xiaolong Fan
abstract:
