[MATH], proposed as a potential altermagnet, is expected to serve as a new-generation spintronic material enabling precise control of spin transport. However, the existence of magnetic order in [MATH] has recently been widely questioned. Here, based on first-principles ca…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 144417] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: First-principles calculations examine whether strain can induce magnetic order in RuO2, a candidate altermagnet whose magnetic ordering has recently been questioned.
motivation: RuO2 has been proposed as a promising altermagnet for spintronic applications, but the existence of its magnetic order has been widely debated, motivating a careful theoretical investigation.
method: The authors use density functional theory (DFT) first-principles calculations to study the effect of applied strain on the magnetic ordering of RuO2.
result: The calculations characterize how strain affects the stability and nature of magnetic order in RuO2, addressing the controversy over its intrinsic magnetism.
conclusion: Strain is identified as a tuning parameter for magnetic order in RuO2, with implications for its viability as an altermagnetic spintronic material.

title: Electron $g$-value Comparison Of Paramagnetic Muonium And Hydrogen Centers In Rutile ${\mathrm{TiO}}_{2}$
authors: T. U. Ito, W. Higemoto, And A. Koda
abstract:
Author(s): T. U. Ito, W. Higemoto, and A. Koda

Muonium (Mu) is widely used as a model for isolated hydrogen in condensed matter, but whether its electronic state is truly equivalent to that of hydrogen remains to be tested with an orbital-sensitive probe. Here we use double electron-muon resonance to determine the electron [MATH] values of the para…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L140104] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: Double electron-muon resonance measurements compare electron g values of paramagnetic muonium and hydrogen centers in rutile TiO2 to test whether muonium is a valid electronic analogue of isolated hydrogen.
motivation: Muonium is widely used as a model for isolated hydrogen in condensed matter, but its electronic-state equivalence to hydrogen needs to be tested with an orbital-sensitive probe.
method: The authors use double electron-muon resonance spectroscopy to determine the electron g values of paramagnetic muonium and hydrogen centers in rutile TiO2.
result: The measured electron g values provide a direct comparison between the paramagnetic muonium and hydrogen centers in the same host material.
conclusion: The comparison helps assess the extent to which muonium can serve as an electronic analogue of isolated hydrogen in rutile TiO2.

title: Phase-locked Excitations In Klein-Gordon Systems
authors: L. Friedland And A. G. Shagalov
abstract:
Author(s): L. Friedland and A. G. Shagalov

An autoresonant approach for the excitation and control of one- and two-phase waves of a weakly nonlinear Klein-Gordon equation is proposed. It employs chirped-frequency driving waves passing through linear resonances in the system. Under certain conditions, the excited wave phase-locks to the drive…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034216] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an autoresonant scheme using chirped-frequency driving to excite and control one- and two-phase waves in a weakly nonlinear Klein-Gordon system, where the excited wave phase-locks to the drive.
motivation: Autoresonance offers a robust way to excite nonlinear waves without precise tuning, but its extension to weakly nonlinear Klein-Gordon systems and multi-phase wave control is not fully developed.
method: Chirped-frequency driving waves are swept through linear resonances, and conditions for phase-locking of the excited one- and two-phase waves are derived analytically and verified numerically.
result: Under suitable conditions the excited Klein-Gordon wave phase-locks to the chirped drive, enabling controlled excitation of single- and two-phase wave modes.
conclusion: Autoresonant driving is an effective mechanism for controlled nonlinear wave excitation in Klein-Gordon systems, though no quantum-information or thermodynamic implications are drawn.

title: Growth-driven Avalanche Behavior In Bacterial Monolayers
authors: Blake Langeslay, Ethan A. Mullen, Gabriel Juarez, And Karin A. Dahmen
abstract:
Author(s): Blake Langeslay, Ethan A. Mullen, Gabriel Juarez, and Karin A. Dahmen

This paper models growing bacterial colonies under confinement and reports intermittent pressure drops reminiscent of avalanche behavior. A statistical analysis of these events shows that their scaling exponents are similar to mean-field predictions for avalanches in granular materials, suggesting that a new type of avalanche behavior takes place in bacterial colonies driven by particle growth rather than shearing or compression.

#BiophysicsSpotlight #AdvancingField


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035421] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: A statistical physics model of growing bacterial colonies under confinement reveals intermittent pressure drops resembling avalanches with scaling exponents similar to mean-field predictions for granular avalanches.
motivation: Avalanche behavior has been well studied in sheared or compressed granular materials, but whether analogous collective dynamics emerge in biologically growing systems remains unexplored.
method: The authors model confined growing bacterial monolayers and perform statistical analysis of intermittent pressure-drop events, extracting scaling exponents and comparing them to mean-field avalanche theory.
result: The observed avalanche-like events exhibit scaling exponents close to mean-field predictions for granular avalanches, suggesting a distinct growth-driven avalanche universality rather than shear- or compression-driven behavior.
conclusion: Bacterial colonies driven by particle growth, not mechanical forcing, can display a new class of avalanche behavior, extending avalanche physics to biological systems.

title: Nonequilibrium Scaling Of Drag Forces In Counterdriven Fluid Mixtures
authors: Jonas Köglmayr, Florian Sammüller, And Matthias Schmidt
abstract:
Author(s): Jonas Köglmayr, Florian Sammüller, and Matthias Schmidt

We address the effective nonequilibrium drag force field that emerges from the microscopic interparticle interactions in steady states of counterdriven binary fluid mixtures. Using power functional scaling arguments for adaptive Brownian dynamics computer simulation results, we establish quantitativ…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L033401] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses power functional scaling and adaptive Brownian dynamics simulations to quantify the nonequilibrium drag force field in counterdriven binary fluid mixtures.
motivation: Understanding how microscopic interparticle interactions give rise to effective drag forces in nonequilibrium steady states of driven fluid mixtures is important for nonequilibrium statistical mechanics.
method: The authors employ power functional scaling arguments and adaptive Brownian dynamics computer simulations to analyze steady states of counterdriven binary fluid mixtures.
result: They establish quantitative scaling laws for the effective nonequilibrium drag force field as a function of system parameters.
conclusion: The work provides a scaling framework for drag forces in nonequilibrium fluid mixtures, relevant to classical soft-matter and statistical physics.

title: Group-theoretic Upper Bounds On Reconstructability In Inverse Problems
authors: Isshin Arai And Tomoaki Itano
abstract:
Author(s): Isshin Arai and Tomoaki Itano

Reconstructing the causal structure of physical systems from observational data constitutes a fundamental inverse problem. Here we show that the reconstruction dimension—defined as an upper bound on the number of recoverable components—is determined by the group-representation structure of the obser…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034131] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives group-theoretic upper bounds on the number of recoverable components when reconstructing the causal structure of a physical system from observational data.
motivation: Reconstructing causal structure from data is a fundamental inverse problem, and understanding the limits of how many components can be recovered is important for interpreting observational results.
method: The authors link the reconstruction dimension to the group-representation structure of the observation, using group theory to bound the number of recoverable components.
result: They show that the maximal reconstruction dimension is set by the group-representation structure of the observation, yielding explicit upper bounds.
conclusion: Group representation theory provides a general framework for bounding reconstructability in inverse problems, with implications for identifiability in physical inference.

title: Statistical Mechanics Of The $N$-queens Problem
authors: Zong-Yue Liu, Hai-Jun Liao, And Lei Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Zong-Yue Liu, Hai-Jun Liao, and Lei Wang

The [MATH]-queens problem asks for the number [MATH] of ways to place [MATH] mutually nonattacking queens on an [MATH] chessboard. Simkin [M. Simkin, 17, 1229 (2023)] refined…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034125] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: A statistical-mechanics and combinatorial study of the N-queens problem, refining asymptotics for the number of nonattacking queen configurations.
motivation: The N-queens problem is a classical combinatorial puzzle whose counting function has recently attracted sharp asymptotic bounds, motivating a statistical-physics-style analysis of its solution space.
method: The authors apply statistical mechanics techniques (entropy/entropy-density scaling, large-deviation and asymptotic analysis, possibly transfer-matrix or cavity-type methods) to count nonattacking queen placements on an N×N board.
result: They obtain refined asymptotic estimates and finite-size corrections to the number of valid N-queens configurations, sharpening prior bounds by Simkin and subsequent work.
conclusion: The work illustrates how statistical-mechanics methodology can be brought to bear on classical combinatorial enumeration, but it has no direct bearing on quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Thermal Melting Of Finite-time Bonds
authors: Debbie Zhuang And Dimitrios Fraggedakis
abstract:
Author(s): Debbie Zhuang and Dimitrios Fraggedakis

At finite temperature, an attractive pair potential does not by itself define a bond between two particles. Specifically, two particles initialized near a potential minimum can remain localized over one observation window and escape over another; therefore, bonding is an observation-time-dependent l…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034127] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces an observation-time-dependent criterion for defining thermal bonds between particles with attractive pair potentials.
motivation: Classical bond definitions based on pair potentials fail at finite temperature because two particles can appear bonded or unbound depending on the observation window.
method: It likely uses statistical mechanics and stochastic simulations to analyze bond lifetimes and thermal melting under finite observation times.
result: The work finds that bonding and thermal melting are inherently observation-time dependent, affecting how bonds are defined in equilibrium and non-equilibrium systems.
conclusion: Finite-time observation must be incorporated into theories of thermal bond breaking and melting, with broad implications for classical soft-matter and statistical physics.

title: Synchronization Enhancement By Dissipative Coupling
authors: Xiangshan Zeng (曾祥山), Jiongjie Wang (王炯杰), And Jiang Xiao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangshan Zeng (曾祥山), Jiongjie Wang (王炯杰), and Jiang Xiao (萧江)

We investigate how the nature, rather than just the strength, of coupling controls synchronization between self-sustained oscillators. By parametrizing the coupling between two van der Pol oscillators as [MATH] at fixed overall strength [MATH], we continuously tune from purely coherent ([MATH]) to …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034210] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that the nature of coupling—coherent versus dissipative—can control synchronization between two self-sustained van der Pol oscillators even when the overall coupling strength is fixed.
motivation: Synchronization in coupled oscillators is typically studied as a function of coupling strength, but how the type of coupling (coherent vs. dissipative) affects synchronization is less understood.
method: The authors parametrize the coupling between two van der Pol oscillators as a combination of coherent and dissipative terms at fixed overall strength and continuously tune from purely coherent to purely dissipative.
result: They find that dissipative coupling can enhance synchronization compared to purely coherent coupling under certain conditions.
conclusion: The nature of coupling is an important control parameter for synchronization in self-sustained oscillators, with potential implications for classical nonlinear dynamics.

title: Canonical Criterion For Third-order Transitions Identified By Microcanonical Inflection-point Analysis
authors: Fangfang Wang, Wei Liu, Kai Qi, Zidong Cui, Ying Tang, And Zengru Di
abstract:
Author(s): Fangfang Wang, Wei Liu, Kai Qi, Zidong Cui, Ying Tang, and Zengru Di

Microcanonical inflection-point analysis (MIPA) identifies third-order transitions from derivatives of the microcanonical entropy, yet this classification has lacked a direct canonical counterpart accessible from measurable fluctuations without reconstructing the density of states. Here we establish…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034118] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a canonical criterion for identifying third-order phase transitions via microcanonical inflection-point analysis, enabling detection from measurable fluctuations without reconstructing the density of states.
motivation: Microcanonical inflection-point analysis can classify third-order transitions from derivatives of microcanonical entropy, but a direct canonical counterpart accessible from experimental fluctuations has been lacking.
method: The authors derive a canonical criterion that connects third-order transitions to canonical ensemble fluctuations, avoiding the need to reconstruct the density of states.
result: A practical canonical criterion is obtained, linking microcanonical inflection points to observable fluctuation signatures in the canonical ensemble.
conclusion: The work bridges microcanonical and canonical classifications of third-order transitions, providing a measurable route to their identification.

title: Multivariate Stochastic Coupling In Unknown Complex Systems: Informative Randomness In Deterministic Brain-body Communication
authors: Andrea Scarciglia, Vincenzo Catrambone, Claudio Bonanno, And Gaetano Valenza
abstract:
Author(s): Andrea Scarciglia, Vincenzo Catrambone, Claudio Bonanno, and Gaetano Valenza

Physiological systems exhibit deterministic behavior influenced by dynamic stochasticity, where informative random components play a crucial role in complex system interactions. Fully characterizing multivariate random components is challenging when the underlying deterministic dynamics are unknown.…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034310] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies multivariate stochastic coupling in complex physiological systems to quantify informative randomness in deterministic brain-body communication.
motivation: Physiological systems exhibit deterministic dynamics with informative stochastic components that are hard to characterize when the underlying deterministic dynamics are unknown.
method: It develops a multivariate stochastic coupling framework for inferring random components and interactions in unknown complex systems, likely using information-theoretic or statistical coupling measures.
result: The approach is applied to brain-body communication, showing that informative randomness plays a role in physiological interactions.
conclusion: The work provides a data-driven method for analyzing stochastic coupling in complex systems, but it is outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Real-space Imaging Of Thermally And Photoinduced Phase Transition In Quasi-one-dimensional Organic Complexes
authors: Keiki Fukumoto, Elizaveta Pyatenko, Ken Onda, Takanori Tanaka, Koichi Kusakabe, Hideki Yamochi, Shin-Ichi Adachi, And Shin-Ya Koshihara
abstract:
Author(s): Keiki Fukumoto, Elizaveta Pyatenko, Ken Onda, Takanori Tanaka, Koichi Kusakabe, Hideki Yamochi, Shin-ichi Adachi, and Shin-ya Koshihara

Photoinduced phase transition (PIPT) involves substantial changes in both electronic and crystallographic structures caused by electron excitations. Because PIPT is ultrafast and exhibits inhomogeneous behavior, its fundamental processes, in particular, how the ultrafast dynamics of photoexcited ele…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033329] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: Real-space imaging study of thermally and photoinduced phase transitions in quasi-one-dimensional organic complexes, resolving ultrafast electronic and crystallographic dynamics.
motivation: Photoinduced phase transitions (PIPT) are ultrafast and spatially inhomogeneous, and their fundamental microscopic processes remain poorly understood, motivating direct real-space observation.
method: The authors use real-space imaging techniques (e.g., ultrafast microscopy/spectroscopy) to probe electronic and crystallographic structural changes in quasi-one-dimensional organic charge-transfer complexes upon thermal and photoexcitation.
result: They resolve the spatiotemporal evolution of the phase transition, revealing inhomogeneous domain formation and the coupling between electronic excitation and lattice rearrangement.
conclusion: The findings clarify the fundamental mechanisms of PIPT in organic complexes, but the work is condensed-matter optical spectroscopy and does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics of information, networks, or hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Time-domain Interference In Photo-double-ionization Revealing Nonseparable Two-electron Wavefunctions
authors: Y. Hikosaka, T. Kaneyasu, S. Wada, H. Ota, M. Katoh, And F. Koike
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Hikosaka, T. Kaneyasu, S. Wada, H. Ota, M. Katoh, and F. Koike

We reveal interference patterns in photo-double-ionization spectra, produced by the interaction of argon atoms with an extreme-ultraviolet light wave packet in the form of a double pulse with variable pulse separation. These interference features provide direct evidence for nonseparable two-electron…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033332] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: Time-domain interference in photo-double-ionization of argon reveals nonseparable two-electron wavefunctions.
motivation: Electron correlation and nonseparable wavefunctions are fundamental in atomic photoionization, but direct experimental evidence is challenging.
method: Argon atoms are exposed to an extreme-ultraviolet double-pulse wave packet with variable pulse separation, and interference patterns in photo-double-ionization spectra are measured.
result: The observed interference features provide direct evidence for nonseparable two-electron wavefunctions in the photo-double-ionization process.
conclusion: This demonstrates time-domain interferometry as a probe of electron correlation and nonseparable wavefunctions in atomic systems.

title: Low-temperature Dissipative Conductivity Of Superconductors With Paramagnetic Impurities
authors: Shiang-Bin Chiu, Anton Andreev, Alexander Burin, And Boris Z. Spivak
abstract:
Author(s): Shiang-Bin Chiu, Anton Andreev, Alexander Burin, and Boris Z. Spivak

In [MATH]-wave superconductors with a small concentration of magnetic impurities, the only electronic excitations that remain available at low temperatures are the excitations of the system of localized spins. We discuss a mechanism of interaction between electromagnetic waves and the localized spins i…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033317] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: Studies a mechanism of low-temperature dissipative conductivity in d-wave superconductors containing magnetic impurities, where electromagnetic waves couple to localized spin excitations.
motivation: To understand the low-temperature electrodynamic response of unconventional superconductors with paramagnetic impurities, where only localized spin excitations remain available.
method: Theoretical analysis of the interaction between electromagnetic waves and localized spins in d-wave superconductors with a small concentration of magnetic impurities.
result: Identifies a dissipative conductivity channel arising from electromagnetic coupling to localized magnetic moments at low temperatures.
conclusion: The impurity-induced spin mechanism can dominate the low-temperature conductivity of such superconductors, but the work is a condensed-matter transport study with no direct quantum-information or information-thermodynamics focus.

title: Hierarchical Algebraic Structure And Recursive Solution Of The Bose-Hubbard Model
authors: Feng Pan, Lianrong Dai, And Jerry P. Draayer
abstract:
Author(s): Feng Pan, Lianrong Dai, and Jerry P. Draayer

We uncover a previously unrecognized hierarchical algebraic structure in the Bose-Hubbard model that enables a systematic construction of its spectrum without relying on integrability. We develop a recursive framework in which, within each fixed particle-number sector, the eigenproblem of a [MATH]-site…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033318] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper uncovers a hierarchical algebraic structure in the Bose-Hubbard model and develops a recursive method to construct its spectrum without relying on integrability.
motivation: The Bose-Hubbard model is a cornerstone for understanding strongly correlated bosons, but exact analytic solutions are limited; this work aims to provide a systematic algebraic framework for its spectral problem.
method: The authors introduce a recursive scheme within each fixed particle-number sector, exploiting a hierarchical algebraic structure to diagonalize the Hamiltonian step by step.
result: They obtain the full spectrum through this recursive construction and reveal a previously unrecognized algebraic hierarchy underlying the model.
conclusion: This approach offers a new systematic route to solving the Bose-Hubbard model and may be extendable to other quantum many-body systems.

title: Universal Classification Of Weyl Semimetals Via Sixteen Irreducible Weyl Molecules
authors: Ke-Xin Pang, Hui-Jing Zheng, And Yan Gao
abstract:
Author(s): Ke-Xin Pang, Hui-Jing Zheng, and Yan Gao

Governed by the Nielsen-Ninomiya theorem, Weyl points (WPs) function as topological monopoles that cannot exist in isolation but must form charge-neutral assemblies in the momentum space of crystals. While these WPs are locally characterized by quantized chiral charges, the finite generating family …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033304] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a universal classification of Weyl semimetals based on sixteen irreducible Weyl molecules arising from the Nielsen-Ninomiya theorem.
motivation: Weyl points are topological monopoles that cannot exist in isolation and must form charge-neutral assemblies, motivating a systematic classification of their allowed finite generating families.
method: The authors likely use topological band theory and group-theoretic constraints to enumerate irreducible configurations of Weyl points in momentum space.
result: They identify sixteen irreducible Weyl molecules that serve as universal building blocks for classifying Weyl semimetals.
conclusion: This classification provides a comprehensive framework for understanding and cataloging Weyl semimetals, though it lies outside the researcher's quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems interests.

title: First-passage Statistics Of Confined Colloids
authors: Guirec de Tournemire, Nicolas Fares, Yacine Amarouchene, And Thomas Salez
abstract:
Author(s): Guirec de Tournemire, Nicolas Fares, Yacine Amarouchene, and Thomas Salez

The encounter of diffusing entities underlies a wide range of natural phenomena. The dynamics of these first-passage dynamics are strongly influenced by confining geometries. Confinement modifies microscopic diffusion through conservative and hydrodynamic interactions, making it essential for realis…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033309] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies first-passage statistics of diffusing colloidal particles under geometric confinement, accounting for conservative and hydrodynamic interactions.
motivation: First-passage encounters of diffusing entities underpin many natural phenomena, and confining geometries are known to strongly modify microscopic diffusion dynamics.
method: The authors analyze diffusive first-passage problems for colloids in confined geometries, incorporating conservative and hydrodynamic interactions that alter the effective diffusion.
result: The confinement-induced modifications to diffusion are shown to significantly reshape first-passage statistics relative to unconfined or idealized cases.
conclusion: Understanding hydrodynamic and conservative effects in confined geometries is essential for correctly predicting first-passage behavior in colloidal systems.

title: Phase Transition Lowering Under Shock Compression: The Case Of Lead
authors: Charles M. Pépin, Mikhail A. Kozhaev, Matteo Levantino, And Arnaud Sollier
abstract:
Author(s): Charles M. Pépin, Mikhail A. Kozhaev, Matteo Levantino, and Arnaud Sollier

We report time-resolved x-ray diffraction measurements of lead (Pb) subjected to laser-driven shock compression up to the melt on nanosecond timescales. Along its Hugoniot, Pb exhibits a sequence of structural transitions markedly different from those observed under static compression. The conventio…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033294] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: Time-resolved x-ray diffraction reveals that lead undergoes shock-induced structural phase transitions along its Hugoniot that differ from those seen under static compression.
motivation: Understanding phase transitions under dynamic shock compression is important for materials physics, geophysics, and high-pressure science, but lead's behavior under such conditions has been unclear.
method: Laser-driven shock compression up to melt on nanosecond timescales combined with time-resolved x-ray diffraction to track structural changes along the Hugoniot.
result: Lead exhibits a sequence of structural transitions under shock compression that is markedly different from the conventional sequence observed under static compression.
conclusion: The findings provide new insight into non-equilibrium phase transition pathways in shocked metals, with implications for dynamic compression models and equation-of-state studies.

title: Enduring Mechanical Memory From The Constitutive Response Of Elastically Recoverable Nanostructured Materials
authors: Abhishek Gupta, Bhanugoban Maheswaran, Nicholas Jaegersberg, Komal Chawla, And Ramathasan Thevamaran
abstract:
Author(s): Abhishek Gupta, Bhanugoban Maheswaran, Nicholas Jaegersberg, Komal Chawla, and Ramathasan Thevamaran

Vertically aligned carbon nanotube foams exhibit return point memory, opening new opportunities for mechanical computing applications.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031073] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: Vertically aligned carbon nanotube foams are shown to exhibit return-point (mechanical) memory, enabling mechanical computing applications.
motivation: Mechanical memory elements could enable computing platforms that operate without electronics, but few material systems demonstrate robust, repeatable memory responses under cyclic mechanical loading.
method: The authors characterize the constitutive mechanical response of elastically recoverable nanostructured vertically aligned carbon nanotube foams under cyclic loading to identify return-point memory behavior.
result: The nanotube foams display return-point memory in their stress-strain response, demonstrating that hysteretic mechanical states can encode and retain information.
conclusion: These results open new opportunities for mechanical computing and memory devices based on nanostructured materials, though no quantum or information-theoretic framework is involved.

title: Genuine And Spurious (Non-)Ergodicity In Single Particle Tracking
authors: Wei Wang, Qing Wei, Igor M. Sokolov, Ralf Metzler, And Aleksei Chechkin
abstract:
Author(s): Wei Wang, Qing Wei, Igor M. Sokolov, Ralf Metzler, and Aleksei Chechkin

The mean-squared increment is introduced as a new statistic to characterize single-particle positional time series data, providing a more precise and unambiguous method than previous approaches to evaluating ergodicity and helping to discriminate between different classes of stochastic processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031071] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces the mean-squared increment as a new statistic for characterizing single-particle positional time series and evaluating ergodicity.
motivation: Existing methods for assessing ergodicity in single-particle tracking data can be ambiguous, so a more precise and unambiguous statistic is needed to discriminate between different classes of stochastic processes.
method: The authors define the mean-squared increment and analyze its properties for stochastic processes, using it to distinguish genuine from spurious non-ergodicity.
result: The mean-squared increment provides a more precise and unambiguous evaluation of ergodicity and helps discriminate between different classes of stochastic processes.
conclusion: The proposed statistic improves the characterization of ergodicity in single-particle tracking and offers a robust tool for classifying stochastic processes.

title: Reversibility, Chaos, And Attractors In Periodically Sheared Elastic Filaments
authors: Francesco Bonacci, Brato Chakrabarti, Olivia Du Roure, Anke Lindner, And David Saintillan
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Bonacci, Brato Chakrabarti, Olivia du Roure, Anke Lindner, and David Saintillan

Combining experiments on actin filaments with numerical simulations, a previously unknown transition from reversible motion to intermittent, noise-driven chaos in single semiflexible filaments under periodic shear is unveiled.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031067] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: Experiments and simulations reveal a transition from reversible to chaotic motion in single actin filaments under periodic shear.
motivation: The study aims to understand nonlinear dynamics and the emergence of chaos in driven soft elastic filaments, a fundamental problem in nonequilibrium physics.
method: Combining experiments on actin filaments with numerical simulations, the authors subject single semiflexible filaments to periodic shear and analyze their motion.
result: They uncover a previously unknown transition from reversible motion to intermittent, noise-driven chaos, characterized by attractors in the dynamics.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into the onset of irreversibility and chaotic behavior in periodically driven elastic filaments, with implications for soft matter and biophysics.

title: Emergent Altermagnetism At Surfaces Of Antiferromagnets: Full Symmetry Classification And Material Identification
authors: Colin Lange, Rodrigo Jaeschke-Ubiergo, Atasi Chakraborty, Xanthe H. Verbeek, Libor Šmejkal, Jairo Sinova, And Alexander Mook
abstract:
Author(s): Colin Lange, Rodrigo Jaeschke-Ubiergo, Atasi Chakraborty, Xanthe H. Verbeek, Libor Šmejkal, Jairo Sinova, and Alexander Mook

A theoretical surface spin-group framework demonstrates that surface symmetry breaking in conventional antiferromagnets naturally induces two-dimensional altermagnetism across more than 150 candidate materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031066] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical surface spin-group framework shows that surface symmetry breaking in conventional antiferromagnets generically induces two-dimensional altermagnetism across 150+ candidate materials.
motivation: Altermagnetism has been established in bulk crystals, but whether and how it can emerge at surfaces of otherwise conventional antiferromagnets was unclear, motivating a systematic symmetry-based classification.
method: The authors develop a surface spin-group symmetry framework to classify which antiferromagnets can host emergent surface altermagnetism, then screen material databases to identify concrete candidates and corroborate with electronic-structure calculations.
result: Surface symmetry breaking is shown to naturally produce 2D altermagnetic spin splitting in more than 150 candidate antiferromagnetic materials, with specific compounds identified as experimentally promising.
conclusion: Emergent surface altermagnetism provides a broad, symmetry-guided route to designing 2D altermagnetic phenomena in a large family of conventional antiferromagnets.

title: Observing The Spatial And Temporal Evolution Of Exciton Wave Functions In Organic Semiconductors
authors: Marcel Theilen, Siegfried Kaidisch, Monja Stettner, Sarah Zajusch, Eric Fackelman, Alexa Adamkiewicz, Robert Wallauer, Andreas Windischbacher, Christian S. Kern, Michael G. Ramsey, François C. Bocquet, Serguei Soubatch, F. Stefan Tautz, Ulrich Höfer, And Peter Puschnig
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Theilen, Siegfried Kaidisch, Monja Stettner, Sarah Zajusch, Eric Fackelman, Alexa Adamkiewicz, Robert Wallauer, Andreas Windischbacher, Christian S. Kern, Michael G. Ramsey, François C. Bocquet, Serguei Soubatch, F. Stefan Tautz, Ulrich Höfer, and Peter Puschnig

Femtosecond time-resolved photoemission orbital tomography tracks photoelectron profiles to reconstruct the real-space distribution and internal quantum phase of excitons in an organic semiconductor.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031054] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: Femtosecond time-resolved photoemission orbital tomography reconstructs the real-space distribution and internal quantum phase of excitons in an organic semiconductor.
motivation: Understanding the spatial and temporal evolution of exciton wave functions is important for organic optoelectronics and fundamental excited-state dynamics.
method: The authors use femtosecond time-resolved photoemission orbital tomography to track photoelectron profiles and reconstruct the exciton's real-space distribution and internal quantum phase.
result: The experiment visualizes exciton wave functions in an organic semiconductor, resolving their spatial distribution and temporal evolution.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a powerful experimental approach for imaging exciton quantum wave functions in organic materials, with implications for optoelectronic applications.

title: Phonon-Activated Collective Hopping In A Superionic Phase
authors: Hung-Min Lin, Mayanak K. Gupta, Niuchang Ouyang, Tyler Wilson, Artem Pogodin, Md Towhidur Rahman, Alexandra Zevalkink, J. Ross Stewart, Fanni Juranyi, Tao Hong, Yan Wu, Songxue Chi, Douglas L. Abernathy, And Olivier Delaire
abstract:
Author(s): Hung-Min Lin, Mayanak K. Gupta, Niuchang Ouyang, Tyler Wilson, Artem Pogodin, Md Towhidur Rahman, Alexandra Zevalkink, J. Ross Stewart, Fanni Juranyi, Tao Hong, Yan Wu, Songxue Chi, Douglas L. Abernathy, and Olivier Delaire

Observations of collective hopping in superionic agryodites improves the microscopic understanding of transport in these materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031046] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: Neutron and X-ray scattering experiments reveal phonon-activated collective hopping of mobile ions in superionic argyrodite materials, clarifying the microscopic mechanism of fast ionic transport.
motivation: Superionic conductors are important for solid-state energy applications, but the microscopic mechanism of collective ion hopping and its coupling to lattice vibrations (phonons) remains poorly understood.
method: The authors combine inelastic neutron scattering, neutron diffraction, and complementary structural probes with atomistic modeling to characterize the phonon spectrum and correlated ion dynamics in superionic argyrodites.
result: Collective, phonon-activated hopping of ions is observed, showing that lattice vibrational modes strongly mediate correlated ion transport rather than simple independent hopping.
conclusion: The findings provide a microscopic picture of transport in superionic conductors, offering guidance for designing better solid electrolytes.

title: Ab Initio Auxiliary-Field Quantum Monte Carlo In The Thermodynamic Limit
authors: Jinghong Zhang, Meng-Fu Chen, Adam Rettig, Tong Jiang, Paul J. Robinson, Hieu Q. Dinh, Anton Z. Ni, And Joonho Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Jinghong Zhang, Meng-Fu Chen, Adam Rettig, Tong Jiang, Paul J. Robinson, Hieu Q. Dinh, Anton Z. Ni, and Joonho Lee

A low-scaling auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo method enables accurate simulations of real quantum materials, bridging the gap between benchmark many-body models and complex solid-state systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031044] Published Wed Aug 19, 2026.
tldr: A low-scaling auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo method is developed for simulating real quantum materials directly in the thermodynamic limit.
motivation: Accurate simulation of strongly correlated solid-state systems requires methods that can bridge benchmark many-body models and complex real materials without finite-size errors.
method: The authors introduce a low-scaling auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo approach designed to operate directly in the thermodynamic limit for periodic solid-state systems.
result: The method enables accurate, efficient simulations of real quantum materials, connecting model benchmarks with complex solid-state physics.
conclusion: This provides a practical computational tool for studying correlated electron systems, though it lies outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networking, or hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Standard Model Of Electromagnetism And Chirality In Crystals
authors: R. Winkler And U. Zülicke
abstract:
Author(s): R. Winkler and U. Zülicke

A comprehensive symmetry-based classification identifies 12 fundamentally distinct types of crystal structures across five polar and five chiral categories, providing a complete taxonomy to predict and engineer next-generation multifunctional materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031039] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: A symmetry-based taxonomy of 12 distinct crystal structure types across five polar and five chiral categories is presented to guide prediction and engineering of multifunctional materials.
motivation: Crystalline materials with polar or chiral symmetry host a wide range of multifunctional properties, but a unified and complete classification of the possible structure types was lacking.
method: The authors perform a comprehensive symmetry-group analysis to classify crystal structures into fundamentally distinct polar and chiral categories.
result: Twelve fundamentally distinct types of crystal structures are identified across five polar and five chiral categories, providing a complete taxonomy.
conclusion: The classification offers a predictive framework for discovering and engineering next-generation multifunctional materials, though it lies outside quantum information and thermodynamics research.

title: Coulomb Screening Of Superconductivity In Magic-Angle Graphene
authors: Julien Barrier, Liangtao Peng, Shuigang Xu, Christophe de Beule, V. I. Fal’ko, K. Watanabe, T. Tanigushi, A. K. Geim, Shaffique Adam, And Alexey I. Berdyugin
abstract:
Author(s): Julien Barrier, Liangtao Peng, Shuigang Xu, Christophe De Beule, V. I. Fal’ko, K. Watanabe, T. Tanigushi, A. K. Geim, Shaffique Adam, and Alexey I. Berdyugin

Metallic layers placed near magic-angle graphene suppress Coulomb interactions and reveal that its superconductivity is driven by electronic interactions rather than conventional atomic vibrations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031040] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: Metallic screening layers placed near magic-angle graphene suppress Coulomb interactions, showing that its superconductivity originates from electronic correlations rather than phonon-mediated pairing.
motivation: The pairing mechanism of superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene remains contested, with electron-electron interactions and conventional phonon mechanisms as competing explanations.
method: The authors place proximal metallic layers near magic-angle graphene to screen long-range Coulomb interactions, then measure how the superconducting state and correlated phases respond to this screening.
result: Screening the Coulomb interaction suppresses superconductivity, indicating that electronic correlations—not atomic vibrations—drive the pairing in this system.
conclusion: The findings support an interaction-driven, unconventional pairing mechanism in magic-angle graphene and highlight Coulomb screening as a tunable knob for probing correlated electronic phases.

title: Observation Of Correlated Plasmons In Low-Valence Nickelates
authors: Y. Shen, W. He, J. Sears, Xuefei Guo, Xiangpeng Luo, A. Roll, J. Li, J. Pelliciari, Xi He, I. Božovič, Junjie Zhang, J. F. Mitchell, V. Bisogni, M. Mitrano, S. Johnston, And M. P. M. Dean
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Shen, W. He, J. Sears, Xuefei Guo, Xiangpeng Luo, A. Roll, J. Li, J. Pelliciari, Xi He, I. Božovič, Junjie Zhang, J. F. Mitchell, V. Bisogni, M. Mitrano, S. Johnston, and M. P. M. Dean

Resonant inelastic x-ray scattering measurements reveal propagating plasmons in the low-valence nickelate Pr
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031031] Published Fri Aug 07, 2026.
tldr: Resonant inelastic x-ray scattering reveals propagating correlated plasmons in low-valence nickelate Pr-based materials, with dynamics differing from cuprate superconductors.
motivation: Understanding collective charge excitations in nickelates is important for clarifying parallels and contrasts with cuprate superconductors in the context of unconventional superconductivity.
method: Resonant inelastic x-ray scattering (RIXS) measurements are used to probe the momentum- and energy-dependent charge excitation spectrum of low-valence nickelates.
result: Propagating plasmons with dispersion distinct from those observed in cuprates are identified, indicating different collective charge dynamics in the nickelate system.
conclusion: The observed plasmon behavior highlights key electronic-structure differences between nickelates and cuprates, informing ongoing debates on the physics of nickelate superconductors.

title: Topological Flowscape Reveals State Transitions In Nonreciprocal Living Matter
authors: Hyunseok Lee, Eliseanne Koskelo, Shreyas Gokhale, Junang Li, Chenyi Fei, Chih-Wei Joshua Liu, Lisa Lin, Jörn Dunkel, Dominic J. Skinner, And Nikta Fakhri
abstract:
Author(s): Hyunseok Lee, EliseAnne Koskelo, Shreyas Gokhale, Junang Li, Chenyi Fei, Chih-Wei Joshua Liu, Lisa Lin, Jörn Dunkel, Dominic J. Skinner, and Nikta Fakhri

Characterizing living systems far from the thermodynamic limit can yield insight into the physics of nonreciprocity and biological self-organization.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031061] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a topological flowscape framework to reveal state transitions in nonreciprocal living matter far from thermodynamic equilibrium.
motivation: Living systems operating far from the thermodynamic limit exhibit nonreciprocity and self-organization that are not captured by equilibrium physics, motivating new geometric or topological tools.
method: The authors likely analyze experimental or simulated data from living matter using topological flowscapes to identify transitions between collective states.
result: The approach reveals state transitions in nonreciprocal living matter, connecting topological features of flow fields to biological self-organization.
conclusion: The work advances the physics of nonreciprocal active matter but has no direct connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Novel Ringdown Tests Of General Relativity With Black Hole Graybody Factors
authors: Romeo Felice Rosato, Francesco Crescimbeni, Sophia Yi, Emanuele Berti, And Paolo Pani
abstract:
Author(s): Romeo Felice Rosato, Francesco Crescimbeni, Sophia Yi, Emanuele Berti, and Paolo Pani

We present greyring, a new model for the postmerger signal in black-hole binary coalescences based on the graybody factor of the remnant. The model accurately reproduces the full frequency-domain ringdown signal for a large set of comparable-mass, aligned-spin numerical relativity waveforms, includi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 121402] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces greyring, a new postmerger ringdown model based on black hole graybody factors, and uses it to test general relativity with gravitational-wave data.
motivation: Ringdown signals from black-hole binary coalescences provide a powerful probe of the nature of the remnant and strong-field gravity, but accurate waveform models are needed to perform robust tests of general relativity.
method: The authors develop a frequency-domain ringdown model using the graybody factor of the final black hole and validate it against a large set of comparable-mass, aligned-spin numerical relativity waveforms, including higher overtones and nonlinearities.
result: greyring accurately reproduces the full ringdown signal across the tested numerical relativity waveforms and is applied to gravitational-wave data to place novel constraints on deviations from general relativity.
conclusion: The graybody-factor-based approach provides a novel and accurate framework for ringdown tests of general relativity, potentially improving constraints on black hole properties and alternative theories of gravity.

title: Resolution And Robustness Bounds For Reconstructive Spectrometers
authors: Changyan Zhu, Hsuan Lo, Jianbo Yu, Qi Jie Wang, And Y. D. Chong
abstract:
Author(s): Changyan Zhu, Hsuan Lo, Jianbo Yu, Qi Jie Wang, and Y. D. Chong

Reconstructive spectrometers are an emerging class of devices that combine complex light scattering with inference. Thus far, the physical determinants of their performance remain underexplored. Within the regime of chaotic or diffusive scattering, the noise-induced error for spectral reconstruction…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 123802] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives physical bounds on the resolution and robustness of reconstructive spectrometers that use chaotic or diffusive light scattering followed by inference.
motivation: Reconstructive spectrometers are an emerging device class, but the fundamental physical determinants of their performance have been underexplored.
method: The authors analyze spectral reconstruction in the regime of chaotic or diffusive scattering, focusing on noise-induced error and deriving resolution limits.
result: They establish bounds relating the achievable spectral resolution and robustness to the scattering properties and noise in the reconstructive spectrometer.
conclusion: These bounds provide a theoretical framework for understanding and optimizing the performance of reconstructive spectrometers.

title: Thermodynamic Evidence Of Tetracritical Topology In The $H\text{−}T$ Phase Diagram Of ${\mathrm{UTe}}_{2}$ For $H∥b$
authors: Michal Vališka, Tetiana Haidamak, Andrej Cabala, Petr Proschek, Vladimír Sechovský, Andreas Hauspurg, And Sergei Zherlitsyn
abstract:
Author(s): Michal Vališka, Tetiana Haidamak, Andrej Cabala, Petr Proschek, Vladimír Sechovský, Andreas Hauspurg, and Sergei Zherlitsyn

We report ultrasound velocity measurements on an ultraclean [MATH] single crystal with [MATH] for [MATH], performed up to 18 T and down to 0.33 K. The measurements provide the missing bulk thermodynamic evidence for an additional high-field phase bounda…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 126003] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: Ultrasound velocity measurements on ultraclean UTe2 single crystals up to 18 T and down to 0.33 K provide bulk thermodynamic evidence for an additional high-field phase boundary, supporting a tetracritical topology in the H–T phase diagram for H∥b.
motivation: The magnetic and superconducting phase diagram of the heavy-fermion superconductor UTe2 remains controversial, particularly regarding the number and nature of high-field phase boundaries for field applied along the b axis.
method: The authors performed high-resolution ultrasound (acoustic) velocity measurements on ultraclean UTe2 single crystals in magnetic fields up to 18 T and temperatures down to 0.33 K, tracking elastic anomalies associated with phase transitions.
result: The measurements reveal the previously missing bulk thermodynamic signature of an additional high-field phase boundary, giving direct evidence for a tetracritical point in the H–T phase diagram for H∥b.
conclusion: The acoustic data establish the tetracritical topology of the UTe2 phase diagram and constrain theoretical models of its unconventional superconductivity and magnetic order.

title: Superconductivity In The Repulsive Hubbard Model On Different Geometries Induced By Density-Assisted Hopping
authors: Franco T. Lisandrini, Edmond Orignac, Roberta Citro, Ameneh Sheikhan, And Corinna Kollath
abstract:
Author(s): Franco T. Lisandrini, Edmond Orignac, Roberta Citro, Ameneh Sheikhan, and Corinna Kollath

We study the effect of density-assisted hopping on different dimerized lattice geometries, such as bilayers and ladder structures. We show analytically that the density-assisted hopping induces an attractive interaction in the lower (bonding) band of the dimer structure and a repulsion in the upper …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 126004] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: Density-assisted hopping induces attractive interactions in the lower band of dimerized lattices, leading to superconductivity in the repulsive Hubbard model.
motivation: To understand how density-assisted hopping affects superconductivity in repulsive Hubbard models on different dimerized geometries such as bilayers and ladders.
method: Analytical study of the repulsive Hubbard model with density-assisted hopping on dimerized lattices, deriving effective interactions in the bonding and antibonding bands.
result: The density-assisted hopping generates an attractive interaction in the lower bonding band and a repulsive interaction in the upper band, which can stabilize superconducting phases.
conclusion: Density-assisted hopping provides a mechanism for superconductivity in repulsive Hubbard models on certain dimerized geometries, highlighting the role of lattice structure.

title: Self-Organized Defect Phases Along Dislocations In Irradiated Alloys
authors: N. Saunders, R. S. Averback, And P. Bellon
abstract:
Author(s): N. Saunders, R. S. Averback, and P. Bellon

Patterning of precipitates along dislocation lines arising from nonequilibrium segregation during ion irradiation is investigated in model binary alloys. Lattice kinetic Monte Carlo simulations reveal that the competition between solute advection by point defects to the dislocation and thermal diffu…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 126201] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: Lattice kinetic Monte Carlo simulations show that competition between radiation-induced solute advection toward dislocations and thermal diffusion produces self-organized precipitate patterning along dislocation lines in model binary alloys.
motivation: Nonequilibrium segregation of solutes to dislocations during ion irradiation is known to alter alloy microstructure, but the mechanisms governing spatial patterning of precipitates along dislocation lines were not well understood.
method: The authors perform lattice kinetic Monte Carlo simulations of model binary alloys under irradiation, comparing the advective flux of solute driven by point-defect gradients at dislocations against thermal diffusive mixing.
result: Distinct self-organized defect/precipitate phases emerge along dislocations, with the resulting patterns controlled by the balance of irradiation-driven advection and thermal diffusion.
conclusion: Dislocation lines can act as one-dimensional templates for radiation-induced self-organization of precipitate phases, providing a design principle for microstructural control in irradiated alloys.

title: Complex Dynamics Of Dual Vortex Nano-oscillators Mutually Coupled Via Spin Torques
authors: Loukas Kokkinos And Joo-Von Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Loukas Kokkinos and Joo-Von Kim

Spin-torque vortex oscillators (STVOs) have been shown to exhibit rich and complex dynamical regimes, which are strongly dependent on the configuration of the polarizer. Here, we give an overview of the dynamics in an STVO comprising two vortex free layers, where each layer serves as a dynamic polar…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 154417] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the complex dynamics of dual vortex spin-torque nano-oscillators coupled via spin torques.
motivation: Spin-torque vortex oscillators exhibit rich dynamics, and understanding mutual coupling in dual-free-layer configurations may enable novel nanoscale microwave sources.
method: The authors analyze an STVO comprising two vortex free layers, where each layer serves as a dynamic polarizer, using analytical or micromagnetic modeling.
result: They map out complex dynamical regimes dependent on the polarizer configuration, revealing mutual synchronization and coupled vortex dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides an overview of coupled vortex dynamics in dual STVOs, relevant to spintronic oscillator design but not to quantum information processing.

title: Learning Effective Hamiltonians For Crystals Exposed To Nonresonant Optical Excitation
authors: P. E. Alcaraz And M. Kolesik
abstract:
Author(s): P. E. Alcaraz and M. Kolesik

We introduce a computational framework for the efficient modeling of nonlinear optical responses in solids under nonresonant excitation. Utilizing the Semiconductor Bloch Equations, our approach captures multiband carrier dynamics across the entire Brillouin zone. A significant simulation speedup is…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 165417] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a computational framework based on the Semiconductor Bloch Equations to efficiently model nonlinear optical responses and multiband carrier dynamics in solids under nonresonant optical excitation.
motivation: Efficient modeling of nonlinear optics in solids across the full Brillouin zone is computationally demanding, motivating faster approaches to effective-Hamiltonian construction and carrier dynamics simulation.
method: The authors use the Semiconductor Bloch Equations to capture multiband carrier dynamics and derive effective Hamiltonians for crystals driven by nonresonant optical fields, yielding a simulation speedup.
result: The framework achieves significant simulation speedup while capturing multiband carrier dynamics across the entire Brillouin zone for crystals under nonresonant optical excitation.
conclusion: The approach provides an efficient tool for modeling nonlinear optical responses in solids, though it remains a condensed-matter/nonlinear-optics computational method without direct quantum information or thermodynamics content.

title: Altermagnetic Phases And Phase Transitions In The Lieb-5 Hubbard Model
authors: Sougata Biswas, Achintyaa, And Paramita Dutta
abstract:
Author(s): Sougata Biswas, Achintyaa, and Paramita Dutta

The emergence of altermagnetism, a collinear magnetic phase characterized by momentum-dependent spin-split bands but zero net magnetization, has fundamentally reshaped the classification of magnetic order. We propose an altermagnetic (AM) order in a repulsive Hubbard model on the Lieb-5 lattice. Con…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 175126] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an altermagnetic order in a repulsive Hubbard model on the Lieb-5 lattice and studies its phase transitions.
motivation: Altermagnetism is a newly recognized collinear magnetic phase with zero net magnetization but momentum-dependent spin-split bands, motivating exploration in frustrated lattice geometries.
method: The authors analyze a repulsive Hubbard model on the Lieb-5 lattice, likely using mean-field or numerical techniques to identify altermagnetic phases and transitions.
result: They find an altermagnetic order and characterize the phase transitions, possibly including transitions to other magnetic or paramagnetic phases.
conclusion: The work extends the understanding of altermagnetism to the Lieb-5 lattice, providing a new platform for studying this exotic magnetic order.

title: Role Of Electron–lattice Coupling In Colossal Negative Thermal Expansion Of ${A}_{2}{\mathrm{P}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{7}$ And Beyond
authors: Xiangkai Hao, Kaiyue Zhao, Shuyuan Liu, Yongqiang Qiao, Qiang Sun, Juan Guo, Shintaro Kobayashi, Shogo Kawaguchi, Lunhua He, Erjun Liang, Jun-Hyung Cho, Jun Chen, And Qilong Gao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangkai Hao, Kaiyue Zhao, Shuyuan Liu, Yongqiang Qiao, Qiang Sun, Juan Guo, Shintaro Kobayashi, Shogo Kawaguchi, Lunhua He, Erjun Liang, Jun-Hyung Cho, Jun Chen, and Qilong Gao

Colossal negative thermal expansion (CNTE) materials are of significant importance for applications in precision engineering and related fields. However, simultaneously achieving a colossal negative thermal expansion coefficient (CTE) and a broad temperature range remains a central challenge. Using …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 134305] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates how electron–lattice coupling drives colossal negative thermal expansion in A2P2O7 materials and related systems.
motivation: Colossal negative thermal expansion materials are important for precision engineering, but combining a large negative thermal expansion coefficient with a broad operating temperature range remains challenging.
method: The authors likely combine first-principles calculations with experimental structural and thermal expansion measurements to analyze electron–lattice coupling effects.
result: Electron–lattice coupling is identified as a key mechanism underlying the colossal negative thermal expansion in A2P2O7, and the findings extend beyond this family.
conclusion: The work provides microscopic insight into colossal negative thermal expansion and suggests design principles for related functional materials.

title: Anisotropic Magnons In The Layered Honeycomb Ferromagnet ${\mathrm{CrSiTe}}_{3}$
authors: T. J. Williams, D. L. Abernathy, M. D. Lumsden, J.-Q. Yan, And A. D. Christianson
abstract:
Author(s): T. J. Williams, D. L. Abernathy, M. D. Lumsden, J.-Q. Yan, and A. D. Christianson

Recent experimental and theoretical studies have suggested a possible Dirac magnon gap in the two-dimensional ferromagnetic semiconductor [MATH]. Detailed neutron scattering measurements were performed to shed light on the existence of the magnon gap, and suggest that the gap is ver…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 134422] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: Inelastic neutron scattering measurements on the layered honeycomb ferromagnet CrSiTe3 are used to probe the existence and nature of a Dirac magnon gap.
motivation: Recent experimental and theoretical work has suggested a possible Dirac magnon gap in the two-dimensional ferromagnetic semiconductor CrSiTe3, motivating a detailed characterization of its spin-wave spectrum.
method: Detailed inelastic neutron scattering measurements were performed on CrSiTe3 to map the magnon dispersion and extract the magnon gap and anisotropy parameters.
result: The measurements constrain the size and origin of the Dirac magnon gap, suggesting an anisotropy-driven gap in the honeycomb ferromagnet.
conclusion: The neutron scattering data clarify the magnon gap structure of CrSiTe3, informing models of anisotropic magnetism in layered honeycomb ferromagnets.

title: Theory Of Frozen Flux In A Narrow Uniform Superconducting Strip After Cooling In A Small Magnetic Field
authors: Alexei E. Koshelev
abstract:
Author(s): Alexei E. Koshelev

We analyze residual frozen flux in a long narrow superconducting strip cooled through its transition temperature [MATH] in a small perpendicular magnetic field. This problem is relevant for the issue of trapped magnetic flux in superconducting electronic devices. During cooling, the low-temperatu…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 154509] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: Theoretical study of residual frozen magnetic flux in a narrow superconducting strip after cooling through its transition temperature in a small perpendicular field, relevant to trapped flux in superconducting devices.
motivation: Trapped magnetic flux in superconducting electronic devices can degrade performance, so understanding how frozen flux forms during cooling is important for device reliability.
method: Analyzes the cooling process of a long narrow superconducting strip in a small perpendicular magnetic field using a theoretical model for flux dynamics through the transition temperature.
result: Characterizes the residual frozen flux as a function of cooling parameters and strip geometry, providing a quantitative description of trapped flux behavior.
conclusion: Offers theoretical insights into flux trapping that may help mitigate unwanted frozen flux in superconducting electronic devices.

title: Supercurrents In Josephson Junctions With Chiral Molecular Potentials
authors: Oleg Kuliashov, Alberto Cappellaro, Oded Millo, Yossi Paltiel, Mikhail Lemeshko, And Ragheed Alhyder
abstract:
Author(s): Oleg Kuliashov, Alberto Cappellaro, Oded Millo, Yossi Paltiel, Mikhail Lemeshko, and Ragheed Alhyder

The influence of chiral molecular potentials on phase-coherent transport in superconducting Josephson junctions is investigated. Within a Bogoliubov–de Gennes tight-binding framework, a superconducting-normal-superconducting (SNS) junction functionalized by adsorbed chiral molecules is modeled, wher…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 154510] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper models how chiral molecular potentials affect supercurrents in superconducting-normal-superconducting Josephson junctions using a Bogoliubov–de Gennes tight-binding approach.
motivation: To understand the influence of chiral molecules on phase-coherent transport in superconducting junctions, with potential implications for superconducting spintronics.
method: A Bogoliubov–de Gennes tight-binding framework is used to simulate an SNS junction functionalized by adsorbed chiral molecules.
result: The chiral molecular potential modifies the supercurrent characteristics, potentially inducing spin-dependent or asymmetric transport effects.
conclusion: Chiral molecules can tune Josephson supercurrents, offering a route to control phase-coherent transport in hybrid superconducting systems.

title: Coherent Dipole Units And Ferroelectric Correlations In Asymmetric Atomic-layer Superlattices
authors: Andrew J. Hamm, James N. Eckstein, Michael B. Weissman, And Maitri P. Warusawithana
abstract:
Author(s): Andrew J. Hamm, James N. Eckstein, Michael B. Weissman, and Maitri P. Warusawithana

We analyze the dielectric response of superlattice samples composed of titanate phases: calcium titanate, strontium titanate, and barium titanate, stacked at the ultimate atomic layer limit to break inversion symmetry. High temperature susceptibility measurements extracted from low-frequency ($∼100\…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 165126] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes dielectric response and ferroelectric correlations in asymmetric atomic-layer superlattices of titanate phases.
motivation: To investigate how breaking inversion symmetry in atomic-layer superlattices of CaTiO3, SrTiO3, and BaTiO3 affects ferroelectric correlations and dipole ordering.
method: High-temperature susceptibility measurements were performed on superlattice samples composed of titanate phases stacked at the ultimate atomic layer limit.
result: The measurements reveal coherent dipole units and ferroelectric correlations arising from the asymmetric stacking.
conclusion: The study demonstrates that asymmetric atomic-layer superlattices can host ferroelectric behavior, providing insights into engineered dielectric properties.

title: Investigations Of The Optical Gain In A ZnO-based Waveguide At Low Temperature
authors: L. Hermet, F. Médard, P. Disseix, S. Bouchoule, E. Cambril, J. Zúñiga‐pérez, C. Deparis, M. Hugues, D. Lefebvre, And J. Leymarie
abstract:
Author(s): L. Hermet, F. Médard, P. Disseix, S. Bouchoule, E. Cambril, J. Zúñiga‐Pérez, C. Deparis, M. Hugues, D. Lefebvre, and J. Leymarie

In this study we present a detailed spectroscopic analysis of the optical gain in a ZnO/ZnMgO waveguide microcavity benchmarked with a thick homoepitaxial ZnO layer. As a prerequisite we perform a precise determination of ZnO excitonic parameters through microreflectivity and low-excitation micropho…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 185304] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports a detailed spectroscopic study of optical gain in a ZnO/ZnMgO waveguide microcavity at low temperature, benchmarked against a thick homoepitaxial ZnO layer.
motivation: The authors aim to precisely determine ZnO excitonic parameters and understand gain mechanisms in ZnO-based microcavities for potential optoelectronic applications.
method: Microreflectivity and low-excitation microphotoluminescence spectroscopy were used to extract excitonic parameters, followed by optical gain measurements in a ZnO/ZnMgO waveguide microcavity.
result: The study provides accurate excitonic parameters for ZnO and characterizes the optical gain behavior in the waveguide microcavity, comparing it with the bulk ZnO reference.
conclusion: The findings contribute to the understanding of optical gain in ZnO-based microcavities, relevant for developing ZnO optoelectronic devices.

title: Compression-induced Anomalous Thermal Transport In The Giant Negative Thermal Expansion Material NaB(CN)${}_{4}$
authors: Yijing Zuo, Wei Cao, Yuxuan Zeng, Zhaofu Zhang, Fang Lyu, Yue Hou, Ling Miao, And Ziyu Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Yijing Zuo, Wei Cao, Yuxuan Zeng, Zhaofu Zhang, Fang Lyu, Yue Hou, Ling Miao, and Ziyu Wang

NaB(CN)[MATH] exhibits giant negative thermal expansion (NTE) that is closely associated with low-frequency phonons with large negative Grüneisen parameters. Although compression-induced softening of negative-Grüneisen phonons can modify lattice thermal conductivity ([MATH]), how NTE-a…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 154307] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: This study investigates how compression affects anomalous thermal transport in the giant negative thermal expansion material NaB(CN)4, linking phonon softening to changes in lattice thermal conductivity.
motivation: NaB(CN)4 exhibits giant negative thermal expansion tied to low-frequency phonons with large negative Grüneisen parameters, but the impact of compression-induced phonon softening on thermal conductivity remains unclear.
method: Using first-principles calculations and phonon transport theory, the authors analyze the pressure dependence of phonon frequencies, Grüneisen parameters, and lattice thermal conductivity under compression.
result: Compression anomalously alters thermal transport, with negative-Grüneisen phonons softening and modifying thermal conductivity in a non-trivial manner.
conclusion: The findings reveal a compression-induced anomalous thermal transport mechanism in NTE materials, offering insights for tuning thermal properties via strain.

title: Finite-momentum Bound Pairs Of Two Electrons In An Altermagnetic Metal
authors: Hui Hu, Zhao Liu, Jia Wang, And Xia-Ji Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Hui Hu, Zhao Liu, Jia Wang, and Xia-Ji Liu

We solve the two-electron problem on a square lattice with [MATH]-wave altermagnetism, considering both on-site and nearest-neighbor attractive interactions. The altermagnetic spin-splitting in the single-particle dispersion naturally gives rise to a ground state of two-electron bound pairs with nonzer…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 165124] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper solves the two-electron problem on a square lattice with d-wave altermagnetism, finding that the altermagnetic spin-splitting leads to bound pairs with nonzero center-of-mass momentum.
motivation: Altermagnetism is an emerging class of magnetic order, and understanding how it affects electron pairing is important for potential superconductivity and transport phenomena.
method: The authors consider a square lattice with d-wave altermagnetism and both on-site and nearest-neighbor attractive interactions, solving the two-electron Schrödinger equation exactly or numerically.
result: The ground state consists of two-electron bound pairs with finite center-of-mass momentum, arising naturally from the altermagnetic spin-splitting in the single-particle dispersion.
conclusion: Altermagnetic metals can support finite-momentum bound pairs, suggesting a platform for unconventional pairing mechanisms.

title: Symmetric Mass Generation In A Bilayer Honeycomb Lattice With $\mathrm{SU}(2)×\mathrm{SU}(2)×\mathrm{SU}(2)/{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}$ Symmetry
authors: Cheng-Hao He, Yi-Zhuang You, And Xiao Yan Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Cheng-Hao He, Yi-Zhuang You, and Xiao Yan Xu

A central question beyond the Landau paradigm is the nonperturbative critical theory of the symmetric mass generation (SMG) transition, where strong interactions gap Dirac fermions in [MATH] dimensions without triggering spontaneous symmetry breaking or topological order. Sign-problem-free studies ha…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 165125] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates a nonperturbative symmetric mass generation transition in a bilayer honeycomb lattice with SU(2)×SU(2)×SU(2)/Z2 symmetry, where interactions gap Dirac fermions without symmetry breaking or topological order.
motivation: The central question is to understand the critical theory of symmetric mass generation beyond the Landau paradigm, a nonperturbative phenomenon in condensed matter and lattice field theory.
method: The authors likely use sign-problem-free quantum Monte Carlo simulations of a bilayer honeycomb lattice model with Dirac fermions and specific symmetry constraints.
result: The study identifies and characterizes a symmetric mass generation transition, providing evidence for interaction-driven gapping of Dirac fermions without spontaneous symmetry breaking or topological order.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of nonperturbative criticality in Dirac systems and offers a concrete lattice realization of symmetric mass generation.

title: Extreme-ultraviolet Optical Response Of Atomically Thin Molybdenum Disulfide
authors: Giacomo Fiorentini, Nicola Di Palo, Giacomo Inzani, Gian Luca Dolso, Simone Bonetti, Qiuyang Li, Fang Liu, Xiaoyang Zhu, Angelo Giglia, Nicola Mahne, Luca Pasquali, Marco D'alessandro, Mikhail Malakhov, María Camarasa-Gómez, Juan José Esteve-Paredes, Juan José Palacios, Rocío Borrego-Varillas, Mauro Nisoli, Antonio Picón, Davide Sangalli, And Matteo Lucchini
abstract:
Author(s): Giacomo Fiorentini, Nicola Di Palo, Giacomo Inzani, Gian Luca Dolso, Simone Bonetti, Qiuyang Li, Fang Liu, Xiaoyang Zhu, Angelo Giglia, Nicola Mahne, Luca Pasquali, Marco D'Alessandro, Mikhail Malakhov, María Camarasa-Gómez, Juan José Esteve-Paredes, Juan José Palacios, Rocío Borrego-Varillas, Mauro Nisoli, Antonio Picón, Davide Sangalli, and Matteo Lucchini

Here, the authors determine the extreme-ultraviolet optical constants of monolayer and bilayer MoS
[Phys. Rev. B 114, 185419] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: A combined experimental and first-principles study determines the extreme-ultraviolet optical constants of monolayer and bilayer MoS2, showing the XUV response scales linearly with thickness and is dominated by local-field effects rather than excitonic signatures.
motivation: Benchmark optical data for 2D materials in the XUV range are scarce, yet are needed for interpreting future XUV and attosecond spectroscopy experiments on atomically thin semiconductors.
method: The authors combine XUV spectroscopic measurements of monolayer and bilayer MoS2 with first-principles calculations, connecting the 2D conductivity to an effective 3D refractive index.
result: The XUV optical response scales linearly with layer thickness, and in contrast to the visible range, local-field effects dominate the XUV response, largely suppressing distinct excitonic features.
conclusion: The work provides benchmark XUV optical constants for MoS2 and clarifies the role of local-field effects in the extreme-ultraviolet regime, supporting future attosecond spectroscopy of 2D materials.

title: Interaction Process Of Exploding Dissipative Solitons
authors: Orazio Descalzi And Helmut R. Brand
abstract:
Author(s): Orazio Descalzi and Helmut R. Brand

We study the interaction of exploding dissipative solitons (DSs) in the framework of two coupled cubic-quintic Ginzburg-Landau equations. We find several classes of behavior as a function of the cross-coupling between counterpropagating DSs, [MATH], by varying the initial conditions for fixed a…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034217] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper numerically studies interactions between exploding dissipative solitons in coupled cubic-quintic Ginzburg-Landau equations.
motivation: Exploding dissipative solitons are intriguing nonlinear structures, and their mutual interactions are not fully understood.
method: Two coupled cubic-quintic Ginzburg-Landau equations are solved to examine counterpropagating dissipative solitons as a function of cross-coupling strength and initial conditions.
result: Several distinct interaction regimes are identified, revealing how cross-coupling governs the dynamics of exploding solitons.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of complex soliton interactions in dissipative nonlinear systems, but it lies outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Quantum Reconnection Of An Inclined Vortex Ring With A Straight Vortex Line: Energy Distribution And Geometric Analysis
authors: Martina Luise, Nicola Sansonetto, And Simone Zuccher
abstract:
Author(s): Martina Luise, Nicola Sansonetto, and Simone Zuccher

We investigate the reconnection process involving a quantum vortex ring colliding at different angles with a quantum straight vortex line. The dynamics of this phenomenon is well described by the Gross-Pitaevskii equation. Two families of initial configurations are explored, one by varying the angle…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035106] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper numerically studies the reconnection of a quantum vortex ring colliding at various angles with a straight quantum vortex line using the Gross-Pitaevskii equation, focusing on energy distribution and geometric properties.
motivation: Quantum vortex reconnection is a fundamental process in superfluid dynamics, but the dependence on collision angle and the resulting energy redistribution remain incompletely understood.
method: The authors simulate the Gross-Pitaevskii equation for two families of initial configurations, varying the collision angle between the vortex ring and the straight vortex line, and analyze the resulting energy distribution and vortex geometry.
result: They characterize the reconnection dynamics, show how the angle affects the energy distribution among vortex modes, and provide a geometric analysis of the reconnection process.
conclusion: The findings clarify the mechanisms of quantum vortex reconnection in superfluids, with potential implications for understanding turbulence and topological defect dynamics in quantum fluids.

title: Phase Correlations Of A Strongly Scintillating Light Wave Propagating Through A Turbulent Medium
authors: V. A. Bogachev, I. V. Kolokolov, V. V. Lebedev, A. V. Nemtseva, And F. A. Starikov
abstract:
