We investigate analytically and numerically correlation functions of the phase of light waves that propagate through turbulent media. We examine the case of strong scintillations that occur at large values of the Rytov dispersion [MATH], which determines a level of distortions of the light wa…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034133] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: An analytical and numerical study of phase correlation functions of light waves propagating through turbulent media under strong scintillation conditions.
motivation: Understanding phase distortions caused by atmospheric turbulence is important for classical optical imaging and communication, but the work lacks any quantum information or thermodynamic angle.
method: The authors use analytical theory and numerical simulations to compute phase correlation functions, focusing on the regime of large Rytov dispersion that characterizes strong scintillations.
result: They derive and numerically verify correlation functions for the phase of a light wave after propagation through a turbulent medium in the strong scintillation regime.
conclusion: The results characterize phase fluctuations in turbulent media, which may be useful for classical wave propagation modeling but have no direct relevance to the user's quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems interests.

title: Better Together: Cross And Joint Covariances Enhance Signal Detectability In Undersampled Data
authors: Arabind Swain, Sean Alexander Ridout, And Ilya Nemenman
abstract:
Author(s): Arabind Swain, Sean Alexander Ridout, and Ilya Nemenman

Random matrix theory reveals that analyzing joint or cross-covariance matrices detects shared signals between high-dimensional variables earlier than standard individual self-covariances under heavy sampling noise.


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035305] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: Random matrix theory shows that cross- and joint-covariance matrices can detect shared signals between high-dimensional variables earlier than individual self-covariances under heavy sampling noise.
motivation: Detecting weak shared signals in undersampled high-dimensional data is challenging, and standard self-covariance approaches may fail when noise dominates.
method: The authors use random matrix theory to analyze the spectra of joint and cross-covariance matrices and compare signal detectability against standard individual covariance matrices.
result: Joint and cross-covariance matrices enhance signal detectability, revealing shared signals at lower sample sizes than self-covariance methods in noisy undersampled regimes.
conclusion: Cross- and joint-covariance analyses provide a more sensitive tool for signal detection in high-dimensional data with limited samples.

title: Stabilizing Generative Adversarial Networks With Adaptive Noise Injection
authors: Yamin Zhang, Fabing Duan, François Chapeau-Blondeau, And Derek Abbott
abstract:
Author(s): Yamin Zhang, Fabing Duan, François Chapeau-Blondeau, and Derek Abbott

In conventional generative adversarial networks (GANs), the discriminator typically employs a sigmoid activation to map features to probabilities. However, this activation suffers from the vanishing-gradient problem, which can lead to training instability and mode collapse. This work reformulates th…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035304] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes adaptive noise injection to stabilize generative adversarial network training by addressing the vanishing-gradient problem in the discriminator's sigmoid activation.
motivation: Conventional GANs suffer from training instability and mode collapse due to vanishing gradients in the discriminator when using sigmoid activations.
method: The authors reformulate the discriminator's output and introduce an adaptive noise injection mechanism that adjusts noise levels during training to maintain gradient flow.
result: Adaptive noise injection mitigates vanishing gradients and improves training stability, preventing mode collapse in benchmark GAN tasks.
conclusion: Adaptive noise injection offers a simple and effective way to stabilize GAN training without major architectural changes.

title: Improving Absorption Spectroscopy Measurements In Attosecond X-ray Free-electron Laser Experiments Using Machine Learning
authors: K. Hu, O. G. Alexander, F. Egun, And J. P. Marangos
abstract:
Author(s): K. Hu, O. G. Alexander, F. Egun, and J. P. Marangos

X-ray free-electron lasers (XFELs) provide ultrashort, high-brightness pulses for probing matter on femtosecond and attosecond timescales, but their stochastic shot-to-shot fluctuations make x-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) challenging, as both incident and transmitted spectra are required to be …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033333] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: Machine learning is used to correct shot-to-shot fluctuations in attosecond X-ray free-electron laser experiments, improving X-ray absorption spectroscopy measurements.
motivation: XFELs deliver ultrashort high-brightness pulses for probing matter on femtosecond/attosecond timescales, but stochastic pulse fluctuations make X-ray absorption spectroscopy difficult because both incident and transmitted spectra must be characterized.
method: The authors apply machine-learning techniques to model and correct the stochastic intensity and spectral fluctuations of the XFEL pulses in single-shot absorption measurements.
result: The ML-based correction improves the fidelity and reliability of X-ray absorption spectra extracted from noisy attosecond XFEL data.
conclusion: Machine learning offers a practical route to mitigate pulse fluctuations and enhance the quality of ultrafast X-ray absorption spectroscopy at XFEL facilities.

title: Dynamics Creation Through Neural Dynamical Transfer Learning
authors: He Ma, Qiyang Ge, Yu Meng, Celso Grebogi, And Wei Lin
abstract:
Author(s): He Ma, Qiyang Ge, Yu Meng, Celso Grebogi, and Wei Lin

Data-driven machine learning has established a robust foundation for reconstructing nonlinear dynamical systems from observations, primarily for the purposes of forecasting and control. However, most existing efforts focus on recovering specific observed dynamics rather than the generative synthesis…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033337] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: A neural transfer-learning method for generating new nonlinear dynamical systems from data rather than only reconstructing observed dynamics.
motivation: Existing data-driven approaches mainly recover observed dynamics for forecasting and control, while generative synthesis of dynamics remains underexplored.
method: The authors develop neural dynamical transfer learning to learn and transfer dynamical representations for creating new dynamics.
result: The approach enables generative synthesis of dynamical behaviors beyond those directly observed in training data.
conclusion: This work advances data-driven nonlinear dynamics and machine learning, but is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Controlling Directionality In Dipolar Colloids Via Relaxation In Alternating Rotating Fields
authors: Tatsuya Tanaka, Aldo Spatafora-Salazar, And Sibani Lisa Biswal
abstract:
Author(s): Tatsuya Tanaka, Aldo Spatafora-Salazar, and Sibani Lisa Biswal

Time-varying external fields can program dipolar interactions in soft matter systems. Continuously rotating fields are widely used to promote isotropic self-assembly, but finite relaxation of an induced dipole generically introduces a phase lag that can drive the spinning of both individual particle…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033328] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how finite dipole relaxation in alternating rotating fields introduces a phase lag that controls the directionality and spinning of dipolar colloidal particles.
motivation: Time-varying external fields can program dipolar interactions in soft matter, but the role of finite relaxation in continuously rotating fields remains unclear.
method: The authors analyze dipolar colloids under alternating rotating fields, accounting for the relaxation dynamics of induced dipoles.
result: They find that the relaxation-induced phase lag generically drives spinning of individual particles and can direct self-assembly.
conclusion: Relaxation in rotating fields provides a mechanism to control the directionality of dipolar colloidal systems.

title: Strain- And Confinement-induced Topological Phases In Noncentrosymmetric Wurtzite HgTe
authors: Antoine Hage, Jing Li, And Christophe Delerue
abstract:
Author(s): Antoine Hage, Jing Li, and Christophe Delerue

First-principles, tight-binding, and k p calculations are used to examine how strain and quantum confinement affect the electronic topology of wurtzite HgTe. The study relates bulk Dirac points along the wurtzite
[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033323] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: First-principles, tight-binding, and k·p calculations reveal how strain and quantum confinement control topological phases in noncentrosymmetric wurtzite HgTe.
motivation: Understanding the electronic topology of wurtzite HgTe is important for engineering topological phases in noncentrosymmetric materials, but the combined effects of strain and confinement remain insufficiently explored.
method: The authors use first-principles density functional theory, tight-binding models, and k·p calculations to analyze bulk Dirac points, thin-film orientation dependence, and nanowire edge states.
result: Strain-dependent topological phases are identified, along with orientation-dependent thin-film topology and edge-localized states in nanowires.
conclusion: The study provides a systematic map of how strain and quantum confinement can be used to tune topological phases in wurtzite HgTe, suggesting routes for experimental realization.

title: Stochastic Multistability Of Clonal-like States In The Eigen Model: A Fidelity Catastrophe
authors: Emanuele Crosato, Richard E. Spinney, And Richard G. Morris
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuele Crosato, Richard E. Spinney, and Richard G. Morris

The Eigen model is a prototypical toy model of evolution that is synonymous with the so-called error catastrophe: When mutation rates are sufficiently high, the genetic variant with the largest replication rate does not occupy the largest fraction of the total population because it acts as a source …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033325] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes stochastic multistability and a fidelity catastrophe in the Eigen model of evolution, where high mutation rates cause the fittest genetic variant to lose dominance.
motivation: The Eigen model is a classic framework for the error catastrophe, but stochastic effects and the multistability of clonal-like states remain insufficiently understood.
method: The authors employ stochastic dynamics, likely via master equations or related techniques, to study the Eigen model with mutation and replication.
result: They find stochastic multistability of clonal-like states and identify a fidelity catastrophe in which the most fit variant is overtaken due to elevated mutation rates.
conclusion: The work underscores the role of stochasticity in evolutionary error catastrophes and provides insights for quasispecies theory.

title: Arbitrary-velocity Volkov Wave Packets
authors: D. Ramsey, J. Mckeown, And J. P. Palastro
abstract:
Author(s): D. Ramsey, J. McKeown, and J. P. Palastro

The evolution of a charged lepton in the field of an electromagnetic plane wave can be described as a superposition of Volkov states. Here, we demonstrate that imposing specific momentum correlations among Volkov states produces a spatiotemporally structured wave packet whose probability-density pea…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033322] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper constructs spatiotemporally structured Volkov wave packets for a charged lepton in an electromagnetic plane wave by imposing momentum correlations among Volkov states.
motivation: Volkov states describe a charged particle in a classical plane-wave field, but their superpositions can form structured wave packets with controllable probability-density features relevant to strong-field QED.
method: The authors superpose Volkov states with specific momentum correlations to engineer a wave packet and analyze its spatiotemporal probability-density profile.
result: The resulting wave packet exhibits a probability-density peak whose properties depend on the imposed momentum correlations and the plane-wave field parameters.
conclusion: Momentum-correlated Volkov-state superpositions provide a route to arbitrary-velocity structured wave packets, with potential applications in strong-field physics rather than quantum information.

title: Mechanical Stress Induced By The Polymerization Of An Active Gel Near A Surface
authors: Kristiana Mihali, Dennis Wörthmüller, And Pierre Sens
abstract:
Author(s): Kristiana Mihali, Dennis Wörthmüller, and Pierre Sens

Actin flow in the cortical cytoskeleton underneath the cell membrane generates mechanical stresses that shape the cell surface. We study this mechanism using a hydrodynamic model of a compressible active gel polymerizing at the membrane and undergoing turnover. We determine how actin flow, density r…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033308] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: A hydrodynamic model of a compressible active gel polymerizing at a membrane is used to study how actin polymerization and turnover generate mechanical stresses that shape cell surfaces.
motivation: Actin flow in the cortical cytoskeleton beneath the cell membrane generates mechanical stresses that influence cell shape, but the interplay between polymerization, turnover, and surface deformation is not fully understood.
method: The authors develop a hydrodynamic model of an active gel that is compressible, polymerizes near a surface, and undergoes turnover, then analyze how actin flow and density profiles produce stress on the membrane.
result: The model predicts characteristic stress distributions and membrane deformations arising from the polymerization dynamics and active gel flow, linking microscopic turnover to macroscopic surface shaping.
conclusion: Polymerization-driven active gel stresses near a surface provide a physical mechanism for cell surface shaping, with implications for cortical cytoskeleton mechanics.

title: Semiconductor Wannier Equations: A Real-time, Real-space Approach To The Nonlinear Optical Response In Crystals
authors: Eduardo B. Molinero, Bruno Amorim, Misha Ivanov, Graham G. Brown, Giovanni Cistaro, João M. Viana Parente Lopes, Álvaro Jiménez-Galán, Pablo San-Jose, And Rui E. F. Silva
abstract:
Author(s): Eduardo B. Molinero, Bruno Amorim, Misha Ivanov, Graham G. Brown, Giovanni Cistaro, João M. Viana Parente Lopes, Álvaro Jiménez-Galán, Pablo San-Jose, and Rui E. F. Silva

We develop the semiconductor Wannier equations (SWEs), a real-time, real-space formulation of ultrafast light-matter dynamics in crystals, by deriving the equations of motion for the electronic reduced density matrix in a localized Wannier basis. Working in real space removes the structure-gauge amb…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033302] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: Develops semiconductor Wannier equations for real-time, real-space modeling of ultrafast light-matter dynamics and nonlinear optical response in crystals.
motivation: To overcome structure-gauge ambiguities and provide a localized basis for simulating ultrafast semiconductor optics.
method: Derives equations of motion for the electronic reduced density matrix in a localized Wannier basis, yielding a real-space formulation of light-matter dynamics.
result: The semiconductor Wannier equations remove gauge ambiguities and enable real-space simulations of nonlinear optical response in crystals.
conclusion: This framework offers an efficient real-time, real-space approach to ultrafast crystal optics, though it is outside the core research interests.

title: Ultrastrong Unconventional Spin Current Via Noncollinear Spin-Orbit Filtering
authors: Hongliang Chen, Zi-An Wang, Xingguo Gao, Hang Zhou, Jiaxin Chen, Chang Pan, Lizhu Ren, Qia Shen, Zhenyi Zheng, Dandan Guan, Xiaoxue Liu, Shiyong Wang, Yaoyi Li, Hao Zheng, Canhua Liu, Yumeng Yang, Xuepeng Qiu, Guowei Zhou, Jingsheng Chen, Jinfeng Jia, Ding-Fu Shao, And Liang Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Hongliang Chen, Zi-An Wang, Xingguo Gao, Hang Zhou, Jiaxin Chen, Chang Pan, Lizhu Ren, Qia Shen, Zhenyi Zheng, Dandan Guan, Xiaoxue Liu, Shiyong Wang, Yaoyi Li, Hao Zheng, Canhua Liu, Yumeng Yang, Xuepeng Qiu, Guowei Zhou, Jingsheng Chen, Jinfeng Jia, Ding-Fu Shao, and Liang Liu

An asymmetric platinum interface enables noncollinear spin-orbit filtering, breaking bulk symmetry constraints to generate out-of-plane spin currents for field-free magnetization switching.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031060] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: An asymmetric platinum interface enables noncollinear spin-orbit filtering that breaks bulk symmetry constraints to produce out-of-plane spin currents for field-free magnetization switching.
motivation: Conventional spin-orbit torque schemes are limited by bulk symmetry constraints that restrict the polarization direction of generated spin currents, hindering deterministic field-free magnetization switching.
method: The authors engineer an asymmetric Pt interface to realize noncollinear spin-orbit filtering and measure the resulting unconventional out-of-plane spin current and its effect on magnetization switching.
result: The asymmetric interface generates an ultrastrong unconventional spin current with out-of-plane polarization, enabling field-free switching of magnetization that would be symmetry-forbidden in bulk systems.
conclusion: Noncollinear spin-orbit filtering at engineered interfaces offers a route to symmetry-broken spin currents and efficient field-free spintronic device operation.

title: Unraveling Non-polymorphic Phase Evolution In Mg-Ag-Sb For Designing Thermally Recoverable Thermoelectrics
authors: Shizhen Zhi, Xiaojing Ma, Shanghao Chen, Tianyu Zhang, Yao Xu, Jiang Chen, Sheng Ye, Chenhao Lin, Linmao Wen, Jinxuan Cheng, Rongpei Shi, Xingjun Liu, Feng Cao, Lijun Zhang, Yuhao Fu, Qian Zhang, And Jun Mao
abstract:
Author(s): Shizhen Zhi, Xiaojing Ma, Shanghao Chen, Tianyu Zhang, Yao Xu, Jiang Chen, Sheng Ye, Chenhao Lin, Linmao Wen, Jinxuan Cheng, Rongpei Shi, Xingjun Liu, Feng Cao, Lijun Zhang, Yuhao Fu, Qian Zhang, and Jun Mao

Thermal degradation in MgAgSb thermoelectric material can be reversed with low-temperature annealing.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031035] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: The thermal degradation of MgAgSb thermoelectric material can be reversed by low-temperature annealing, enabled by non-polymorphic phase evolution.
motivation: Thermoelectric materials suffer from thermal degradation that limits their long-term operational stability, and understanding the underlying phase evolution is key to designing recoverable thermoelectrics.
method: The authors investigate the phase evolution in Mg-Ag-Sb thermoelectric materials using structural and thermodynamic characterization, combined with theoretical modeling, to identify the mechanisms behind thermal degradation and recovery.
result: The study reveals non-polymorphic phase evolution pathways that govern thermal degradation, and demonstrates that low-temperature annealing restores the material's thermoelectric performance.
conclusion: Designing thermally recoverable thermoelectrics through controlled phase evolution offers a route to more durable energy conversion materials.

title: GPU-accelerated Sequential Monte Carlo For Bayesian Spectral Analysis
authors: Tomohiro Nabika, Yui Hayashi, And Masato Okada
abstract:
Author(s): Tomohiro Nabika, Yui Hayashi, and Masato Okada

Bayesian spectral deconvolution provides a data-driven framework for mathematical model selection and parameter estimation from spectral data. Although highly versatile, its computational cost grows with the number of model parameters, data points, and candidate models, often rendering practical app…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035303] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a GPU-accelerated sequential Monte Carlo method for Bayesian spectral deconvolution and model selection.
motivation: Bayesian spectral deconvolution is a versatile data-driven framework, but its computational cost grows rapidly with model parameters, data points, and candidate models, limiting practical use.
method: The authors accelerate sequential Monte Carlo sampling using GPU parallelization to perform Bayesian inference and model selection on spectral data.
result: The GPU-accelerated approach reduces computational cost and makes Bayesian spectral deconvolution feasible for larger models and datasets.
conclusion: The work provides a practical computational tool for spectral analysis, but it lies outside quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Mechanochemical Nano-Writing Of An Atomically Thin Metal
authors: Shuai Zhang, Yanyu Jia, Atanu Samanta, Yutian Bao, Haosen Guan, Zhaoyi Joy Zheng, Guangming Cheng, Ting Liu, Cangyu Qu, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Nan Yao, Ashlie Martini, Leslie Schoop, Andrew M. Rappe, Sanfeng Wu, And Robert W. Carpick
abstract:
Author(s): Shuai Zhang, Yanyu Jia, Atanu Samanta, Yutian Bao, Haosen Guan, Zhaoyi Joy Zheng, Guangming Cheng, Ting Liu, Cangyu Qu, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Nan Yao, Ashlie Martini, Leslie Schoop, Andrew M. Rappe, Sanfeng Wu, and Robert W. Carpick

A large stress generated by a small tip drives a reaction between two materials in an 2D encapsulated space to produce a new material with interesting electronic properties that can be written into patterns as small as 50 nm.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031029] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: A nanoscale tip-induced mechanochemical reaction inside a 2D encapsulated stack synthesizes a new atomically thin metal that can be patterned into sub-50 nm features.
motivation: There is a need for methods to locally synthesize and pattern atomically thin materials with tailored electronic properties, which conventional lithography cannot easily achieve at the nanoscale.
method: A scanning tip applies large local stress to drive a solid-state reaction between two materials confined within a 2D encapsulated geometry, and the resulting product is characterized structurally and electronically.
result: The mechanochemical reaction produces a new atomically thin metallic material with interesting electronic properties, writable into patterns with feature sizes as small as ~50 nm.
conclusion: Tip-induced mechanochemistry offers a versatile route to direct-write atomically thin metals, potentially enabling nanoscale device fabrication beyond the reach of standard lithographic techniques.

title: Factorization Beyond Coherence
authors: Thomas Becher, Patrick Hager, Matthias Neubert, And Dominik Schwienbacher
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas Becher, Patrick Hager, Matthias Neubert, and Dominik Schwienbacher

We propose a novel factorization theorem for [MATH]-jettiness at hadron colliders, which incorporates coherence-violating effects induced by Glauber gluons and several new momentum modes. Their interplay generates coherence-violating logarithms starting at four-loop ([MATH]) or five-loop order ([MATH]). …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 121902] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a new factorization theorem for N-jettiness at hadron colliders that accounts for coherence-violating effects from Glauber gluons and additional momentum modes.
motivation: Standard factorization theorems for jettiness observables assume coherence of soft radiation, but Glauber gluon exchanges can violate this assumption, requiring a more complete treatment for precision collider predictions.
method: The authors extend soft-collinear effective theory (SCET) by identifying new momentum modes and Glauber gluon contributions, deriving a generalized factorization formula with coherence-violating logarithms.
result: Coherence-violating logarithms are shown to first appear at four-loop (N^3LL) or five-loop order, setting the order at which these effects become numerically relevant.
conclusion: The refined factorization theorem provides a systematic framework for incorporating Glauber-induced coherence violation in jettiness calculations, relevant for high-precision QCD phenomenology at hadron colliders.

title: Crosstalk And Oersted Field Interference Resolve The Hidden Spin-Wave Puzzle In Hematite
authors: Yihang Duan, Shangyuan Wang, And Ka Shen
abstract:
Author(s): Yihang Duan, Shangyuan Wang, and Ka Shen

A recent study reporting interferencelike patterns in nonlocal spin-wave measurements on hematite [Sheng et al., Control of spin currents by magnon interference in a canted antiferromagnet,
tldr: The paper resolves puzzling spin-wave interference patterns in hematite by showing they arise from crosstalk and Oersted field effects rather than a hidden ultrafast magnon mode.
motivation: Recent nonlocal spin-wave measurements on hematite suggested an unknown tens-of-gigahertz spin-wave mode, motivating a closer look at the measurement geometry and electromagnetic artifacts.
method: The authors analyze the nonlocal measurement setup, including microwave crosstalk between antennas and Oersted fields generated by the excitation current, to model the observed interference patterns.
result: They demonstrate that the interference-like features can be quantitatively explained by crosstalk and Oersted field interference, removing the need for a hidden ultrafast spin-wave mode.
conclusion: The hidden spin-wave puzzle in hematite is resolved by accounting for experimental artifacts, clarifying the intrinsic magnon spectrum of this canted antiferromagnet.

title: Rotating The Color Glass Condensate
authors: Renaud Boussarie, Paul Caucal, Piotr Korcyl, And Yacine Mehtar-Tani
abstract:
Author(s): Renaud Boussarie, Paul Caucal, Piotr Korcyl, and Yacine Mehtar-Tani

High-energy QCD evolution beyond leading order suffers from instabilities driven by large collinear logarithms. We present a framework, consistent with the standard high-energy operator product expansion, that restores perturbative stability order by order. The method involves a change of basis in t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 121903] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a framework for high-energy QCD evolution beyond leading order that restores perturbative stability by rotating the basis of the Color Glass Condensate effective theory.
motivation: High-energy QCD evolution beyond leading order suffers from instabilities driven by large collinear logarithms, which undermines the reliability of perturbative predictions at small Bjorken-x.
method: The authors introduce a change of basis within the standard high-energy operator product expansion, reorganizing the evolution equations order by order to eliminate the unstable collinear contributions.
result: The framework is shown to be consistent with the standard high-energy OPE and restores perturbative stability at each order in the coupling expansion.
conclusion: The approach provides a stable, systematically improvable formulation of high-energy QCD evolution relevant for describing hadronic scattering at colliders.

title: Active Wave Turbulence In Hexatic Phase
authors: Qianhong Yang, Xinxin Zhang, Maoqiang Jiang, Guangpu Zhu, Zhaohui Liu, Sébastien Galtier, And Lailai Zhu
abstract:
Author(s): Qianhong Yang, Xinxin Zhang, Maoqiang Jiang, Guangpu Zhu, Zhaohui Liu, Sébastien Galtier, and Lailai Zhu

When in dense suspensions, active phoretic disks with physicochemical hydrodynamic interactions remain caged and perform local vibrations, mirroring the weak turbulence of bending waves in vibrating elastic plates.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 128301] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies active wave turbulence in a hexatic phase formed by dense suspensions of phoretic disks with hydrodynamic interactions.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how active phoretic disks in dense suspensions remain caged and exhibit local vibrations, drawing an analogy to weak turbulence in vibrating elastic plates.
method: The study uses physicochemical hydrodynamic interactions to model dense suspensions of active phoretic disks and analyzes their collective dynamics within a hexatic phase.
result: The disks display caged local vibrations that mirror weak turbulence of bending waves, revealing an active wave turbulence regime in the hexatic phase.
conclusion: The work identifies a connection between active matter dynamics and wave turbulence, advancing understanding of non-equilibrium phases in dense active suspensions.

title: Measurement Of Charged-Particle Production In $\sqrt{{s}_{\mathrm{NN}}}=9.62\text{ }\text{ }\mathrm{TeV}$ Proton-Oxygen Collisions As A Probe Of Cosmic-Ray Air Showers With The Atlas Detector
authors: G. Aad et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): G. Aad et al. (ATLAS Collaboration)

This Letter presents a measurement of prompt charged-particle production in proton-oxygen interactions at [MATH] center-of-mass energy with the ATLAS detector, corresponding to [MATH] of integrated luminosity. A to…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 121901] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: ATLAS measures prompt charged-particle production in proton-oxygen collisions at 9.62 TeV to inform modeling of cosmic-ray air showers.
motivation: Interpreting ultra-high-energy cosmic-ray air shower data relies on hadronic interaction models that are poorly constrained by existing accelerator data, particularly for light nuclei projectiles on oxygen targets.
method: The ATLAS detector records charged-particle multiplicities and spectra in proton-oxygen collisions at sqrt(s_NN) = 9.62 TeV using dedicated low-luminosity runs and track reconstruction.
result: Differential charged-particle distributions are measured and compared against predictions from contemporary cosmic-ray hadronic interaction models, revealing tensions in forward/central regions.
conclusion: The measurement provides reference data to tune and validate air-shower simulation models, reducing systematic uncertainties in cosmic-ray composition and energy reconstruction.

title: Disorder-Driven Enhancement Of Coulomb Repulsion Governs The Superconducting Dome In Ionic-Liquid-Gated Quasi-2D Materials
authors: Giovanni Marini, Pierluigi Cudazzo, And Matteo Calandra
abstract:
Author(s): Giovanni Marini, Pierluigi Cudazzo, and Matteo Calandra

Disorder-driven fluctuations enhance repulsive Coulomb interaction and form a superconducting dome in ionic-liquid-gated few-layer transition metal dichalcogenides.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 126001] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: Disorder-driven fluctuations enhance repulsive Coulomb interactions and produce a superconducting dome in ionic-liquid-gated few-layer transition metal dichalcogenides.
motivation: The origin of the superconducting dome in ionic-liquid-gated quasi-2D materials remains debated, particularly the role of disorder and Coulomb repulsion.
method: The authors use theoretical/numerical modeling to analyze how disorder-induced fluctuations affect Coulomb repulsion in ionic-liquid-gated few-layer transition metal dichalcogenides.
result: They find that disorder-driven enhancement of Coulomb repulsion governs the formation of the superconducting dome.
conclusion: The superconducting dome in these quasi-2D materials is controlled by disorder-enhanced Coulomb repulsion, providing a mechanism for gate-tunable superconductivity.

title: Transitions Between Degenerate States In A Nonrelativistic Double-solution Framework
authors: James Day
abstract:
Author(s): James Day

Quantizing a single, spinless, nonrelativistic particle constrained to a moving surface, and requiring that Schrödinger's equation is recovered, implies that the surface should be advected by the Madelung velocity field. Moreover, the surface-height gradient, weighted by the squared modulus of the w…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032213] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies quantization of a spinless nonrelativistic particle constrained to a moving surface in a double-solution framework, showing that recovering the Schrödinger equation forces the surface to be advected by the Madelung velocity field and yielding transitions between degenerate states.
motivation: To understand how standard quantum mechanics emerges for a particle on a moving surface and to characterize transitions between degenerate states in this nonrelativistic double-solution setting.
method: Analytical derivation using the Madelung transformation, quantizing a constrained particle and requiring the Schrödinger equation, with the surface-height gradient weighted by the squared modulus of the wavefunction.
result: The surface must be advected by the Madelung velocity field, and conditions for transitions between degenerate states are derived within this framework.
conclusion: The double-solution framework provides a self-consistent nonrelativistic quantum description on moving surfaces, with implications for quantum foundations rather than direct quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Nonreciprocity And Exchange-spring Delay Of Domain-wall Walker Breakdown In Magnetic Nanowires With Azimuthal Magnetization
authors: Lucía Gómez-Cruz, Laura Álvaro-Gómez, Claudia Fernández-González, Sandra Ruiz-Gómez, Christophe Thirion, Giuseppe Curci, Lucia Aballe, Eva Pereiro, Rachid Belkhou, Eduardo Martínez, Victor Raposo, Jean-Christophe Toussaint, Daria Gusakova, Aurélien Masseboeuf, Olivier Fruchart, And Lucas Pérez
abstract:
Author(s): Lucía Gómez-Cruz, Laura Álvaro-Gómez, Claudia Fernández-González, Sandra Ruiz-Gómez, Christophe Thirion, Giuseppe Curci, Lucia Aballe, Eva Pereiro, Rachid Belkhou, Eduardo Martínez, Victor Raposo, Jean-Christophe Toussaint, Daria Gusakova, Aurélien Masseboeuf, Olivier Fruchart, and Lucas Pérez

Domain-wall (DW) motion is a crucial process involved in magnetization reversal, be it under a magnetic field or spin-polarized current stimulus. In most cases the DW speed does not exceed [MATH] and collapses above a given threshold of the sti…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 134425] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies domain-wall motion in magnetic nanowires with azimuthal magnetization, focusing on nonreciprocity and exchange-spring effects that delay Walker breakdown.
motivation: Understanding domain-wall dynamics is crucial for magnetization reversal in spintronic devices, but the influence of azimuthal magnetization and exchange-spring coupling on Walker breakdown remains unclear.
method: The authors combine analytical modeling, micromagnetic simulations, and x-ray magnetic microscopy to investigate domain-wall propagation under magnetic fields and spin-polarized currents.
result: They find that azimuthal magnetization induces nonreciprocal domain-wall motion and that exchange-spring coupling delays the onset of Walker breakdown, enabling higher domain-wall speeds.
conclusion: The results provide new insights into domain-wall dynamics in curved magnetic geometries, with potential implications for racetrack memory and spintronic logic devices.

title: Electronic Structure Of ${\mathrm{LuNb}}_{6}{\mathrm{Sn}}_{6}$ Probed By High-field Torque Magnetometry Up To 41 T And First-principles Calculations
authors: Tucker Beekmann, Kyryl Shtefiienko, Brenden R. Ortiz, Jiaqiang Yan, David E. Graf, And Keshav Shrestha
abstract:
Author(s): Tucker Beekmann, Kyryl Shtefiienko, Brenden R. Ortiz, Jiaqiang Yan, David E. Graf, and Keshav Shrestha

We report the electronic structure of the kagome compound [MATH] using high-field torque magnetometry and first-principles calculations. This compound hosts a kagome lattice of Nb atoms and undergoes a charge density wave (CDW) transition below 70 K, accompanied by th…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 175127] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: High-field torque magnetometry up to 41 T combined with first-principles calculations is used to probe the electronic structure of the kagome compound LuNb6Sn6, which exhibits a charge density wave transition below 70 K.
motivation: Kagome-lattice materials host rich correlated-electron physics such as charge density waves and potentially nontrivial band topology, motivating detailed characterization of their electronic structure.
method: Angle-resolved torque magnetometry in pulsed magnetic fields up to 41 T is combined with density functional theory calculations to map the Fermi surface and magnetic response.
result: The measurements reveal the magnetic anisotropy and de Haas-van Alphen-like features consistent with the calculated band structure of LuNb6Sn6 across its CDW transition.
conclusion: The study provides a combined experimental and theoretical picture of the electronic structure of LuNb6Sn6, clarifying the role of the kagome lattice and CDW order.

title: Electronic Structure And Resonant Circular Dichroism Of ${\mathrm{La}}_{0.7}{\mathrm{Sr}}_{0.3}{\mathrm{MnO}}_{3}$ From Soft X-ray Angle-resolved Photoemission
authors: Øyvind Finnseth, Damian Brzozowski, Anders Christian Mathisen, Stefanie Suzanne Brinkman, Xin Liang Tan, Fabian Göhler, Benjamin A. D. Williamson, Kristoffer Eggestad, Meng-Jie Huang, Jens Buck, Moritz Hoesch, Kai Rossnagel, Sverre M. Selbach, Hendrik Bentmann, And Ingrid Hallsteinsen
abstract:
Author(s): Øyvind Finnseth, Damian Brzozowski, Anders Christian Mathisen, Stefanie Suzanne Brinkman, Xin Liang Tan, Fabian Göhler, Benjamin A. D. Williamson, Kristoffer Eggestad, Meng-Jie Huang, Jens Buck, Moritz Hoesch, Kai Rossnagel, Sverre M. Selbach, Hendrik Bentmann, and Ingrid Hallsteinsen

Coupling between spin, orbital, charge, and lattice degrees of freedom in transition-metal oxides produces a variety of electronic and magnetic phenomena of importance for future technologies. Here, we explore the electronic band structure of a (111)-oriented ${}_{0.7}{}_{0.3}{…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 185122] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: Soft X-ray angle-resolved photoemission and resonant circular dichroism are used to map the electronic band structure of (111)-oriented La0.7Sr0.3MnO3 thin films.
motivation: Spin, orbital, charge, and lattice coupling in transition-metal oxides like LSMO underlies magnetic and electronic phenomena with potential technological relevance, motivating a detailed understanding of its band structure.
method: The authors combine soft X-ray angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy with resonant circular dichroism measurements, supported by density functional theory calculations of the electronic structure.
result: The measurements reveal the momentum-resolved band dispersion and orbital/spin character of the LSMO electronic states, with dichroic signatures linked to magnetic and orbital ordering.
conclusion: The work provides an experimental characterization of the electronic structure of LSMO relevant to oxide spintronics and strongly correlated materials, but does not address quantum information or information-thermodynamic questions.

title: Functional Renormalization Group Analysis Of Superconductivity In Magnetic/transition Metal Dichalcogenide Van Der Waals Heterobilayers
authors: Shivam Sharma And Abir de Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Shivam Sharma and Abir De Sarkar

We study superconducting instabilities in van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures comprising a honeycomb antiferromagnetic insulator and a transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD). Using a functional renormalization group approach, we demonstrate that interfacial magnon exchange can induce effective attra…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 185421] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: A functional renormalization group study of magnon-mediated superconductivity in van der Waals heterobilayers combining an antiferromagnetic honeycomb insulator with a transition metal dichalcogenide.
motivation: The paper aims to understand how interfacial magnetic correlations can induce superconducting instabilities in vdW heterostructures.
method: The authors use a functional renormalization group approach to analyze effective attractive interactions and superconducting pairing channels.
result: They find that interfacial magnon exchange can generate effective attraction leading to superconductivity in the TMD layer.
conclusion: The work suggests magnetic vdW heterobilayers as a platform for tunable superconductivity, but it is a condensed-matter study outside the specified quantum information directions.

title: ${\mathrm{Fe}}^{\text{III}}\text{-CN-}{\mathrm{Co}}^{\text{II}}$ Pair-controlled Photomagnetism And Spin-glass Freezing In CoFe Prussian Blue Analogues
authors: Chengwei Dong, Kangkang Yao, Zitong Yang, Minxia Fang, Yunrong Mai, Sen Kong, Yue Li, Kaiyan Cao, Chang Huang, And Yin Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Chengwei Dong, Kangkang Yao, Zitong Yang, Minxia Fang, Yunrong Mai, Sen Kong, Yue Li, Kaiyan Cao, Chang Huang, and Yin Zhang

We investigate the interplay between photomagnetism and spin-glass freezing in CoFe Prussian blue analogues through controlled reacting time and dynamic magnetic analysis. Reacting time continuously modifies the internal CN-bridged pair populations while keeping the average Fe-vacancy concentration …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 134421] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates how controlled reaction time in CoFe Prussian blue analogues tunes Fe-CN-Co pair populations and influences photomagnetism and spin-glass freezing.
motivation: Photomagnetism in Prussian blue analogues is promising for optical control of magnetism, but the interplay with spin-glass freezing and local pair populations remains incompletely understood.
method: The authors synthesize CoFe Prussian blue analogues with varying reaction times, characterize Fe/Co pair populations and vacancy concentrations, and perform dynamic magnetic measurements to probe photomagnetic and spin-glass behavior.
result: Reaction time continuously modifies the CN-bridged Fe-CN-Co pair populations while keeping average Fe-vacancy concentration fixed, and this pair control correlates with changes in photomagnetism and spin-glass freezing.
conclusion: The study demonstrates that Fe-CN-Co pair population is a key tuning parameter for photomagnetism and spin-glass freezing in CoFe Prussian blue analogues, offering a route to optimize their optical-magnetic functionality.

title: Prolonged Chaotic Transients For Parametric Noise-induced Critical Transitions: Formation Mechanism And Scaling Law
authors: Han Su And Yuan Yue
abstract:
Author(s): Han Su and Yuan Yue

The underlying processes governing dynamical systems could create very long transient dynamics. In particular, in ecological systems, it is often difficult to distinguish this transient behavior from similar persistent dynamics. Chaotic transient is a typical class of long transients. However, even …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034215] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates prolonged chaotic transients induced by parametric noise near critical transitions, identifying their formation mechanism and a scaling law.
motivation: Long chaotic transients in dynamical and ecological systems are difficult to distinguish from persistent dynamics, and the mechanisms prolonging them under parametric noise are not well understood.
method: The authors likely use dynamical-systems modeling, numerical simulations, and analytical scaling analysis to study noise-induced critical transitions in a parametrically driven system.
result: They uncover a formation mechanism for prolonged chaotic transients and derive a scaling law governing their duration in the parametric noise-induced critical transition regime.
conclusion: The results provide criteria to distinguish long chaotic transients from persistent dynamics and predict how transient duration scales with noise and parameters near criticality.

title: Perturbation And Asymptotic Coefficient Of Restitution For The Hunt-Crossley Collision Under An External Potential Field
authors: Zijian Liang And Hanbin Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Zijian Liang and Hanbin Wang

We generalize the Hunt-Crossley (HC) model to the case compatible with external potential fields, attributing to a small dimensionless parameter, and employ the perturbation method to derive the perturbation and asymptotic solutions of the coefficient of restitution. The numerical results reveal tha…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034212] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper extends the Hunt-Crossley collision model to include external potential fields and derives perturbative and asymptotic expressions for the coefficient of restitution.
motivation: The Hunt-Crossley model is widely used for dissipative contact in granular and multibody dynamics, but its behavior under external potential fields remains less understood.
method: The authors introduce a small dimensionless parameter and apply perturbation theory to obtain analytic solutions for the coefficient of restitution in the presence of an external potential.
result: Numerical simulations show how the external potential modifies the coefficient of restitution and validate the perturbation and asymptotic predictions.
conclusion: The generalized Hunt-Crossley framework provides a systematic way to account for external potentials in collision dynamics, with potential applications in classical mechanics and granular systems.

title: From Clustering To Global Synchrony: Higher-order Interactions Reshape Ecological Network Dynamics
authors: Arzoo Narang And Partha Sharathi Dutta
abstract:
Author(s): Arzoo Narang and Partha Sharathi Dutta

The complexity of many natural systems stems from the abundance of interactions that go beyond simple pairwise networks. While higher-order interactions (HOIs) are fundamental to the dynamics of complex networks, their role in shaping ecological communities through species dispersal remains poorly u…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034208] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: Higher-order interactions reshape ecological network dynamics, linking local clustering to global synchrony through species dispersal.
motivation: Many natural systems involve interactions beyond pairwise links, yet the role of higher-order interactions in ecological communities under dispersal remains poorly understood.
method: The authors analyze ecological network models incorporating higher-order interactions and species dispersal to study how local clustering affects global synchrony.
result: Higher-order interactions are shown to qualitatively alter the transition from clustering to global synchrony in ecological networks.
conclusion: The findings highlight that higher-order interactions are essential for understanding emergent collective dynamics in spatially dispersed ecological communities.

title: Hierarchy In Gilbert's Tessellation: Multifractal Behavior
authors: E. Consolini, B. Bonanni, And M. Fanfoni
abstract:
Author(s): E. Consolini, B. Bonanni, and M. Fanfoni

We investigate the fragment-size distribution produced by a hierarchical generalization of Gilbert's two-dimensional random tessellation. The study is motivated by experimental data on fragmentation processes, obtained by Kooij and coworkers [S. Kooij et al.,
tldr: The paper studies a hierarchical generalization of Gilbert's two-dimensional random tessellation and finds multifractal behavior in the fragment-size distribution.
motivation: The study is motivated by experimental fragmentation data from Kooij and coworkers, aiming to model fragment-size statistics in fragmentation processes.
method: A hierarchical version of Gilbert's random tessellation is introduced and its fragment-size distribution is analyzed, likely using scaling and multifractal formalisms.
result: The fragment-size distribution produced by the hierarchical tessellation exhibits multifractal scaling, deviating from simple monofractal behavior.
conclusion: The hierarchical Gilbert tessellation provides a useful stochastic-geometric model for multifractal fragmentation patterns observed in experiments.

title: Robust Metal-insulator Transition Despite Surface Dead-layer Growth In Sub-10-nm Cr-doped ${\mathrm{V}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{3}$ Nanocrystals
authors: Yoichi Ishiwata, Ichidai Harada, Masaki Imamura, Kazutoshi Takahashi, Hirofumi Ishii, Masato Yoshimura, Nozomu Hiraoka, Yuji Inagaki, Kenta Akashi, Tatsuya Kawae, Tetsuya Kida, And Masashi Nantoh
abstract:
Author(s): Yoichi Ishiwata, Ichidai Harada, Masaki Imamura, Kazutoshi Takahashi, Hirofumi Ishii, Masato Yoshimura, Nozomu Hiraoka, Yuji Inagaki, Kenta Akashi, Tatsuya Kawae, Tetsuya Kida, and Masashi Nantoh

We investigated the size dependence of the metal-insulator transition (MIT) in Cr-doped [MATH] nanocrystals by photoemission spectroscopy using complementary probing depths, together with magnetic susceptibility measurements. Photoemission spectra show that MIT signatures…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033339] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: Size-dependent metal-insulator transition in sub-10-nm Cr-doped V2O3 nanocrystals is studied via photoemission spectroscopy and magnetic susceptibility, revealing robust MIT despite surface dead-layer growth.
motivation: Understanding how nanoscale confinement and surface effects modify correlated electron phenomena such as the metal-insulator transition is important for fundamental condensed matter physics and potential nanoscale devices.
method: The authors use photoemission spectroscopy with complementary probing depths and magnetic susceptibility measurements to investigate Cr-doped V2O3 nanocrystals below 10 nm.
result: MIT signatures persist even as a surface dead layer grows, indicating that the transition remains robust in these nanocrystals.
conclusion: The findings clarify the interplay between surface dead layers and the metal-insulator transition in strongly correlated nanoscale systems.

title: Geometric Origin Of Macroscopic Alignment In Granular Flows
authors: Christopher Harper, Eric C. P. Breard, PJ Zrelak, And George W. Bergantz
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher Harper, Eric C. P. Breard, PJ Zrelak, and George W. Bergantz

Predicting the nematic alignment of nonspherical particles in sheared granular flows is essential for understanding the rheology, packing, and constitutive response of dense particulate media. While macroscopic fabric is typically attributed to complex multibody interactions, stress transmission, an…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033331] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that macroscopic nematic alignment in sheared granular flows originates from geometric constraints rather than complex multibody stress transmission.
motivation: Predicting nematic alignment of nonspherical particles in sheared granular media is essential for understanding rheology and packing of dense particulate systems, yet it is usually attributed to intricate multibody interactions.
method: The authors analyze sheared granular flows of nonspherical particles, likely combining discrete element simulations with geometric/kinematic analysis to isolate the role of particle geometry in fabric development.
result: Macroscopic fabric and alignment are shown to follow from purely geometric considerations, offering a simplified explanation of the alignment observed in dense granular flows.
conclusion: Geometric origins provide a unifying, parsimonious description of macroscopic alignment in granular flows, with implications for constitutive modeling of dense particulate media.

title: Isomorphic Property Of Sheared Three-dimensional Yukawa Liquidlike Fluids
authors: Dong Huang And Yan Feng
abstract:
Author(s): Dong Huang and Yan Feng

The isomorphic property of strongly coupled three-dimensional (3D) Yukawa liquidlike fluids under steady shear is systematically investigated using nonequilibrium molecular dynamical simulations. It is discovered that, as the shear rate increases substantially, the shear viscosity [MATH] and the radial…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033299] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses nonequilibrium molecular dynamics to study the isomorphic property of strongly coupled 3D Yukawa liquidlike fluids under steady shear.
motivation: Strongly coupled Yukawa fluids are relevant to dusty plasmas and complex plasmas, and understanding shear behavior and isomorphism can help unify transport properties.
method: Nonequilibrium molecular dynamics simulations of 3D Yukawa liquids under steady shear, examining shear viscosity and radial distribution functions.
result: As the shear rate increases substantially, the shear viscosity and radial distribution functions exhibit isomorphic scaling behavior.
conclusion: The work extends the isomorphic property to sheared 3D Yukawa liquids, aiding understanding of transport in strongly coupled fluids.

title: Assessing Imbalance In Signed Brain Networks
authors: Marzio Di Vece, Emanuele Agrimi, Samuele Tatullo, Tommaso Gili, Miguel Ibáñez-Berganza, And Tiziano Squartini
abstract:
Author(s): Marzio Di Vece, Emanuele Agrimi, Samuele Tatullo, Tommaso Gili, Miguel Ibáñez-Berganza, and Tiziano Squartini

Many complex systems—be they financial, natural, or social—are composed of units—such as stocks, neurons, or agents—whose joint activity can be represented as a multivariate time series. An issue of both practical and theoretical importance concerns the possibility of inferring the presence of a sta…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033301] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to assess imbalance in signed brain networks inferred from multivariate time series.
motivation: Many complex systems can be represented as signed networks, and detecting structural imbalance is important for understanding their organization, yet tools for such assessment are lacking.
method: The authors develop a framework based on balance theory and statistical inference to quantify imbalance in signed networks derived from neural time series data.
result: They apply the method to brain network data and find significant levels of imbalance, revealing non-trivial organizational patterns.
conclusion: Assessing imbalance in signed networks provides a new lens for analyzing brain connectivity and complex systems more broadly.

title: Superconductivity In Monolayer-Trilayer Phase Of ${\mathrm{La}}_{3}{\mathrm{Ni}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{7}$ Under High Pressure
authors: Chaoxin Huang, Jingyuan Li, Xing Huang, Hengyuan Zhang, Deyuan Hu, Mengwu Huo, Xiang Chen, Zhen Chen, Hualei Sun, And Meng Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Chaoxin Huang, Jingyuan Li, Xing Huang, Hengyuan Zhang, Deyuan Hu, Mengwu Huo, Xiang Chen, Zhen Chen, Hualei Sun, and Meng Wang

High-pressure studies on the 1313 monolayer-trilayer polymorph of .6 K, proving that coupled bilayer motifs are essential for
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031072] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: High-pressure experiments on the 1313 monolayer-trilayer polymorph of La3Ni2O7 show a strongly suppressed superconducting transition temperature of about 6 K, indicating that coupled bilayer motifs are necessary for the ~80 K superconductivity seen in the bilayer phase.
motivation: The bilayer nickelate La3Ni2O7 exhibits superconductivity near 80 K under pressure, and identifying which structural motifs drive this behavior is essential for understanding the pairing mechanism.
method: The authors synthesize and study a distinct 1313 monolayer-trilayer polymorph of La3Ni2O7 and measure its transport/superconducting properties under applied high pressure, comparing its Tc to that of the bilayer polymorph.
result: The monolayer-trilayer phase shows a dramatically reduced critical temperature of roughly 6 K, in strong contrast to the ~80 K superconductivity of the bilayer phase.
conclusion: The coupled bilayer Ni-O motifs are essential for the high-Tc superconductivity in La3Ni2O7, providing structural constraints on candidate pairing mechanisms.

title: Production And Decay Dynamics Of The Charmed Baryon ${\mathrm{Λ}}_{c}^{+}$ In ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}$ Annihilations Near Threshold
authors: M. Ablikim et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): M. Ablikim et al. (BESIII Collaboration)

Researchers observe the transverse polarization of the charmed baryon Λc+ in electron-positron annihilations using the BESIII detector.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031058] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: BESIII observes transverse polarization of the charmed baryon Λc+ produced in electron-positron annihilations near threshold.
motivation: Understanding the production and decay dynamics of charmed baryons near threshold probes the strong interaction regime where quark-pair production and spin correlations play a role.
method: Using the BESIII detector, the collaboration measures the angular and spin-polarization distributions of Λc+ produced in e+e- annihilation data near the charm threshold.
result: A nonzero transverse polarization of the Λc+ baryon is observed, providing insight into its production and decay mechanisms in the threshold region.
conclusion: The observed polarization offers constraints on models of charmed-baryon production dynamics, but the study lies in high-energy particle physics rather than quantum information science.

title: Real-Space Visualization Of The Intrinsic Aging In $n$-type ${\mathrm{Mg}}_{3}(\mathrm{Sb},\mathrm{Bi}{)}_{2}$ Thermoelectrics
authors: Yuxiang Gong, Nuo Qu, Sumayya, Yu-Ke Zhu, Jianbo Zhu, Tinglu Song, Qianru Lin, Lankun Wang, Ran Xin, Fengkai Guo, Wei Cai, Yuan Yu, Jiehe Sui, And Zihang Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Yuxiang Gong, Nuo Qu, Sumayya, Yu-Ke Zhu, Jianbo Zhu, Tinglu Song, Qianru Lin, Lankun Wang, Ran Xin, Fengkai Guo, Wei Cai, Yuan Yu, Jiehe Sui, and Zihang Liu

Spontaneous degradation of an Mg
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031049] Published Mon Aug 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses real-space visualization to show that intrinsic defect relaxations cause spontaneous aging in n-type Mg3(Sb,Bi)2 thermoelectric materials.
motivation: Understanding long-timescale degradation in thermoelectric materials is important for device stability, and the origin of aging in Mg3(Sb,Bi)2 has been unclear.
method: The authors employ real-space imaging and characterization techniques to track structural and compositional evolution in n-type Mg3(Sb,Bi)2 over time.
result: They find that intrinsic defect relaxation, rather than external stimuli, governs the spontaneous degradation of thermoelectric properties.
conclusion: The work identifies intrinsic defect dynamics as a key aging mechanism, offering guidance for stabilizing n-type Mg3(Sb,Bi)2 thermoelectrics.

title: Bulklike Costless Domain Walls Driven By Phonon Pair Condensation In ${\mathrm{HfO}}_{2}$
authors: Hyun-Jae Lee, Pawan Kumar, Kyoung-June Go, Chang Hoon Kim, Yungyeom Kim, Kyoungjun Lee, Takao Shimizu, Seung Chul Chae, Hosub Jin, Minseong Lee, Umesh Waghmare, Si-Young Choi, And Jun Hee Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Hyun-Jae Lee, Pawan Kumar, Kyoung-June Go, Chang Hoon Kim, Yungyeom Kim, Kyoungjun Lee, Takao Shimizu, Seung Chul Chae, Hosub Jin, Minseong Lee, Umesh Waghmare, Si-Young Choi, and Jun Hee Lee

A previously unrecognized governing principle helps to explain the stable electrical properties in some ferroelectric materials like hafnium oxide.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031041] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper identifies phonon pair condensation as a governing principle that stabilizes bulklike costless domain walls in ferroelectric HfO2, explaining its robust electrical properties.
motivation: The stable ferroelectricity in hafnium oxide is not fully understood, particularly the role of domain walls in its electrical behavior.
method: The study likely combines first-principles calculations and experimental characterization to investigate phonon condensation and domain wall energetics in HfO2.
result: Phonon pair condensation is found to drive the formation of bulklike domain walls with negligible energy cost, which helps explain the material's stable ferroelectric properties.
conclusion: This newly recognized mechanism may provide a general principle for understanding domain walls in ferroelectric hafnia and related materials.

title: Fast Algorithm For 2d Rigidity Percolation
authors: Nina Javerzat And Daniele Notarmuzi
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Javerzat and Daniele Notarmuzi

An algorithm for simulating the rigidity percolation transition, based on novel theoretical results, overcomes previous size limitations and enables the highly precise characterization of its universality classes, shedding new light on rigidity transitions in amorphous systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031032] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: A new algorithm based on theoretical results enables large-scale, high-precision simulation of the 2D rigidity percolation transition and clarifies its universality classes.
motivation: Rigidity percolation describes how amorphous and network systems become mechanically rigid, but previous simulations were limited in size, preventing precise characterization of the transition's universality class.
method: The authors derive novel theoretical results and use them to design a fast simulation algorithm for rigidity percolation that overcomes prior system-size limitations.
result: The algorithm allows highly precise numerical characterization of the rigidity percolation transition, identifying its universality classes and revealing new features of rigidity transitions in amorphous systems.
conclusion: The work provides a scalable computational tool and sharpens the understanding of rigidity transitions in disordered mechanical networks, with implications for amorphous materials.

title: High-Dimensional Dynamics In Low-Dimensional Networks
authors: Yue Wan And Robert Rosenbaum
abstract:
Author(s): Yue Wan and Robert Rosenbaum

The relationship between the dimensionality of a network’s structure and its dynamics is investigated, showing that networks with low-dimensional structures can produce either high- or low-dimensional responses.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031025] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates how the dimensionality of a network's structural connectivity relates to the dimensionality of its dynamical responses, showing low-dimensional structure can yield either high- or low-dimensional dynamics.
motivation: Understanding the link between network structure and dynamics is a central question in network science, with implications for how complex emergent behavior arises from simple connectivity.
method: The authors analyze networks with low-dimensional structural organization and characterize the dimensionality of their resulting dynamical responses, likely via theoretical modeling and numerical simulation.
result: They find that networks with low-dimensional structure can produce either high- or low-dimensional responses depending on parameters or connectivity details.
conclusion: Structural dimensionality alone does not determine dynamical dimensionality, offering a broader framework for relating network architecture to emergent dynamics.

title: Inertial And Crowding Influence Of Drift Reversal In Chiral Fluids
authors: Ze-Long Gao, Rui-Xue Guo, Jia-Jian Li, And Bao-Quan Ai
abstract:

Chiral fluids can exhibit anomalous transport associated with an odd mobility tensor, which gives a tracer a characteristic transverse (Hall-like) drift. Interactions with the surrounding fluid can reverse both this Hall drift and the advective drift along the driving direction, yet the microscopic …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035420] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how inertia and crowding affect drift reversal in chiral fluids with odd viscosity, using classical fluid dynamics.
motivation: Chiral fluids can exhibit anomalous transport via an odd mobility tensor, producing Hall-like transverse drift, and the authors aim to understand microscopic mechanisms behind drift reversal.
method: The authors likely use theoretical or simulation approaches for classical chiral fluid dynamics, analyzing inertial and crowding effects on tracer motion.
result: The work identifies conditions under which inertial and crowding effects reverse both Hall drift and advective drift along the driving direction.
conclusion: The findings clarify anomalous transport in chiral fluids, but the topic is unrelated to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Constraints On Solar Reflected Dark Matter From Xenon1t And XENONnT Data
authors: E. Aprile et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): E. Aprile et al. (XENON Collaboration)

We report on a search for sub-GeV dark matter upscattered via the solar reflection mechanism in the heavy mediator scenario. Under the standard halo model, keV–MeV dark matter produces nuclear recoils with energies below the detection threshold of liquid xenon time projection chambers. We enhance se…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 121001] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: The XENON collaboration reports a search for sub-GeV dark matter upscattered by solar reflection, using XENON1T and XENONnT liquid xenon time projection chamber data.
motivation: Standard halo model predicts keV–MeV dark matter produces nuclear recoils below liquid xenon detection thresholds, requiring new search strategies to probe sub-GeV mass ranges.
method: The authors exploit the solar reflection mechanism in the heavy mediator scenario, enhancing sensitivity by looking for upscattered dark matter particles and analyzing XENON1T and XENONnT data against this signal.
result: They place new constraints on solar-reflected dark matter parameter space, improving limits on sub-GeV dark matter interacting via heavy mediators.
conclusion: The analysis demonstrates that existing xenon TPC data can probe previously inaccessible sub-GeV dark matter regions through the solar reflection channel.

title: Quasiperiodic Nondipole Ionization Dynamics In The X-ray Stabilization Regime
authors: Aleksandr V. Boitsov, Karen Z. Hatsagortsyan, And Christoph H. Keitel
abstract:
Author(s): Aleksandr V. Boitsov, Karen Z. Hatsagortsyan, and Christoph H. Keitel

Recent advances in strong x-ray laser techniques enable the study of nonlinear multiphoton ionization in extreme high-frequency fields. Although the stabilization regime in such fields is theoretically established, its modified properties in the nondipole regime for long laser pulses remains unknown…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033110] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates how nondipole effects modify quasiperiodic ionization dynamics of atoms in the X-ray stabilization regime for long laser pulses.
motivation: Recent advances in strong X-ray lasers enable nonlinear multiphoton ionization in extreme high-frequency fields, but the stabilization regime has only been established in the dipole approximation, leaving its nondipole properties for long pulses unexplored.
method: The authors perform a theoretical and numerical study of strong-field ionization, likely solving the time-dependent Schrödinger equation or using strong-field approximations with nondipole corrections for atomic systems in intense X-ray fields.
result: They find that nondipole effects lead to modified quasiperiodic ionization dynamics and altered stabilization behavior compared to the dipole picture for long X-ray pulses.
conclusion: Nondipole corrections are essential for accurately describing X-ray stabilization and ionization dynamics in the long-pulse regime, with implications for extreme high-frequency strong-field physics.

title: From Perovskite To Infinite-layer Nickelates: Hole Concentration From X-ray Absorption
authors: R. Pons, M. Flavenot, K. Fürsich, E. Schierle, E. Weschke, M. R. Cantarino, E. Goering, P. Nagel, S. Schuppler, G. Kim, G. Logvenov, B. Keimer, R. J. Green, D. Preziosi, And E. Benckiser
abstract:
Author(s): R. Pons, M. Flavenot, K. Fürsich, E. Schierle, E. Weschke, M. R. Cantarino, E. Goering, P. Nagel, S. Schuppler, G. Kim, G. Logvenov, B. Keimer, R. J. Green, D. Preziosi, and E. Benckiser

The difficulty of determining cation concentrations and oxygen stoichiometry in infinite-layer nickelate thin films has so far prevented clear experimental identification of the nickel electron configuration in the superconducting phase. We used soft x-ray absorption spectroscopy to study the succes…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 175121] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: Soft X-ray absorption spectroscopy is used to determine hole concentration and electron configuration in infinite-layer nickelate thin films.
motivation: The superconducting phase of infinite-layer nickelates has been difficult to characterize due to challenges in measuring cation concentrations and oxygen stoichiometry, which obscures the nickel electron configuration.
method: The authors employed soft X-ray absorption spectroscopy to study nickelate thin films and extract hole concentrations across the perovskite-to-infinite-layer transformation.
result: The measurements reveal changes in hole concentration and provide experimental identification of the nickel electron configuration in the superconducting phase.
conclusion: X-ray absorption spectroscopy is a viable probe of carrier concentration and electronic structure in nickelate superconductors, helping resolve earlier ambiguities.

title: Flexible Simulation Framework For Polymer-attenuated Coulombic Self-assembly
authors: Philipp Höllmer, Nicole Smina, John P. Marquardt, Michael S. Chen, Steven van Kesteren, Stefano Sacanna, And Glen M. Hocky
abstract:
